title: Asian Games: Arshad Nadeem finishes fourth as Rumesh Pathirage strikes javelin gold in rainy Nagoya
author: Dawn Sport
description: The result caps a difficult season for Arshad, who has struggled to rediscover the form that saw him win Olympic gold in Paris with a record 92.97m throw.
text: Arshad Nadeem threw a season-best 80.29m but still finished fourth as Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Pathirage claimed javelin gold in a rain-soaked final at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Monday. The Olympic champion, competing under heavy skies and on a slick runway, had a difficult start, managing 76.69m on his first attempt before a foul on his second. He improved drastically on his third with 80.29m to climb to fourth, but could not build on it — three consecutive fouls followed, ending his challenge. Pathirage, the World No. 1 and heavy favourite, lived up to his billing. Third after three throws with 83.56m, he unleashed 88.33m on his fourth attempt, beating his chest in delight as he moved ahead of both Indians. He improved again in the sixth with 88.55m. The Sri Lankan’s dominance is all the more remarkable given the disruption to his season. Just two weeks before the Games, all five of his javelins — the same implements he used for every 90m throw this year — were found shattered after a flight from Budapest, where he had won the World Athletics Ultimate Championship. India’s Yashvir Singh took silver with a personal-best 85.72m on his final attempt, while compatriot Rohit Yadav claimed bronze with 84.35m. Yashvir had set the tone early with 83.56m on his first throw, before Rohit briefly moved ahead with 84.35m in the third round. Pakistan’s Mohammad Yasir finished ninth, his best effort 73.50m. The result caps a difficult season for Arshad, who has struggled to rediscover the form that saw him win Olympic gold in Paris with a record 92.97m throw. He finished ninth at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and fifth at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest. Pathirage, by contrast, has been unstoppable. The 23-year-old has won 11 of his 12 competitions this year, thrown beyond 90m three times, and claimed the Diamond League Final, Commonwealth gold and the World Ultimate title.

title: Red Bull sues Indian regulator over 'energy drink' label ban
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: Austrian beverage maker Red Bull has sued India’s food regulator for prohibiting the use of the “energy drink” descriptor without issuing any warning notice, which it claims is impacting its investments in India, its court filing showed. Red Bull is one of a number of globally recognized brands to have sued the Indian regulator in recent months amid an unprecedented food standards enforcement drive, which has included surprise raids and scrutiny over legal compliance impacting companies like Diageo. India in June ordered makers of high-caffeine beverages sold as “energy drinks” to stop using that description, rejecting efforts to stall the regulatory intervention in a market expected to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028. The move has triggered a standoff, as Pepsi, Red Bull, Monster Beverage and billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance fear removing the category label could damage brands built around instant-energy claims, Reuters has reported. India tightens proposed food warning labels in setback to industry In the first legal challenge against the move, Red Bull told the Delhi High Court on September 25 that legal processes were not followed in prohibiting use of the term “energy drinks”, which is globally recognized, according to the company’s filing seen by Reuters. ‘Against India’s policy’ Red Bull’s India unit said the “abrupt prohibition” of the descriptor, without any change to the underlying product standard, “introduces substantial regulatory uncertainty and adversely affects” its existing and planned commercial investments. The order is against India’s stated policy of facilitating “international trade, promote investment and provide greater certainty to businesses,” Red Bull said, adding that its “effect is to bring the petitioner’s entire business to a standstill”. A government source said the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India will defend its decision in court against Red Bull, saying the FSSAI historically never allowed the use of ‘energy drinks’ on the label. India wanted red flags on chip packets and soda. Big Food fought back India’s energy drinks retail sales are growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, Euromonitor estimates. The market in India boomed after Pepsi launched Sting in 2017, with its 20-rupee ($0.21) plastic bottles proving popular among 15- to 19-year-olds, Euromonitor says. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago. Energy drinks have sparked health concerns among some regulators globally who worry they contain high caffeine, sugar and taurine, an amino acid. They will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

title: MongoDB CEO Desai steps down to lead Meta's enterprise platform
author: Reuters
description: Database software firm MongoDB’s Chirantan “CJ” Desai has stepped down as president and CEO to join Meta Platforms as chief enterprise platform officer, the companies said on Monday. Shares of MongoDB fell 14% in premarket trading. Desai has served as MongoDB’s CEO for less than a year, having taken the role in November from Dev Ittycheria. Meta’s social networks down for thousands of users in US, Downdetector says MongoDB’s board has appointed Ittycheria as interim president and CEO. It is searching for a permanent CEO and has retained an executive search firm to assist in that process.

title: Aleema provided basic facilities, essential items in jail, Punjab govt tells LHC
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: Aleema provided with a bedsheet, blanket, shoes, six suits, a towel and other essential items, according to the report.
text: LAHORE: The Punjab government on Monday told the Lahore High Court (LHC) that Aleema Khan, a sister of PTI founder Imran Khan, had been provided basic facilities and essential items in jail. Aleema was detained on Sep 20 after the Lahore deputy commissioner ordered her detention or arrest under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. The detention has come amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has postponed to Oct 4. The protest has been called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. Assistant Advocate General Farrukh Khan Lodhi submitted a report on behalf of the Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent during the hearing of a petition filed by Shahrez Khan, Aleema’s son. According to the report, Aleema had been provided with a bedsheet, blanket, shoes, six suits and a towel. She was also given face wash, a toothbrush, a skincare kit and a shawl, it added. In light of the government’s report, Justice Abher Gul Khan disposed of the petition. The judge also directed the home secretary to decide, in accordance with the law, on the petitioner’s request seeking permission to meet Aleema. At the last hearing on Sept 26, Barrister Taimur Malik had told the court that his client, Aleema, was facing difficulties in receiving her medicines and other essentials in jail. Aleema’s sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, have also been detained for 30 days ahead of the PTI’s protest and march to Islamabad. On Sept 24, the LHC turned down a request to immediately suspend the preventive detention notifications issued against Noreen and Uzma.

title: Tarar says PTI-led KP govt has failed to act against terrorism
author: BR Web Desk
description: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar has regretted that the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has neither taken practical steps against terrorism nor has the intention to do so. Addressing a news conference along with Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry in Islamabad on Monday, he alleged that the provincial government was facilitating the terrorism for they reaped political and financial gains from it, despite loss of numerous innocent lives. “The PTI leadership in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the B team of the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP),” he said. He said the provincial government has provided facilitation to terrorists for its political and financial interests. Tarar said the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government has deliberately refrained from bringing non-customs-paid vehicles in the province under the legal framework. He said these non-customs-paid vehicles are used in terrorist activities. The information minister also demanded that the provincial government provide details of how the resources meant for counter-terrorism efforts were utilised in the province. “You have not installed Safe City cameras despite taking huge funds,” he said. Tarar expressed the federal government’s firm resolve to eliminate the scourge of terrorism. “The PTI has been in power in the province for more than twelve and a half years, yet the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa still travel to other provinces for medical treatment,” he said, criticising the performance of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government. In his remarks, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry highlighted the involvement of Afghan nationals in terrorist incidents in Pakistan. He regretted that PTI does not condemn Afghanistan over the issue. He said the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government has neither provided adequate resources to the police nor empowered them to deal with the menace of terrorism. He lamented that under the KP Police Act, 2026, an attempt has been made to further curtail the powers of the police.

title: Irish players refuse handshakes, wear black armbands in Nation Leagues clash against Israel
author: Reuters | AFP
description: Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says his team “raised awareness worldwide” about Gaza conflict; secures 3-0 win against Israel in Hungary.
text: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in a Nations League clash on Sunday amid an eerie and sombre atmosphere that saw the Irish players wear black armbands over the war in Gaza. Ireland’s players also bowed their heads as the Israeli national anthem was played at the near-empty Debrecen stadium in Hungary. The teams skipped the traditional pre-match handshakes and did not exchange pennants either. Troy Parrott made a heart sign with his hands after opening the scoring on 14 minutes, while Jack Moylan kissed the Irish badge on his jersey and his black armband after netting the third goal 25 minutes in. Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson said his team had “raised awareness worldwide” about the Gaza conflict after they chose not to shake hands with Israeli players. The game, in which Israel were the nominal hosts, had been in doubt earlier in the week until Ireland’s players voted overwhelmingly to fulfil the fixture, despite pressure from back home to boycott the match. Only one player, goalkeeper Gavin Buzunu, pulled out, saying “it would be wrong to participate” in either this match or the return fixture in Serbia on October 4 due to the “killing of innocent people”. “It has been so difficult for so many players,” Icelander Hallgrimsson told broadcaster RTE after the game. “I hope that will not be in the next game because they have shown support to the protest, they have raised awareness worldwide, not only in Ireland, on the subject and that is normally the reason for protesting, to raise awareness of a situation. “I think these players have done that with all their actions, with all that they have been saying. No more than Gavin Bazunu, but the others have done it here on the pitch and how they have shown their actions, so I hope people understand that.” Since Ireland were drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel in February, prominent Irish figures including sportspeople, fan groups and pro-Palestinian campaigners have protested against the matches going ahead. The Irish federation did not reserve any tickets for fans to attend the match and public broadcaster RTE was due to show it without commentary. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar accused Ireland of being “on the wrong side of history” over the players’ actions. In a lengthy post on X, Saar referenced the Irish team of 1939 giving the Nazi salute ahead of a match against Germany in Bremen. He also referred to Irish neutrality during the Second World War and the condolences offered by then-prime minister Eaemon de Valera to the German representative in Dublin following Adolf Hitler’s death. “Almost 90 years have passed. Ireland’s unique talent for finding itself on the wrong side of history remains intact,” he added. “Sports, soccer, basketball, everything is for the public, the people, and not for politics,” 31-year-old software development teacher Mol Michael, draped in an Israeli scarf, told AFP . “Once you decide, because of politics, to cancel the Irish audience, this is a really stupid move from Ireland, in my opinion.” Ireland has long been a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause, with sympathy often linked to the country’s own history of British rule. Dublin formally recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway, and has repeatedly criticised Israel over its relentless bombardment of Gaza.

title: Lahore ATC extends physical remand of PTI's Hammad Azhar for 7 days in Jinnah House attack case
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: Govt lawyers inform LHC that Azhar's mother and wife have met him.
text: LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Monday extended the physical remand of PTI leader Hammad Azhar for another seven days in the 2023 Jinnah House attack case . Sarwar Road police had booked several PTI leaders and workers on charges of attacking and vandalising the Jinnah House , which also serves as the residence of the corps commander, during the May 9, 2023 protests against the arrest of ex-premier Imran Khan. On Monday, police produced the former federal finance minister before ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill upon the completion of his 21-day physical remand . During the hearing, a state prosecutor said police needed further remand to recover the suspect’s mobile phone and SIM, describing them as important pieces of evidence. He urged the court to extend the remand for a further seven days. Speaking before the court, Azhar questioned why further remand was being sought, saying he had already been kept on physical remand for 21 days in an alleged occurrence where he said he was not even present. “Even a murder suspect is sent on 14-day remand here. Has my offence become more serious than murder?” he asked. The former minister also complained that he had earlier not been allowed to meet his lawyers or family members — a concern also voiced earlier by his family before a court. The ATC then reserved its decision on the prosecution’s request for further remand, and later announced its decision, granting the police Azhar’s remand for another seven days. Separately, a two-member Lahore High Court (LHC) bench headed by Justice Syed Shahbaz Ali Rizvi disposed of a petition filed by Azhar’s mother and wife against the alleged denial of access to him during police custody. A Lahore ATC had already disposed of a similar plea filed by the family, directing them to approach the police on the matter. A Punjab government lawyer informed the LHC bench that Azhar had been allowed to meet his mother and wife. The law officer further said that the PTI leader would also meet his lawyer at the trial court on Monday. Relying on the government lawyer’s statement, the bench disposed of the petition. According to his family , Azhar was arrested on Sept 5. However, police said the next day they were unaware of his arrest, prompting the PTI leader’s mother to approach the LHC on Sept 7, and he was produced before an ATC the same day. Azhar, the son of late former Punjab governor Mian Muhammad Azhar , has been declared a proclaimed offender by multiple anti-terrorism courts for not joining the proceedings against him in cases related to the May 9 riots . Azhar had reappeared in public on May 22, 2024, a year after he had gone into hiding when the state launched a crackdown against the party leadership following the violent incidents of May 9 . At the time, the PTI leader had evaded arrest when the Counter-Terrorism Department raided the party’s secretariat in Islamabad.

title: Palm oil falls for a second session on weak rival oils
author: Reuters
description: JAKARTA: Malaysian palm oil futures dropped for the second consecutive session on Monday, tracking rival vegetable oils on Chicago and Dalian exchanges, though stronger crude prices and a softer ringgit capped losses. The benchmark palm oil contract for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange fell 9 ringgit, or 0.19%, to 4,663 ringgit ($1,142.05) a metric ton at closing. The contract traded in a tight range between 4,642 ringgit and 4,720 ringgit, after dropping 4.61% last week. A Kuala Lumpur-based trader said the contract was supported by strong crude oil and a weaker ringgit —its currency of trade — “but weak Dalian and Chicago oils cap gains.” Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract fell 0.84%, while its palm oil contract lost 1.6%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade ticked down 0.24%. Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market. Brent crude rebounded more than 3% on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock. The ringgit palm’s currency of trade, eased 0.25% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies. Palm oil may extend losses into a range of 4,588-4,622 ringgit per ton, as suggested by a projection analysis, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. Exports of Malaysian palm oil products for September 1-25 likely fell between 15.1% and 24.3% from a month earlier, cargo surveyors Intertek Testing Services and AmSpec Agri Malaysia said. Indonesia’s palm oil exports in July stood at 3.19 million metric tons, down 9.87% from the same period of last year, palm oil association GAPKI said on Monday.

title: India's Aug industrial output jumps 8% as manufacturing output surges
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: India’s industrial output grew at a stronger-than-expected pace of 8% in August, government data showed on Monday, boosted by a surge in manufacturing and electricity output even as mining output contracted. Economists polled by Reuters expected industrial output growth at 6.5% in August from a revised 7.4% a month earlier. “In a record performance, manfuacturing recorded growth of 8% or more in the last three consecutive months,” the statistics ministry said in an official statement. title: China, US agree tariff cuts on $60bn of goods including agriculture, household items
author: Reuters
description: BEIJING: China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on $60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended $30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was “unlocking improved market access” for about 30% of US exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. China says US trade truce extension creates space to advance talks In another list were Washington’s reciprocal tariff cuts for Chinese small appliances such as coffee makers and toasters, tableware, blankets and bed linens. The lists also included toys, fireworks, artificial flowers, Christmas tree lamps and other holiday decorations, and children’s car seats. Longer trade truce China’s commerce ministry said on Monday a two-month extension of a trade truce with the United States through to January 10 would provide room for both sides to evaluate their ongoing arrangement to resolve economic and trade issues, while considering how to advance on those fronts. The extension also provides a “relatively stable and predictable policy environment” for cooperation among companies and continued active discussions. Both sides will hold regular talks on potential investment opportunities and barriers, enhancing policy transparency and predictability, and responding to enterprises’ concerns, the ministry said. China, US agree to $30 billion tariff cut, AI dialogue during Xi visit Stocks fell sharply in China on Monday, with investors having few concrete details to cheer from the leaders’ summit and underlying tensions resurfacing. Technology stocks fell on a bipartisan US push to ban Chinese components from data centres and the benchmark blue-chip index .CSI300 slid more than 2% to a one-year low. Agriculture and coal China’s choice of products for tariff cuts looks designed to help Beijing meet what the White House says is a $17-billion commitment to buy agricultural goods. China has already resumed large-scale buying of US soybeans under a deal struck last year to buy 25 million metric tons annually. Both countries will set up an agriculture working group under a trade council, which will hold its first meeting before the year ends to discuss two-way market access and regulation, the commerce ministry said. The presidential summit also yielded an agreement for China to import 10 million metric tons of coal annually from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the White House release showed. That amount roughly equals 2% of China’s coal imports each year. title: Rupee gains against US dollar
author: Recorder Report
description: The Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains against the US dollar in the interbank market on Monday. The local unit closed the day at 277.15, a gain of Re0.01 against the greenback. During the previous week, the Pakistani rupee closed at 277.16 against the greenback, a gain of Re0.09 from 277.25 it had closed at a week earlier. Internationally, the US dollar inched higher to hold near a two-month high on Monday, as the US-Iran standoff continued to push up oil prices while investors looked ahead to a data-packed week for more clues on inflation and central banks’ moves. The euro and sterling were both 0.1% weaker against the dollar, last at $1.1379 and $1.3232, respectively, hovering near multi-month lows against the greenback. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, was a touch higher at 101.15 and on track for a 1.7% gain in September, its best month since June. The market’s focus is set to turn to US data releases as the week unfolds, with the PCE Index on Wednesday and non-farm payrolls on Friday both expected to be consistent with further policy tightening. Currently, markets are seeing a 65% chance of a rate hike from the Fed when the central bank meets next at the end of October, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. Oil prices , a key indicator of currency parity, rebounded more than 2% on Monday after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent futures rose $2.60, or 2.49%, to $106.92 a barrel at 0803 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $94.49 a barrel, up $2.08 or 2.25%.

title: Russian oil supply to India tightens on reduced exports, strong Chinese demand
author: Reuters
description: MOSCOW/NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to further tighten in October and November due to reduced exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the world’s third-largest crude importer to buy more costly alternatives for the rest of the year, four trade sources said. India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts. However, in recent months, the world’s top crude importer China has ramped up purchases as supplies from the Middle East tightened due to the Iran war. Some Indian refiners would not be getting adequate Russian supplies in October and November, people familiar with procurement plans said. “Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners,” a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said. Russian oil arrivals to India are set to fall to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest since April, according to analytics firm Kpler. They had already declined 16.5% to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, trade data showed, although Russia remained India’s main supplier, ahead of the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela. Overall Russian export availability has contracted, notably from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have fallen by roughly half as drone attacks repeatedly suspended loadings. Oil India explores ways to get back Russian dividend India seeks alternatives from Mideast, West Africa Indian refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, traders said, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia’s Urals grade, while also purchasing Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes. Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows, with seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) providing a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China. In contrast, shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis. “It’s not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination,” a second trader said, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.

title: Pakistan becomes first country to join Hong Kong's ValidAP trade verification platform
author: BR Web Desk
description: Pakistan has taken another step towards trusted digital trade with the operationalisation of Pakistan Single Window’s (PSW) integration with ValidAP, a blockchain-based digital document verification platform developed and hosted by the Customs and Excise Department of Hong Kong, China. According to a statement, the integration, which became operational on 25 September 2026, enables electronic trade documents issued through PSW to be independently verified for authenticity and integrity using cryptographic technology, without requiring the underlying document or its sensitive information to be transmitted to or stored on the verification platform. The initiative follows the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between Pakistan Customs and the Customs and Excise Department of Hong Kong on 18 May 2026, formalising Pakistan Customs’ participation in ValidAP. Pakistan is the first country to join the platform, and the integration marks Pakistan’s first implementation of ValidAP-based digital document verification, the statement read. ValidAP uses cryptographic technology to create a unique digital fingerprint, or “hash”, of an electronic trade document. This enables authorities to verify that a document is genuine and has not been altered, without the document itself or its sensitive information being transmitted or stored on the verification platform. Pakistan’s participation in ValidAP also connects its digital trade infrastructure with an emerging regional approach to trusted electronic document verification. For Pakistan, the integration represents a further step towards a digital trade environment in which documents can be issued electronically, verified digitally and trusted across borders. It can help reduce reliance on paper-based verification and support faster and more secure processing of international trade documentation, it added.

title: Indian firms ready $3 billion of debt issues with eye on potential RBI rate hike
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: Indian companies are rushing to lock in borrowing costs ahead of a potential rate hike by the central bank, with about $3 billion of rupee debt issuances lined up over the next few days. Large Indian conglomerates, state-run firms, infrastructure investment trusts and non-bank finance companies are preparing at least 290 billion rupees ($3.02 billion) of short- to long-duration bond sales ahead of the central bank’s October 7 monetary policy decision. Some ofthe prominent corporate borrowers issuing debt include Reliance Industries, Vedanta, Delhi International Airport, Adani Airport Holdings and JSW Energy , seeking an aggregate 185 billion rupees, while infrastructure-related firms Cube Highways Trust, Interise Trust and India Infradebt are eyeing 60 billion rupees. “Issuers who have a view that rupee interest rates will go even higher are locking in rates,” said Akshay Naik, India head of debt capital markets at Citibank. “We expect issuances, particularly from large, frequent and high-rated issuers to be absorbed by investors.” India RBI may increase debt sales to drain liquidity after first such auction in 9 years Likely rate hike A large majority of market participants expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise interest rates, with further liquidity-draining measures on the cards. If they’re right, it would mark the RBI’s first rate hike since February 2023. “With the October policy approaching, there is some uncertainty around the direction of interest rates and liquidity conditions,” said Harish Reddy, co-founder, Stable Money, a fixed income investment platform. The policy decision has as its backdrop signs of broadening inflation in India and hikes by major central banks globally, including by the US Federal Reserve. Expectations for RBI policy have shifted over the past month amid a pickup in inflation and stubbornly higher oil prices, bringing prospects of an October rate hike into focus. Several foreign banks, including Citi and Deutsche Bank, have brought forward their rate-hike calls from December to October, while market pricing reflects a higher likelihood of a longer tightening cycle. While a rate hike hanging over the market’s head is pushing up corporate issuance, there is also “a lot of liquidity in the (banking) system to absorb this supply,” said Ankit Gupta, founder and MD, Digifinn, an online bond trading platform.

title: FPCCI seeks one-month extension to the income tax return deadline
author: BR Web Desk
description: Atif Ikram Sheikh, President of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FPCCI), has formally urged the government and the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns by one month – moving the cutoff date to October 31, 2026 – to facilitate trade, industry, and other tax filers. According to a statement released on Monday, the apex trade body emphasised that this extension is not a concession but a practical necessity to ensure maximum tax compliance, broaden the tax base, and alleviate the immense pressure currently faced by the business community, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and individual taxpayers. Sheikh highlighted that as the September 30 deadline approaches, taxpayers and tax practitioners are facing severe systemic bottlenecks. The FBR’s IRIS portal has been experiencing frequent slowdowns, glitches, and downtimes due to heavy national traffic. These technical disruptions are preventing thousands of willing taxpayers from submitting their returns and wealth statements accurately and on time, he added. Sheikh explained that the business community of Pakistan remains committed to fulfilling its national duty and contributing to the national exchequer. However, penalising them for systemic inefficiencies and a highly congested and insufficient digital infrastructure is deeply unfair. Income tax returns, wealth statements: PM urged to extend deadline The FPCCI leadership outlined several critical reasons for the demanded extension, pointing first to the severe instability within the FBR’s digital infrastructure. Constant lagging and crashing of the IRIS system during peak hours have made it nearly impossible for tax lawyers, chartered accountants, and individual business owners to process filings efficiently. FPCCI chief maintained that a one-month extension will provide a much-needed breathing space for taxpayers to reconcile their accounts, navigate the recent complexities introduced in the tax code, and file their returns without the fear of system crashes. Sheikh highlighted that the recent complex amendments in tax laws and reporting requirements have created widespread confusion; meaning taxpayers require additional time to thoroughly understand these technicalities to avoid unintended errors in their wealth reconciliations. He stressed that, alongside these technical hurdles, the ongoing macroeconomic challenges, including high inflation and surging operational costs, have severely stretched the administrative capacities of SMEs. Many businesses are struggling to finalize their financial audits and gather the necessary documentation within the rigid timeframe. The FPCCI stressed that granting this extension directly supports the government’s own primary objective of increasing the number of active filers. Rushing the process will inevitably result in a lower volume of submissions, whereas an extended window will yield higher revenue collection and wider, more accurate compliance. Sheikh appealed to the Prime Minister of Pakistan, the Minister for Finance and Revenue, and the Chairman of the FBR to take immediate cognisance of the ground realities. The federation warned that failure to extend the deadline could force many legitimate businesses into the non-filer category, resulting in unwarranted penalties and disruption of commercial activities that the fragile economic conditions cannot sustain.

title: Oil woes push Indian rupee to over one-week low, RBI caps fall near 96/USD
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: The Indian rupee slipped to its weakest in more than a week on Monday as oil prices marched higher, dragging down regional stocks and currencies as investors fretted over the impact of high energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty. Dollar sales from state-run banks, most likely on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India, curbed losses with the rupee settling down 0.2% at 95.9825 per dollar. Brent crude rose nearly 4% to $108.2 per barrel. US President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s peace plan, but told Axios in a phone interview that he expected US negotiators to engage in more talks this week. Investors responded by pushing bond yields higher and stocks lower. MSCI’s gauge of Asian stocks fell nearly 1% while stocks in Mumbai declined nearly 1.5% to their lowest level since April. India imports nearly 90% of its crude requirements, making the rupee one of the world’s most vulnerable currencies to the Middle East oil shock. “Several investors just have an outright bearish view on all EM Asia high-yield currencies, including the PHP, IDR and INR, given their vulnerability to higher energy costs,” analysts at Goldman Sachs said in a note, summarising feedback from investors located in the UK. Goldman, meanwhile, says the RBI has the ability to keep the rupee within the 94-97 range, or at least manage the pace of its depreciation. A glut of capital inflows sparked by policy measures has given the Indian central bank ammunition to go against the tide but investors are keeping an eye on the persistence of that defence. Between June 8 and September 18, these measures drew in $143.6 billion. “For now, 96 is the floor under INR and it doesn’t seem like the RBI will allow a move past that,” a trader at a foreign bank said.

title: Indian shares slide to near six-month low as US-Iran deadlock lifts oil prices
author: Reuters
description: Indian shares fell to near six-month lows on Monday, extending a seven-week losing streak, as oil prices rose after US-Iran peace talks reached a deadlock. US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the fighting, while Iran said only diplomacy could resolve its conflict with the United States and Israel. The deadlock raised concerns over oil supplies through the key shipping route, pushing Brent crude futures up 3.7% to $108 a barrel. For India, the world’s third-largest crude importer, higher oil prices risk stoking inflation, widening the import bill and squeezing corporate margins. The Nifty 50 fell 1.56% to 22,780.25, while the BSE Sensex shed 1.52% to 72,771.72. The indexes fell nearly 6% over the previous seven weeks, in one of their longest weekly losing streaks on record. “Markets came under renewed selling pressure on the day, with the rise in Brent crude remaining a major concern,” said Sachin Gupta, vice president of research at Choice Broking. “Another important factor is elevated global bond yields. Higher US Treasury yields can make dollar-denominated fixed-income investments relatively more attractive and increase global borrowing costs, potentially reducing foreign investment flows into emerging markets.” All 16 major sectors fell. The broader small-caps and mid-caps slipped 1.9% and 1.6%, respectively. High-weightage financials and banks lost 1.7% and 2%, respectively. Shares of top private lender HDFC Bank and oil-to-telecom conglomerate Reliance Industries slid 2.3% each, while ICICI Bank fell 1.9%. The three firms carry large weights on the benchmarks. Among stocks, Yes Bank fell 5.9% with brokerage Citi flagging near-term pressure on the stock due to weaker earnings, elevated credit costs. Bucking the broader trend, Borosil gained 6% after Investec reiterated “buy” on the consumer goods maker and hiked the price target, citing gains from anti-dumping duty on Chinese borosilicate table and kitchen glassware.

title: Special delivery: India's Tamil Nadu state hands out gold for newborns
author: AFP
description: Under the scheme, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gramme gold ring, worth some $143.
text: Authorities in India’s Tamil Nadu state gave babies born in government-run hospitals a free gold ring on Monday, an initiative aimed at boosting confidence in the public healthcare system. Under the scheme launched by actor-turned-Chief Minister Vijay, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gramme gold ring, worth some $143. Gold has immense cultural significance in India, featuring prominently in weddings and religious ceremonies, and seen as a safe generational asset. “The gold ring would give the child something valuable to keep for the years ahead,” said one mother at a government hospital in the state’s Madurai district, who declined to give her name. She was among dozens of mothers who cradled their newborns as they queued up to receive the gift. “This scheme feels personal,” another grateful mother, Stella Mary, told AFP. Officials say the initiative aims to highlight maternal and newborn care, while strengthening faith in public healthcare institutions in the southern state of over 72 million people. The scheme, however, drew some criticism from the Bharatiya Janata Party, which is in the opposition in Tamil Nadu. “A gold ring for a newborn may be a welcome gesture, but for families, the most immediate need is ensuring that essential nutrition is available every day,” party member Tamilisai Soundararajan said in a social media post. India’s overcrowded public hospitals often struggle with staff shortages, long waiting times and patchy infrastructure, prompting many patients to seek treatment in the costly private sector. While most women in India give birth in hospitals, home deliveries still occur in some rural communities, making institutional childbirth a priority for health authorities. Despite significant gains in recent years, infant and maternal mortality rates continue to languish in India. The country recorded 24 infant deaths per 1,000 live births while maternal deaths stood at 88 per 100,000 live births, according to latest official data. The gold ring scheme, known as the “Thaimaman” (maternal uncle) programme, draws on the special cultural significance of a child’s maternal uncle, who is often expected to play a key role in family milestones and celebrations. It also taps into India’s enduring obsession with gold. For many women, particularly in rural areas, gold jewellery can serve as a form of personal financial security. India is one of the world’s largest consumers of the metal. According to the World Gold Council, demand in the country reached $25 billion in the first quarter of this year.

title: Three policemen killed in firing on police vehicle in Tank
author: BR Web Desk
description: Three police personnel were killed and two others injured when unidentified armed men opened fire on a police vehicle in Wazirabad area of Tank district, Aaj News quoted police as saying on Monday. According to police, the attack took place within the jurisdiction of SMA police station, where armed men targeted the police vehicle. Three personnel died at the scene, while two others sustained injuries. Following the attack, a heavy contingent of police reached the area and cordoned it off. Police teams also collected evidence from the crime scene. The bodies of the deceased and the injured were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital, for medico-legal formalities and medical treatment, respectively. Police launched a search operation in the area to trace and arrest the attackers, while further investigation into the incident was under way. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi condemned the terrorist attack and expressed grief over the deaths of three police personnel. He extended condolences to the families of the deceased and paid tribute to the policemen for their sacrifice. Naqvi said the government stood with the families of the slain personnel and that their sacrifices in the fight against terrorism would not go in vain.

title: Imran Haleem Shaikh to take charge as BankIslami President & CEO from Sept 29
author: BR Web Desk
description: BankIslami Pakistan Limited, Pakistan’s leading Islamic financial institution, has appointed its Deputy Chief Executive Officer Imran Haleem Shaikh as President and Chief Executive Officer for a three-year term effective September 29, 2026. The bank informed the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) in a notice on Monday. “Please be advised that Imran Haleem Shaikh will take charge as President & CEO of BankIslami Pakistan Limited with effect from September 29, 2026,” read the notice. As per information available on LinkedIn, Shaikh joined BankIslami as Deputy Chief Executive Officer in January 2024, after spending more than 13 years at JS Bank, where he served as Chief Operating Officer from July 2020 to December 2023. At JS Bank, he was responsible for retail banking, consumer, product, marketing and administrative functions and was involved in the launch and expansion of Zindigi, the bank’s digital banking platform. Prior to becoming COO, Shaikh served as Chief of Staff and held several senior positions in marketing and brand management at JS Bank. He began his career at JS Group, where he worked in corporate affairs from 2006 to 2010. According to his LinkedIn profile, Shaikh holds a BBA in Marketing from the Institute of Business Management and a master’s degree with a specialisation in AI from HEC Paris. Last month, BankIslami’s Board decided that Rizwan Ata would continue to serve as the bank’s President and CEO until the completion of his current three-year term on September 28, 2026. “The Board recognised and appreciated the efforts of Rizwan Ata,” BankIslami said back then. BankIslami Pakistan appoints chairman, CEO The bank further announced the appointment of Imran Haleem Shaikh as the incoming President and CEO for a three-year term effective September 29, 2026. BankIslami Pakistan Limited was incorporated in Pakistan as a public limited company in 2004, founded by Jahangir Siddiqui & Company Limited and the Randaree family. Dubai Bank later joined as a founding shareholder in 2005. The bank was granted a license as a “Scheduled Islamic Commercial Bank” in 2005 under the Islamic banking policy of 2003 from the SBP, and it officially began operations on April 7, 2006.

title: Establish a gas market for boosting exports
author: Shahid M. Sattar
description: A functioning gas market would reward exploration at home and buy LNG abroad when its full delivered cost is competitive. Pakistan currently does neither. Pakistan’s gas debate is usually presented as a choice between indigenous gas and imported LNG. That framing hides the real problem: Pakistan does not yet have a market capable of telling either source where it is economical, where it is reliable, and where it should lose. The country needs both, but neither should be protected from competition. Local producers should be able to sell directly to creditworthy buyers at transparent market-linked prices. LNG should enter through the same open network whenever its full delivered cost is competitive. The cheapest reliable molecule should win; every subsidy, bottleneck and payment delay that prevents that outcome should be treated as an economic cost. That sounds obvious. Pakistan has managed to make it revolutionary because gas policy still treats molecules as instruments of allocation rather than commodities moving through a disciplined market. Gas is assigned administratively, transported by utilities that also trade it, priced through layers of cross-subsidy and used to rescue whichever part of the energy system is in trouble that month. Producers wait for allocations and payments. Private LNG suppliers wait for pipeline access. Consumers wait for gas. The only thing that moves promptly is circular debt. Exploration policy and LNG policy cannot succeed separately because both depend on the same missing institution: a functioning gas market. The indigenous decline is a market failure The policy debate therefore needs a different sequence. Pakistan should not ask first whether domestic gas or LNG deserves priority. It should ask what market design would make each source reveal its true cost, attract capital where supply can be developed, and exit where it cannot compete. Without that architecture, every new discovery risks becoming another administered allocation and every imported cargo risks becoming another liability on the public balance sheet. The official numbers are stark. During July–March FY2026, Pakistan consumed an average 2,929 mmcfd of gas: 2,316 mmcfd of indigenous supply and 613 mmcfd of RLNG. The Pakistan Economic Survey says depletion of indigenous reserves is a major concern and that no significant discoveries have been made. These figures show more than geological decline; they show a market that has stopped transmitting investable signals. Weak incentives, delayed decisions, payment risk, constrained marketing freedom and a downstream system that cannot reliably convert discovery into cash have turned exploration risk into policy risk. Exploration is risky capital. Investors spend first, often for years, and may find nothing. If they do find gas, they need a bankable route from the wellhead to a paying customer. A policy can offer an attractive headline price, but the incentive is meaningless if allocation is delayed, the buyer is insolvent, the pipeline is controlled by a commercial rival, invoices remain unpaid or government changes the rules after the investment has been sunk. The recent offshore round is encouraging but should be read honestly. Bids covered 23 blocks and about 53,510 square kilometres. The Petroleum Division reports roughly US$80 million of Phase-I commitments, with possible investment of US$750 million to US$1 billion if drilling proceeds. These are commitments, not discoveries. Serious drilling still requires a route from any discovery to a solvent market. Pakistan has done this before The lesson is not theoretical. I was involved in the producer-pricing reforms of the early 1990s that replaced discretionary, rate-of-return thinking with compensation linked to international energy values. The subsequent petroleum policy carried that logic forward through market-related producer pricing, clearer block awards and greater marketing freedom. Foreign and local companies brought capital, technology and management expertise, and national gas production rose from roughly 1,800 mmcfd to around 4,000 mmcfd within the following years. The evidence matters because it shows that geology responds to institutions: when investors can see price, access and payment discipline, capital follows. The point is not nostalgia for one policy formula. Oil linkage designed three decades ago is not automatically the right benchmark today. The point is that investors respond when economic terms are credible, rules are implemented and the route to market is clear. Pakistan later weakened that bargain through delayed payments, administrative allocation, distorted consumer prices and a utility structure that socialized inefficiency. title: South African rand slips as US-Iran stalemate pushes oil prices higher
author: Reuters
description: JOHANNESBURG: The South African rand slipped half a percent in early trade on Monday as the US-Iran standoff continued to drive oil prices higher, weighing on risk-sensitive currencies in oil-importing economies. At 0734 GMT the rand traded at 16.40 against the dollar , about 0.5% weaker than its previous close. Oil prices climbed more than 3% on Monday with Brent crude futures last above $107 a barrel, after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. South Africa imports most of its fuel, leaving the economy vulnerable to swings in global oil prices since the Iran conflict began in late February. “Volatility in the rand could be elevated this week as the data calendar is jam-packed with data out of the US, culminating in the US non-farm payrolls on Friday,” said Andre Cilliers at TreasuryONE. On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index fell 1.7% in early trade. Gold Fields led losses, dropping about 13% after Australia’s Northern Star Resources said it had rejected an unsolicited A$38.7 billion ($27.1 billion) takeover approach. South Africa’s benchmark 2035 government bond also weakened, as the yield rose 5.5 basis points to 8.855%.

title: Xavi pleased with first week as Netherlands coach, but wants more
author: Reuters
description: AMSTERDAM: Netherlands coach Xavi Hernández is pleased with his first week in charge but now wants his side to show an even more attacking game in their next two Nations League fixtures. The Spanish World Cup winner wants the Dutch side playing with more of the attacking intensity that paid off last Thursday when their persistent forays forced a late equaliser against Germany in Amsterdam. This was followed by their first victory under Xavi, a 2-1 defeat of Serbia on Sunday. “It is always most important to get the three points, I’m happy that we managed to do that. But we do need to play better, because, especially in the first half, we did not press well,“ he said. “Nevertheless, I’m very satisfied after a week of work.” Greece stun Germany 1-0 in losing home debut for Klopp Xavi singled out AZ Alkmaar striker Mexx Meerdink, who made his a debut as a substitute against Germany and then marked his first start for the Dutch by scoring both goals against Serbia. “Mexx is a very hard worker who understands how we want to play,“ Xavi said. “He helped the team with more than just his goals, although those certainly helped. The work he did for the team was fantastic.” The Dutch side face Greece next, in Thessaloniki on Thursday, then entertain Serbia in Eindhoven on Sunday. Xavi was clear about where improvements on last week were needed. “For example, there were many moments when we needed to attack the spaces, but we didn’t do it. That is something we need to improve. But also things such as making the pitch wider and moving the ball around more quickly,“ he said. “But the most important thing is that we are creating a lot of chances. The players feel comfortable on the pitch with the structure we are playing in, so a lot of things are also going well.“

title: AKD Securities warns of deepfake scam impersonating Dhedhi, Hina Junaid
author: BR Web Desk
description: AKD Securities Limited has warned investors about AI-generated and deepfake videos impersonating AKD Group Chairman Aqeel Karim Dhedhi and company Chairperson Hina Junaid, saying the content was being used to solicit funds through unauthorised investment schemes and stock-market advisory services. In a notice to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) on Monday, the brokerage house said that unidentified individuals or groups had created fake social media accounts and pages, including on Facebook, using the names, photographs and voices of Dhedhi and Junaid, which “are being misused through AI-generated and/or deepfake video content”. “The purpose of this activity appears to be the solicitation of funds under the name of fake & unauthorized schemes/ advisory for investing in listed securities/stocks,” the company said. AKD Securities said it had filed a complaint with the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on September 16 seeking an investigation and registration of a case against those involved, as well as removal or blocking of the fraudulent content from the relevant platforms. “We are pursuing all available legal remedies against those responsible for such fraudulent activities.” “The company hereby categorically denies any connection to the fraudulent content, accounts, callers, or any website or application promoting such claims. Neither Aqeel Karim Dhedhi, Hina Junaid, the company, nor any entity within the AKD Group has launched, endorsed, sponsored, authorised, or otherwise been associated with any such investment scheme, platform, account, page or group,” the listed company said. The brokerage urged investors and the general public “to exercise caution and to refrain from engaging with, relying on, or acting upon any such unauthorised content or calls”.

title: Foreign woman allegedly gang-raped records statement before Lahore magistrate
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: The Defence C police has registered a case against three unidentified suspects on the woman’s complaint.
text: LAHORE: A foreign woman who was allegedly gang-raped recorded her statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before a judicial magistrate at the Cantonment Courts on Monday. The 20-year-old Azeri woman had traveled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday. It was the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. The woman was brought to the court under tight security to record her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer. Before the proceedings began, the magistrate ordered all unrelated persons to leave the courtroom. The statement continued for more than an hour. The Defence C police had registered a case against three unidentified suspects on the woman’s complaint. title: 'Hurting' badminton star Sindhu says Asian Games schedule 'took toll'
author: AFP
description: NAGOYA: India’s two-time Olympic badminton medallist P.V. Sindhu said Monday she was “hurting” after defeat following three matches in 18 hours at the Asian Games. The former world champion is the latest badminton player to take aim at the scheduling at the Games in Nagoya. Sindhu battled to defeat over three gruelling games against China’s Chen Yufei in Sunday’s quarter-finals. The 31-year-old played both her second- and third-round matches on Saturday, and was back on court the next day to face former Olympic champion Chen. Following the gruelling last-eight clash, which Chen won 11-21, 21-18, 21-10, Sindhu took to social media to voice her pain at her exit. “I needed a little time to put this into words. My Asian Games campaign is over, and I’m hurting,” she wrote on X to her three million followers. “Three points from closing out that quarter-final. I keep coming back to those three points.” Sindhu, who clinched Olympic silver in 2016 and bronze in 2021, added: “Letting it slip hurts. “Three matches in 18 hours. Back at 3:00 am, out again at 8:30 am. It took a toll.” Sindhu’s India teammate H.S. Prannoy has similarly condemned the scheduling for badminton players at the Games. “It’s cruel because everybody is aiming for a good Asian Games, which comes once in four years,” Prannoy said at the weekend. “To have two singles games in a day, I haven’t seen it like that in ages.”

title: CM Afridi strikes defiant tone as federal ministers rail against KP govt's counter-terror fight
author: News Desk
description: Chaudhry assails KP govt's lack of efforts; Tarar says PTI will have to decide if it is "with Pakistan or with Afghanistan".
text: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday struck a defiant tone and again panned the Centre’s counterterrorism policy as federal ministers railed against his government’s efforts to combat terrorism. Afridi, who was elected as the KP CM in October 2025, has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan. Earlier in the day, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar held a press conference in Islamabad, where they highlighted flaws in the KP government’s “leadership” and governance. Meanwhile in Peshawar, addressing a meeting regarding law and order, the KP CM stressed that merely providing resources to the police would not solve the problem until there was a policy shift. “We repeatedly stated that the state’s current policy was flawed. The blood of our Pakhtuns will flow again,” Afridi said, regretting that federal ministers “dismissed our repeated warnings as propaganda and lies”. The chief minister highlighted that he had been consistently calling for a change to the “failed policy of 22 years”. Flanked by Tarar, Chaudhry said the PTI-led KP government had not made adequate efforts to combat terrorism. He noted that a political leadership could “provide three things in the fight against terrorism: leadership, resources and powers”. Chaudhry contended that the provincial administration in KP — where the PTI has been in power since 2013 — “did not provide leadership to the security forces over the past 14 years”. The interior official accused the PTI-led government of “creating space” for terrorists. “If Pakistan is burning in the fire of terrorism, it is because of KP’s incompetent leadership,” he maintained. Chaudhry then noted that it was the provincial government’s responsibility to allocate funds for counter-terrorism in the budget. “[Then], why did you not provide the resources?” he asked, adding that the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) was still not functional in the entire province. “Your forces cannot fight unarmed. You do not have bulletproof jackets, cars, training, CTD, Safe City [project], or a forensic lab,” he said, claiming that Safe City projects had been completed on the tehsil level as well in Punjab. The state minister sought accountability from KP over the usage of even one per cent of the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award, which he said amounted to Rs800 billion. Chaudhry pointed out that Afridi and his information minister did not attend the funeral prayers of the victims of the Sept 18 Kohat blast , but were rather “busy in their street movement or other matters”. He recalled that the KP CM held a “very lengthy” press conference in Dera Ismail Khan in the wake of Saturday’s suicide blast , which claimed 12 lives. “Why did they not condemn Afghanistan? Why do you have a soft attitude on Afghanistan? Why do you deliberately employ such ambiguity and demeanour, and do not openly condemn or name the real enemy or from where these proxies operate?” he asked. Chaudhry reiterated his criticism of the recent KP Police Act , which has been proposed to replace a 2017 version and is aimed at curtailing the powers of the provincial inspector general (IG). He also responded to PTI’s allegation that the party had not been included in discussions about war on terrorism, saying that the party leadership did not show up to meetings when invited. “You come to Islamabad to demand NFC funds , but your CM does not show up for anti-terrorism meetings,” Chaudhry said. Meanwhile, Tarar said PTI had not taken ownership of the fight against terrorism, again terming the party as the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan’s (TTP) “B team”. He alleged that PTI had facilitated terrorists in its over 12 years of governing KP and that it was not condemning them as it “suits PTI’s financial interests”. “Sohail Afridi organised a ceremony and two Afghans did not stand up to pay respect to the national anthem. If I was there, I would have dealt with them right then and there. I would have banned them,” Tarar said. Such an incident took place in September 2024 , when PTI’s Ali Amin Gandapur was serving as the chief minister. Tarar went on to highlight that the KP government had not ensured the registration of all vehicles yet, as doing so makes the “surveillance of terrorists easier”. He added that potential revenue generated from car registration could have been used for the benefit of the people of KP. “You sacrificed the security of the entire province for your political gains. “You will now have to decide if you are with Pakistan or with Afghanistan. It is as clear as that,” the information minister declared. During his press conference, Chaudhry also highlighted the Afghan Taliban’s support for terrorist activities in Pakistan. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. The state minister noted that terrorist “proxies are financed by our eastern border and their hideouts are on the western border”. He emphasised that Islamabad had employed “every way” to convey its concerns to Kabul, including dialogue, dossiers and international forums, but to no avail. Referring to the recent attack on a rescue vehicle carrying DI Khan blast victims, Chaudhry said that attacking rescue teams was not allowed even during war. “This is their true face. Is this jihad? Even an enemy with some rules does not carry out such attacks.” He said such terrorist activities were carried out in exchange for receiving funds in dollars, which were proportional to the number of casualties. The interior official asserted that Pakistan had the “best systems” for investigating the identity of a suspected terrorist. “Very few countries have enough data that in less than a minute, any heinous crime or terrorist incident-related information can be accessed in Nadra and other databases […] we instantly find out whether they are Pakistanis [or not].” He then recalled that when authorities did not find any details in the database for a recent incident, they used open-source intelligence and geolocated a terrorist’s picture to Kabul’s Pashtunistan Square. September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan, with the former saying it struck terrorist sites in the border region in response to a recent spate of terrorist attacks . Pakistan conducted “aerial and drone strikes” in another 10 locations across Afghanistan in retaliation for drones launched from across the border that were shot down in KP. The Foreign Office (FO) has said a demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on Saturday on account of the Sept 23 airspace violation by drones. Meanwhile, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi urged the PTI to further postpone its long march now set for Oct 4 . “Fire is raging here,” he told the media while speaking on the province’s security situation. “I advise the provincial government to postpone their long march due to the law and order situation, call all stakeholders and political parties to discuss peace in the province, and fight terrorism on the frontline.” He contended that the PTI wanted to march on Islamabad and “spread chaos” even when terrorist incidents in KP were claiming people’s lives. On speculations regarding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said that in his opinion, such a move could be taken if the federal government deemed it necessary “to save the province”. He warned the PTI government not to “force the Centre” to impose governor’s rule.

title: 3 traffic policemen martyred in attack on vehicle in KP's Tank
author: Muhammad Irfan Mughal
description: An investigation into the attack was under way, with efforts being made to identify and arrest those involved, police say.
text: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Three traffic policemen were martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on their mobile van in the Wazirabad Bazaar area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district, a senior police official confirmed. “Three traffic policemen travelling in the mobile van were martyred on the spot in the attack,” District Police Officer Abdul Samad Khan told Dawn , adding that the attackers fled the scene. Khan said the attackers had also taken away the traffic police vehicle after the incident. However, the vehicle was later recovered from the Garah Budha area, he added. He added that two passers-by were also injured in the firing and were shifted to a hospital for treatment. “Police have sealed the roads and other possible routes, including pedestrian tracks, to prevent the attackers from escaping,” the DPO told Dawn . He said efforts were underway to trace and arrest those involved. The attack triggered a security operation in the area, with police personnel deployed at various points and search efforts continuing. Further details about the identity of the attackers and the motive behind the attack were not immediately available. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed deep sorrow over the attack and sought a report from the relevant senior authorities. In a statement, the governor conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and colleagues of the martyred policemen. Kundi directed the authorities to ensure that all possible medical treatment was provided to the injured and prayed for their early recovery. Earlier this month, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials. On July 26, a terrorist attack on a joint police checkpost in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Tank district martyred 15 people, including 14 security personnel, the military’s media wing. Among those martyred were 12 soldiers, two policemen and a government official. In another attack during the same month, two cops were martyred and as many injured in what police suspected was an improvised explosive device (IED) attack. KP has been facing security challenges, and according to monthly data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), mainland KP recorded 54 terrorist attacks last month, marking a 50 per cent increase compared to July.

title: India, Pakistan on Asian Games collision course after cricket washout
author: AFP
description: NAGOYA: India and Pakistan stayed on course to meet in the Asian Games cricket final after both men’s quarter-finals were abandoned Monday because of rain and a sodden outfield in Nagoya. Pakistan went through first against Hong Kong without a ball being bowled under competition rules that say the highest-seeded side progresses. A few hours later, with rain in the air, India progressed against Afghanistan with no prospect of play for the same reason. It deprived spectators at the Korogi Athletic Park the chance to see India’s 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in action. The fearless teenager topped the T20 Indian Premier League batting charts earlier this year. “We are here for the match but unfortunately it rained. The rain started yesterday, so hard luck for us. We would have been happy to play here with India – our players are in form,” said Afghanistan’s Mohammad Akram. World T20 champions India on alert for Afghanistan after Japan scare “We played two matches here on this ground, so we know the condition very well. But unfortunately the rain has ruined everything. “We saw the rain on our mobile phones. Everyone was sad.” Sri Lanka play Nepal and Bangladesh face Malaysia, weather permitting, in the last two quarter-finals on Tuesday.

title: CM Murad approves request to extend Mir Raza judicial commission’s tenure
author: BR Web Desk
description: The tenure of the one-member judicial commission probing the death of young businessman Mir Raza Ali has been extended until October 15, as the panel continues examining alleged lapses in the investigation and medical examination of the case, Aaj News reported on Monday. The commission’s one-month term expired on September 27. According to its registrar, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah has approved a summary to extend its tenure until October 15, while formal notification of the extension will require approval from the Sindh Cabinet. The commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, has currently adjourned proceedings until October 2 to allow completion of statements from remaining witnesses and work on its final report. During its proceedings, the commission has raised questions over the handling of evidence and the performance of the initial investigation team. It has also examined discrepancies in the first post-mortem and issues surrounding the constitution of medical boards. The commission has expressed concern over the handling of CCTV footage from the crime scene. During earlier proceedings, it was told that 52 cameras were installed around the area but footage from only one camera had initially been obtained. The commission also questioned the circumstances in which part of the crime scene was set on fire. Justice Sial has also questioned the performance of the first investigation team and summoned senior officials over issues relating to the investigation and medical examination. The commission has examined alleged discrepancies in Mir Raza’s first post-mortem report, with police surgeon Dr Summaiyya Syed pointing out deficiencies in the report. A subsequent post-mortem reportedly ruled out suicide, according to earlier court proceedings. The commission has also raised concerns over the constitution and functioning of medical boards and summoned senior health officials, including Health Secretary Tahir Hussain Sangi and Director General Health Shehryar Memon, according to the information provided by the commission. Mir Raza’s sister Alishba and family lawyer Jibran Nasir have said they would approach the court seeking the formation of an empowered joint investigation team (JIT) to identify and arrest those responsible for his death, citing shortcomings in the police investigation. Case background Mir Raza Ali, a young businessman, went missing on July 28, 2026, and his body was recovered the following day. Initial police reports suggested suicide, but his family insisted he was murdered. A second post-mortem, conducted after exhumation, revealed signs of torture, multiple fractures, and a gunshot wound from the rear, leading to a murder charge being added to the case. A new police investigation team was formed, and the Sindh High Court constituted a judicial commission to investigate his death. The investigation team has since confirmed that Mir Raza was murdered, ruling out suicide.

title: Belgium’s new boss Van Bommel relishing clash with Zidane
author: Reuters
description: BRUSSELS: Belgium coach Mark van Bommel is relishing the opportunity to pit his wits against Zinedine Zidane but is disappointed that Kylian Mbappe will be missing when they host France in the Nations League on Monday. Van Bommel got off to a dream start in his first game in charge of Belgium with a 2-0 away win over Italy in their Group A1 game on Friday and said he wants his side to keep up the attacking approach they showed in Rome. “I started (my coaching tenure) last Monday by emphasising intensity and willingness to work,” he told a press conference on Sunday. “The idea has to remain the same. title: 5 men held over bomb scare at England base used by US to attack Iran are UK nationals: police
author: Reuters | AFP
description: The five suspects — a 25-year-old, three men aged 24 and a 23-year-old — are all based in London, say police.
text: Five men held over a bomb scare at a British air base used by the US are all UK nationals aged in their mid-20s, British counter-terror police said Monday. The five — a 25-year-old, three men aged 24 and a 23-year-old — all based in London, have been detained since Sunday on suspicion of offences including “preparation of a terrorist act” under UK anti-terrorism laws, according to police. The five were questioned by the police on Monday. Officers detained the group in the early hours of Sunday after they received a tip-off that three large white vans had been seen heading to the military airfield of RAF Fairford in the west of England. US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to do “big damage” and had been under investigation by British and US authorities. However, a local farmer said she had tipped off police after seeing a group of “hooded and masked men” running into the fields. British counterterrorism detectives have publicly shared little about the suspects but a source familiar with the investigation earlier said an Iranian-linked motive was considered the most likely, while a Russian sabotage operation or a terrorism plot were also being looked at as possibilities. Defence minister Wes Streeting told BBC News on Monday that he would not speculate about motives of a live investigation. But he added on the general Iranian threat to the country: “We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm. We know that they hate our democracy, and we know that we regularly have to thwart Iranian attempts to threaten either our interests or indeed our allies.” The Iranian embassy in London said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation that Tehran was involved in the bomb scare. In an X post, the embassy criticised “the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Iran” to the incident. In May, Britain sanctioned 12 individuals and entities linked to Iran, accusing them of involvement in hostile activity including plotting attacks and providing financial services to groups seeking to destabilise the UK and other countries. Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in attacks or plots in the UK and elsewhere. The British government had given authorisation to the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The government has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being regularly updated on the incident and he cancelled attending at least two events at his Labour Party’s annual conference on Sunday. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards had warned Britain in July not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target. In Fairford, police have imposed a 400-metre cordon around the base and evacuated residents from 85 homes. A bomb disposal robot could be seen on Sunday operating around the three white vans, while security was stepped up around the base. Armed police stood guard at the main entrance while large machinery was used to block other access points. Security was also stepped up at other US bases in Britain.

title: India's top court says need to fix accountability over Delhi rape cases, media reports
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court of India on Monday pushed for accountability over a recent spate of rape cases in the national capital and neighbouring districts, saying they reflected a “failure of law enforcement”, local media reported. Hundreds of students protested in Delhi last week demanding better safety for women after a teenager said she was gang-raped by three men at a park in the city. Last month, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped in a moving bus by the driver and conductor, local media reported. The Supreme Court said public spaces, including parks and buses, could not become “high-risk” zones because of poor lighting and surveillance, and other basic facilities, legal news website Live Law reported. The court said fixing accountability was necessary and directed its administration to file a public interest petition on the issue for the court to pursue, legal news website Bar and Bench said. India opposition lawmaker arrested on rape charges Sexual violence is a major problem across India, with more than 80 rapes reported to police every day, according to the National Crime Records Bureau. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta told a TV channel last week that there had been lapses and vowed to improve security, while Delhi Police said it had increased “visible policing” and intensified patrolling.
