title: UK's Miliband announces sanctions on goods from West Bank over 'ethnic cleansing' by Israeli settlers
author: AFP | News Desk
description: Twelve countries, including France and the UK, say to sanction trade from Israeli settlements.
text: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Tuesday accused the Israeli government of turning a “blind eye” to what he called “ethnic cleansing” by settlers in the West Bank. In a video statement, he called the situation in Palestine a “moral emergency” and said that there is increasing evidence of war crimes in Gaza. “We are witnessing unprecedented settler terrorism in the West Bank,” he said. “The British government has come to the same conclusion as the former prime minister of Israel and others, that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists.” He noted that Tel Aviv had not only ignored these developments, but that members and officials had made statements or taken actions enabling the forced displacement of Palestinians. “We will not stand by. We’re going to be stronger in standing up for what is right, and bolder in the action we take,” Miliband said, adding that London’s north star was the two-state solution. “Today, we are calling out the occupation of Palestine as unlawful,” he added. “We are banning the import of goods from illegal settlements, we’re taking action on services to target those who finance, facilitate or construct new settlements, and we’re banning advertisements of settlement properties and land.” In parliament today, Miliband said the British government would introduce “an import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories”, in a move coordinated with other countries. “The British government agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists,” said Miliband. He also announced that Britain would “take action against specific companies and individuals who provide services such as construction, infrastructure, financing, or real estate for settlement expansion” and that the measures would be in place within six to nine months. Miliband added that the UK was sanctioning “a further set of extremist settlers who have supported or incited acts of violence against Palestinian communities”. Miliband, the son of Jewish refugees to Britain, said he was “proud” of his Jewish heritage and was “unwavering” in his support of Israel. “There is absolutely no contradiction between this and my support for the State of Palestine,” he added. Twelve countries, including the UK, Canada and France, said they would slap sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, after increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the occupied territory. Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, and Sweden also plan to limit trade with the settlements, the nations’ foreign ministers said in a joint statement . Ireland and Spain have already taken measures against trade with Israeli settlements, and France has for weeks been pushing for a similar decision from the European Union , Israel’s leading trading partner, but has been blocked by some members. “The government of Israel’s actions in the West Bank are undermining the possibility of a two-state solution,” the 12 ministers said, referring to a plan under which two states — one Israeli and one Palestinian — would live peacefully side by side. “The situation is rapidly deteriorating amid unprecedented levels of settler violence and settlement expansion,” they warned. “The government of Israel must immediately halt the expansion of settlements and civilian administrative powers, ensure accountability for settler violence, and investigate allegations against Israeli forces.” The ministers said the 12 countries “confirm their intention to introduce national and/or support European restrictions on trade in goods with settlements which are illegal under international law, or that they are actively considering these and other measures, in accordance with their national procedures.” An Israeli court rejected a bid from rights groups to halt the development of a settlement in the occupied West Bank that would severely undermine the territorial contiguity of a future Palestinian state. The Jerusalem District Court said in a ruling it had dismissed the motion, which aimed to stall the publication of tenders for the settlement east of Jerusalem. Israel’s construction and housing ministry opened a tender for construction of more than 1,200 housing units in July , leading NGOs to file motions against it. The E1 plan — approved by Israel last year after decades of being frozen, notably due to pressure from successive US administrations — would further isolate Israeli-occupied east Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank. Six European countries, including the UK and France, called on Israel to halt the project in August. The Israeli judge ruled that “no irreversible physical changes are imminent, and adequate legal safeguards are in place” for the development project, arguing that courts could bring a permanent ruling on the project as a whole, well before physical construction begins on the ground. The petitioners, including Israeli NGO Peace Now, had argued that the project would lead to the eviction of hundreds of Palestinians. “The court’s decision plays into the government’s hands, allowing it to use the final months of its term to establish facts on the ground that will create a destructive reality which will be extremely difficult to reverse,” the NGOs said in a statement reacting to the ruling.

title: Pakistan announces first national action plan to conserve sharks
author: APP
description: Among the proposed measures are mandatory fins-naturally-attached policies, species-specific protections, shark sanctuaries and mangrove restoration.
text: Maritime Affairs Minister Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry on Tuesday announced the country’s first national action plan for shark conservation. The 10-year National Plan of Action for the Conservation and Management of Sharks (NPOA) will seek to restore declining shark populations, curb illegal finning and bycatch, protect critical marine habitats and promote sustainable fisheries in Pakistani waters through 2035. The plan is to be implemented in three phases, with an estimated $3.8 million to $5m in funding during its first five years. Chaudhry said the plan would be overseen by a multi-stakeholder National Advisory Committee. The minister said the plan sought to “strengthen fisheries management and enforcement while improving data collection and scientific research on shark populations”. Among the proposed measures are mandatory fins-naturally-attached policies, species-specific protections, shark sanctuaries, mangrove restoration and steps to reduce shark deaths as bycatch across fisheries. The plan also seeks to improve the livelihoods of coastal fishing communities through targeted support, while encouraging sustainable shark fisheries and greater international cooperation, including through Pakistan’s participation in the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission. Chaudhry said the implementation would be assessed annually against performance indicators such as landing-site monitoring coverage, completion of stock assessments, use of vessel monitoring systems and reductions in bycatch mortality. Formal reviews would be carried out every three years. The plan covers all chondrichthyan species found in Pakistani waters, including sharks, rays, skates and chimaeras, with a particular focus on species targeted by fisheries or facing high levels of bycatch mortality. “Although the primary emphasis is on sharks, the management frameworks, data collection systems and enforcement mechanisms established through the NPOA will also benefit other elasmobranch species,” the minister said. He said the action plan was tailored to Pakistan’s ecological, institutional and socio-economic conditions while remaining aligned with the Food and Agriculture Organisation’s International Plan of Action for Sharks and other international best practices. Chaudhry said preparation of the plan met Pakistan’s responsibilities as a shark-fishing nation under international fisheries law. The FAO’s international shark action plan encourages countries to develop national conservation and management plans, minimise waste and promote sustainable fishing practices, he added. “Responsible management of marine resources must come first,” Chaudhry said, stressing the need for stronger safeguards for vulnerable shark species and those whose capture is prohibited. According to a 2021 assessment by the World Wide Fund for Nature-Pakistan (WWF-P), shark landings in Pakistan decreased by over 85 per cent in five decades, which is more than the average decline in shark resources across the world. WWF-P had suggested a ban on the catch of endangered shark species and the import and export of shark fins at the time.

title: Sindh AG interrupts Mir Raza commission proceedings during police surgeon's testimony, objects to family's queries
author: Ishaq Tanoli
description: "Deliberate attempt" made by AG to restrain commission from addressing family’s questions, says Justice Sial; notice issued to Sindh home minister.
text: KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to probe the circumstances and possible negligence around the Mir Raza Ali murder case issued a notice to Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar after the Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero interrupted the proceedings on Tuesday and objected to the lawyer representing the victims’ family asking any questions. The interruption came during Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed’s testimony. The order issued after the commission’s proceedings stated: “It is regrettable that the commission’s proceedings have been interrupted by Sindh Advocate General Jawad Dero. He has objected to the family’s counsel asking any questions on behalf of the deceased’s family. “The highest law officer of the Sindh government making such a submission surprised me. It is more meaningful that the disturbance comes at a time when the police surgeon was explaining the role of senior police officers during the post-mortem examination.” The murder case has been mired in controversy, particularly after Dr Syed pointed out flaws in the findings of Ali’s first autopsy. Following that, Ali’s body was exhumed a second post-mortem was conducted. Dr Syed was part of the medical board that conducted the second autopsy, whose findings ruled out the possibility of suicide — a likelihood around which the law enforcers had initially tried to build the case. Meanwhile, Ali’s family accused police of trying to bury the facts. The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, heard the case today and noted in its order that Sindh Assembly member Faryal Talpur had suggested its formation to the provincial chief executive “for a transparent and impartial comprehensive investigation”. The order cited a Dawn report dated Aug 9, according to which, it said, Talpur stressed that justice for Ali must be ensured and “public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case. The newspaper further cites her as saying that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system was the fundamental responsibility of the government and relevant institutions”. Sindh Home Minister Lanjar and Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah had echoed these sentiments, the order stated. Justice Sial further wrote in the order that he was saddened that the advocate general had objected to requests by Ali’s family through their counsel for certain clarification. “It is the commission’s discretion to determine whether a query is relevant to the proceedings or not. Further, the commission’s terms of reference required it to find the true facts and circumstances of the case,” he said, adding that a notice was being issued to Lanjar to appear before the commission on Sept 10 and “put forward his stance […] as to whether the family is barred from asking questions to satisfy themselves that justice is being done”. Justice Sial further stated, “In my opinion, a deliberate attempt has been made by the Sindh advocate general to restrain the commission from addressing the family’s queries in a transparent manner.” In a separate development, a two-member bench of the SHC, headed by Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar and including Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri, took up a petition seeking the quashing of a case registered on August 27 against “around 100 people” for staging a protest in connection with the case. In the first information report (FIR), the protesters have been accused of blocking the road for vehicular movement and pedestrians at Karachi’s Sharea Faisal. The plea, a copy of which is available with Dawn , named Ammar Ahmed Khan, Muhammad Zubai Ali, Taha Shaikh, Zarar Khalid, Saad Shehriyar, and Hassan Surya as the petitioners. The SHC issued notices to the Sindh advocate general, the prosecutor general and other respondents for Nov 11 after hearing the plea today, directing that in the meantime, no coercive action should be taken against the petitioners. The court further directed that the investigation should be conducted strictly in accordance with the law and directed the petitioners to cooperate when required. “It is clarified that this order shall not be construed as an impediment in conducting the investigation strictly in accordance with law,” the court said. The body of 25-year-old Ali was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. Days after the recovery of Ali’s body on July 29, Dr Syed had told Geo News that the post-mortem findings in the case had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. On August 6, a Karachi court took up an application by Ali’s father, allowed the exhumation of his body, ordered the formation of a medico-legal board for the purpose and directed that a second autopsy of Ali’s body be conducted. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with police surgeon Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed. But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, the counsel for Ali’s family, Nasir, accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on August 8. A day later, the Sindh inspector general of police’s (IG) office notified the reconstitution of the investigating team probing Ali’s death while Karachi Additional IG Azad Khan transferred the investigation into Ali’s murder to Zaman Town police station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was registered under charges of kidnapping. The order for the probe team’s reconstitution also showed that a murder charge had been added to the first information report. The same day, the Sindh government decided to seek a judicial commission for the case’s investigation, only to defer the plan a day later after Ali’s family said they had made no such demand and had faith in the new investigation team. On Aug 19, Ali’s parents, Mir Hussain and Mariam Hussain, wrote to Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, seeking his “direct supervision of the murder investigation”. They also urged the chief minister to order an investigation and departmental inquiry into the previous investigation team and immediately suspend the officers involved. The provincial government acknowledged the letter and announced the decision on Aug 23 to form a judicial commission to determine whether the investigation in the case was being conducted impartially and to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ali’s death. However, soon after the announcement, the counsel for Ali’s family raised objections and later approached the Sindh High Court (SHC). The petition was filed on August 24 in objection to the provincial government’s decision to form a judicial commission and sought the formation of an independent and multi-agency JIT “comprising officers who have had no previous involvement in the case” in place of the commission. On Sept 2, the SHC dismissed a petition filed by Ali’s family, seeking the formation of a JIT to probe his murder, observing that constituting such a body was the “prerogative of the government”. Meanwhile, the final report of Ali’s second post-mortem for the Mir Raza Ali murder case confirmed that his death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back. “Death occurred due to cardiac rupture consequent to perforating firearm injury of the chest,” the report stated, adding that the entry wound was on the posterior thorax (back) and the exit wound on the anterior thorax (front of the chest). “The findings are inconsistent with suicide as the manner of death,” it confirmed.

title: PM Shehbaz seeks input from business community as he stresses export-led growth
author: News Desk
description: Notes govt made long-overdue structural reforms through consultation with businesspeople.
text: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday sought recommendations from industrialists and businesspeople on how to increase export-led growth in the country. “Whatever growth we have to achieve, it has to be export-led growth, period,” the premier remarked while addressing a meeting with prominent leaders of the business community. He added that any other kind of growth had “no meaning” and reinforced that economic growth had to be export-led. “Today’s meeting is because we’re in the first quarter, in the month of September. I need your opinions on how to increase our exports, as well as what challenges we will face and how to address them,” PM Shehbaz said. The prime minister gave the example of special tax relief to exporters as a means to achieve this growth. He recalled that in the run-up to the federal budget presented in June this year, the government held multiple meetings and had “intense consultations” with the business community. “Through your consultations in difficult times, the way we brought structural changes over the past two-and-a-half years … it’s teamwork. It’s a tremendous teamwork,” PM Shehbaz said. “As a result, we made overdue structural reforms. It’s a long journey, but through enforcement we recovered Rs800 billion in one year. No new taxes were imposed.” PM Shehbaz praised the teamwork involved between the business community and the government, adding that Pakistan was ready to pursue growth with their input. In July, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the government was pursuing a strategy to diversify exportable products and market portfolios to achieve a target of six per cent sustainable economic growth. “Our destination is not only stabilisation but sustainable growth of at least 6pc. That growth has to be export-led; otherwise it will become another economic bubble that bursts within a few years,” he said. Last Monday, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said that the government’s focus was on building an ecosystem to support sustainable growth that was led by the private sector and export-driven. The minister said Pakistan had moved from stabilisation towards growth, but the key challenge now was to ensure its sustainability. Earlier this week, PM Shehbaz welcomed the launch of export insurance coverage by the Export Development Fund (EDF) and the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan, saying the facility would help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) expand the country’s exports. Chairing a meeting on the EDF, he said the Rs3bn risk pool would expand access to export credit insurance, especially for SMEs, and help the business community increase export volumes. title: IHC forms larger bench to hear plea against PTI's Sept 27 protest
author: Malik Asad
description: Notices issued to Islamabad IG and police chiefs of KP, Balochistan and KP, among others; IHC CJ says matter is sensitive and has constitutional implications.
text: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday decided to form a larger bench to hear a petition against the PTI’s planned Sept 27 protest, terming the matter sensitive and observing that it could have constitutional implications. The IHC also issued notices to the police chiefs of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Balochistan, among other officials, seeking their attendance at the next hearing on Sept 10. The PTI has announced a nationwide protest on Sept 27 to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move in the IHC on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital. Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfaraz Dogar took up the plea on Tuesday, with the petitioner’s lawyer, Akhter Cheena, informing the court that his client was a trader in Islamabad and would be “directly affected” by the planned protest. When the IHC CJ asked how the petitioner would be affected, the lawyer replied that the protest had been announced by KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who planned to lead the demonstration in Islamabad. This could disrupt businesses and normal life in the capital, he explained. The lawyer also read out newspaper clippings containing statements attributed to the KP CM and argued that several cases against PTI leaders were already pending in courts. “All these cases have to be decided according to law,” the lawyer stressed, arguing that if pressure through street protests was accepted as a means of obtaining relief in one case, people across the country with cases pending in court could use the same means. He also voiced concerns about the possibility of an attack on Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail — where Imran is incarcerated — asking whether a plan similar to the May 9, 2023 attack at the General Headquarters in Rawalpindi could be carried out. Terming the planned protest “illegal”, he recalled the November 2024 protest by the PTI. November 26 protests , as they famously came to be known as, saw more than 10,000 PTI protesters surge into Islamabad, defying a ban on public gatherings and a lockdown to skirmish with 20,000 security forces enlisted to turn them back. A day of clashes between security forces and protesters in the city’s Red Zone had ended in the PTI leadership’s hasty retreat. Lawyer Cheena noted that casualties were also reported in the incident. He said three Rangers personnel had lost their lives and questioned how that happened if the claims that the protesters were unarmed were true. Citing media reports, he said the protest caused losses of around Rs240 million. He argued that political pressure “should not be used to get judicial relief”. “The only purpose [of the Sept 27 protest] is to exert pressure and obtain relief,” the counsel alleged. The lawyer contended that the Constitution allowed the government to impose “lawful restrictions” on protests. He referred to the legal framework governing protests in Islamabad and questioned whether the protesters would enter the federal capital on Sept 27 with government machinery with them. At that, CJ Dogar repeated the question, asking whether the protesters would have the KP government’s machinery. The counsel claimed that they would and produced before the court a letter dated Nov 21, 2024, issued by the Ministry of Interior. He argued that despite the federal government’s communication, government machinery had allegedly been used during the 2024 protest. The lawyer further claimed that, so far, no application had been submitted before the Islamabad district magistrate, seeking permission for the planned protest. He further contended that Imran was a convicted prisoner and that two cases concerning him were pending before the IHC. He also read out the orders passed in the £190m Al-Qadir Trust case and argued that the court had repeatedly asked Imran’s counsel to advance arguments on the appeal against his conviction, but arguments had not been concluded. “This is his position in a legal matter before this court,” the counsel said. He then questioned whether the government could direct a court to suspend a sentence in an appeal merely because two million people came out in support of the convict. “Can the government direct the court to suspend the sentence in an appeal? Is this possible?” the counsel asked and asserted that the Constitution clearly provided for the independence of the judiciary. Referring to political developments in other provinces, the counsel said a march had also taken place in Sindh, and KP authorities had announced that facilities would be provided to the protesters. He again argued that the courts could issue guidelines regarding protests, but such arrangements could not be used to provide relief to individuals facing criminal cases. After hearing the initial arguments, CJ Dogar observed that the matter was sensitive and had constitutional implications. Subsequently, the court decided to constitute a larger bench to hear the petition, comprising CJ Dogar, Justice Muhammad Azam Khan and Justice Muhammad Asif. It also issued notices to the relevant parties, including the attorney general for Pakistan; chief secretaries and inspectors general (IG) of KP, Punjab and Balochistan; as well as the chief commissioner, deputy commissioner and IG of Islamabad. The court summoned these officials in their personal capacity. Notices were also issued to the advocates general of KP, Punjab and Balochistan, along with the Islamabad prosecutor general.

title: Houthi attacks disrupt Saudi energy facilities, wound 73, authorities say
author: Reuters | News Desk
description: Riyadh condemns targeting of civilian and economic sites, which resulted in fires; flare-up follows Yemeni govt's offensive against Houthis; PM Shehbaz condemns attack.
text: Operations at some energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, were halted on Tuesday following attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels that wounded 73 people, in what Saudi authorities described as a dangerous escalation. Saudi Arabia’s foreign ministry strongly condemned the “terrorist Houthi militia’s targeting of civilian and economic” sites in the southern cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan, and Najran. The ministry said the attacks resulted in 73 civilians being injured, including women and children. Fires erupted at the sites and several people were injured as firefighting and other emergency teams rushed to contain the blazes and assess the damage, the Saudi energy ministry said. It added that the authorities concerned were dealing with the repercussions of the attacks. “The needed measures will be taken to ensure the safety of the facilities and workers and the continuation of work according to the approved operational plans,” said the ministry. The Saudi foreign ministry said Riyadh would “take all necessary measures to defend its sovereignty”. It also called for an “immediate halt to all forms of escalation practised by this militia”, as well as Houthi attacks on shipping. The flare-up in violence between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis came as tensions mounted between the United States and Iran as the wider Middle East conflict sent oil prices soaring with diplomatic negotiations stalling. Brent crude futures rose $1 to $98 per barrel after the Saudi energy ministry statement, while US crude futures rose over $2 to $93.65 per barrel. On Monday, the Financial Times said Aramco’s Jazan oil facilities were hit in new strikes, and the damage was being assessed. Reuters was not immediately able to verify the report and Aramco has not commented. The Houthi military spokesperson said the group will announce in the coming hours a broad operation deep into Saudi territory. Spokesperson Yahya Saree said on Monday that Riyadh had taken “escalatory steps” by conducting airstrikes on Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition did not announce any recent strikes on Yemen, but the Yemeni government has in recent days mounted an offensive on multiple fronts against the Houthis in Yemen. The coalition vowed to respond firmly to the latest outbreak of hostilities , saying the latest escalation against the de facto Opec leader was “dangerous”. “The coalition will take all necessary operational measures to deter this terrorist militia and resolutely confront its hostile approach,” Colonel Turki al-Malki said in a statement on X. The Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have been launching attacks towards Saudi Arabia since they declared a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting its vessels in the Red Sea. After the latest attack, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif issued a condemnation and expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia. “I condemn in the strongest terms the cowardly attack by Houthis targeting civilian and energy facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, which have left many people injured,” he posted on X. The premier added that Pakistan stood in “unwavering solidarity” with the leadership and people of Saudi Arabia. “Such dastardly attacks threaten innocent lives as well as regional peace and security. We reaffirm our steadfast support for the kingdom’s sovereignty, security and territorial integrity, and pray for the swift recovery of all those injured,” he concluded. Meanwhile, the Foreign Office issued a statement condemning, in the strongest possible terms, the “reprehensible” attacks carried out by the Yemeni Houthis against targets in Saudi Arabia. Terming the attacks “a flagrant violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the kingdom”, the FO added that they threaten peace and stability in the region and undermine efforts to ensure a peaceful and durable resolution of the conflict in Yemen. “Pakistan reiterates its unwavering support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and prosperity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and stands in complete solidarity with the leadership, Government and brotherly people of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the FO said, conveying Pakistan’s wishes for the swift and full recovery of those injured in the attacks. “Consistent with the UN Charter and international law, Pakistan fully supports the kingdom’s legitimate right to take all necessary measures to defend its territory, protect its citizens and residents and safeguard its national assets against any threat,” the statement read. “Pakistan has been and will continue to make all efforts for achieving lasting peace and stability in the region.” Pakistan had condemned previous Houthis’ threats to Saudi Arabia and to trading with the kingdom via the Red Sea. It also warned that it had the right to self-defence if its “maritime interests” were targeted in “any hostile act”. In late July, Saudi Arabia unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, had voiced support for the coalition. Last month, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye also signed a joint defence agreement under which an attack against one of them would be treated as an attack against all of them. The Yemeni threat to shipping and Saudi oil facilities comes in parallel with Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz , which has become the central flashpoint between Tehran and Washington amid efforts to end the Middle East war begun by the US and Israel in February.

title: Fire erupts at Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab's office located in historic KMC building
author: Imtiaz Ali | Imran Ayub
description: Officials say the fire erupted in the outer unit of an air conditioner, no casualties reported in incident.
text: KARACHI: A fire broke out in an air conditioner’s outer unit at Mayor Murtaza Wahab’s office on the first floor of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) building on Tuesday, officials said. South Deputy Inspector General Asad Raza told Dawn that it was a “minor fire”. There were no casualties, and fire tenders dispatched to the site brought the fire under control, Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaanul Haseeb Khan said. Mayor Wahab, speaking to the media outside his damaged office, said a “spark occurred at around 9:15am”. “Whether it was a short circuit or something related to the AC, all aspects are being looked into,” he added, noting that wooden objects and a false ceiling further aggravated the fire. “There was no loss of life. The furniture in the room was damaged, but because of the timely action, my chamber, which is adjacent to the room, was protected, and the conference room was also kept safe,” Wahab said. “My room has been completely gutted by the fire, and all the furniture has been destroyed,” he added, clarifying that there were no records or files in his room. “Files only come to me for signatures; I sign and pass orders on them, after which they are sent to the relevant department. If there are any files with me at all, they are only those on which my signature is pending,” he said. The mayor highlighted that the KMC staff immediately called the fire brigade and the fire team succeeded in confining the blaze to his room. “Once the area has been cleared, our fire team will properly inspect it, and whatever details emerge will be shared with you,” he said. “If anyone thinks that I will stop working or will not come to the office, that is not the case. I have come to the office today and will continue working from another room. I will also continue making my field visits as usual,” the mayor affirmed. Wahab further said that another fire had broken out at Kareem Plaza this morning, where the rescue team took timely action to extinguish the fire. Fires frequently erupt in buildings across Pakistan due to a mix of poor infrastructure, weak enforcement of safety regulations, and widespread negligence. Many structures lack proper fire exits, alarms, and emergency protocols, while faulty wiring and overloaded power systems increase the risk of electrical short circuits. In Karachi, at least three people suffered minor injuries from smoke inhalation after a huge fire erupted in a factory at the Karachi Export Processing Zone (EPZ), near Landhi Industrial Area on Monday. The blaze destroyed half of the three-storey unit and badly damaged other factories. Another massive fire had broken out at the city’s Gul Plaza shopping mall on the night of Jan 17 and claimed at least 73 lives . The blaze took nearly two days to be fully extinguished and left over 1,100 shops in ruins. In early February, a massive fire in a plastic factory at Landhi EPZ engulfed several nearby factories, and it took 13 hours of efforts to bring it under control. Days later, a fire erupted in a high-rise building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony on Feb 12, with around 150 people evacuated . On Feb 17, a fire had also erupted at a chemical factory in the SITE Industrial Area. The next month, a blaze that broke out in Imtiaz Superstore’s Zamzama branch was brought under control after hours-long efforts by rescue officials. In June, hundreds of people were evacuated as a fire erupted in the cold storage of a department store situated in a mega shopping mall on Rashid Minhas Road in Federal B Area.

title: Why has oil stayed below $100 a barrel despite supply disruptions amid US-Iran escalation?
author: Reuters
description: Gulf producers have found alternative routes and are expected to continue sending cargoes for ship-to-ship transfers outside of Hormuz; non-Opec producers set to increase output.
text: Global oil benchmark Brent crude has rallied this month but stayed below $100 a barrel despite recent escalation in the US-Iran conflict that has disrupted Gulf exports from the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Crude oil shipments from Middle East producers are at about 11 million barrels per day (bpd) now, from 18m bpd before the US-Israeli war on Iran began seven months ago, according to Argus. Here are some of the factors driving oil prices: In the week before fighting erupted again on August 30, roughly 8m to 9m bpd had been flowing through Hormuz, double the previous week’s volume, said Rystad Energy’s Chief Economist Claudio Galimberti. While flows have since fallen to below 2m bpd, the daily moving average is still around 4m to 5m barrels, which puts Brent at a “fair” price of $95, Galimberti said. Industry estimates put daily exports between 6m and 8m barrels. There has been no visible very large crude carrier exiting the strait since September 2, Kpler data showed on Monday. During the interim US-Iran peace deal in July, Hormuz exports touched pre-war levels of 16m bpd. Gulf producers have found alternative routes and are expected to continue sending cargoes for ship-to-ship transfers outside of Hormuz, mitigating some of the earlier shortfall. Saudi Aramco resumed loadings from its Ras Tanura port inside the Gulf in August, although its exports from Yanbu in the Red Sea remain under pressure from a naval blockade by the Yemeni Houthis. Yanbu exports hit a six-month low of 1.43m bpd in August, from an average of 3.9m bpd in the previous three months, provisional Kpler data showed. Exports from the alternative port of Egypt’s Sidi Kerir hit 2.14m bpd in August, more than double June volumes. Exports from No.2 Opec producer Iraq rebounded in August to around 2.34m bpd. Shipments from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) hovered around 2.9m bpd in August and July after hitting a record in June, Kpler data showed. Kuwaiti crude exports have recovered to about 1m bpd in July and August. However, Iran’s oil exports have fallen sharply due to the US blockade. Non-Opec producers, including the US, Canada and Guyana, are set to increase output by a combined 1.4m bpd this year, according to Jarand Rystad, founder of Rystad Energy, partly filling the shortfall. Meanwhile, Russian crude exports held steady at about 5.5m bpd in July and August, down from the 6.4m bpd peak in June, but still 23 per cent higher than February as processing at Russian refineries has fallen due to damage to Russian plants from Ukrainian attacks, Kpler data showed. However, Russia has downgraded its 2026 oil output forecast to a 17-year low, which may reduce its exports. Demand destruction in petrochemicals and transportation fuels remains significant in the third quarter at 3.5m bpd, versus 4.5m bpd in the second quarter, with China accounting for more than half of that due to rising transport electrification and coal-based chemicals, Rystad said. Top importer China, dubbed the “new demand Opec” for its market influence, slashed seaborne crude shipments to 7m bpd in July and August, from over 11m bpd in February. Beijing’s vast reserves, estimated by Kpler at 1.17 billion barrels, have also given markets comfort. Spot premiums have rebounded to April levels with Dubai and Oman at $19 to $20 a barrel above Dubai quotes for cargoes loading in November, Reuters data showed. Oman futures were at $104.54 a barrel on Monday while cash Dubai traded at $105.10 a barrel. “At the moment, it’s telling us that physically things are incredibly tight,” said David Fyfe, chief economist at Argus. “We’ve already got prices substantially above $100 a barrel and even more important, you’ve got a diesel market that is screaming shortage.” The recent US-Iran escalation is expected to curb Gulf exports while demand rises as refiners ramp output of diesel, which has hit a record high price in the US. Several banks have raised their Brent price forecasts, including Morgan Stanley which expects prices averaging $100 a barrel in the fourth quarter. Goldman Sachs raised its Brent and West Texas Intermediate forecasts by $5 a barrel for December 2026 and 2027, citing an expectation that Middle East shipping disruptions will persist into next year. It now forecasts Brent at $85 a barrel and WTI at $80 for December 2026, and 2027 prices at $80 and $75 a barrel, respectively.

title: Azma Bokhari defends CM Maryam over terrorism remarks
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
description: “Maryam Nawaz is referring to terrorists who do not remain confined to one province and eventually move towards Punjab. What exactly is objectionable about that?” she asks.
text: LAHORE: Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari on Monday defended Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz after her remarks about terrorism triggered a political storm, saying the critics were deliberately giving the issue a “provincial and ethnic colour”. The controversy erupted after Ms Nawaz while discussing security concerns last week said “the unfortunate thing is that the threat Punjab faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces.” Her remarks drew sharp criticism particularly from political leaders in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa where successive governments and residents have long complained of bearing the brunt of Pakistan’s decades-long war against militancy. Responding to the backlash in a video statement, Ms Bokhari insisted that the chief minister had merely highlighted the movement of militants across provincial boundaries and had not targeted any ethnic community. “Maryam Nawaz was referring to terrorists who do not remain confined to one province and eventually move towards Punjab. What exactly is objectionable about that?” she asked. Bokhari said terrorists operating in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa including groups she described as being backed by India posed a security threat to the entire country. “The Punjab government has revamped its Counter-Terrorism Department and that terrorist sleeper cells have been dismantled in the province,” she said and also referred to attacks on police checkpoints in Punjab, saying several police officials had been killed while combating militancy. “Pakistan’s armed forces are fully capable of defending the country against external threats,” she said, adding that India, according to her, was pursuing its objectives through proxies rather than direct confrontation. The minister also hit out at the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government, saying that maintaining law and order was primarily the responsibility of provincial authorities. “You cannot simply hand over a province to the army and the police and then abdicate your own responsibility,” she said and questioned the demand by the KP chief minister for an apology from Ms Nawaz, arguing that the provincial government should instead focus on confronting the growing militant threat. “Terrorist sleeper cells in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa should be eliminated just as they have been dealt with in Punjab,” she said, accusing the province’s leadership of focusing on political confrontation rather than security. Maryam Nawaz’s remarks have become the latest flashpoint in the increasingly bitter political confrontation between the Punjab government and the PTI-backed administration in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. title: Lahore Development Authority begins digital monitoring of action against illegal constructions
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
description: The new standard operating procedures aim at bringing greater transparency and accountability to field operations, officials says.
text: LAHORE: The Lahore Development Authority (LDA) claims to have revamped its enforcement and inspection regime, introducing digital monitoring of action against illegal constructions, unauthorised commercial use of properties, violations of land-use regulations and non-payment of dues. The new standard operating procedures (SOPs) aim at bringing greater transparency and accountability to field operations, officials said. Under the new system, notices, sealing and demolition proceedings will be processed through a digital file-management mechanism. Notices will carry QR codes, while geo-tagged photographs and other relevant records will be uploaded and monitored online. Properties facing enforcement action have been divided into three categories — illegal construction, unauthorised change in the use of an existing building and non-payment of dues. The authority has also introduced digital record of de-sealing proceedings. A sealed property will only be de-sealed after payment of the applicable fine, restoration of the property to its lawful status, or approval from the competent authority. The new SOPs also spell out the powers and responsibilities of assistant directors, deputy directors and directors of town planning. All zones of the Town Planning Wing will be required to inform the relevant chief town planner before undertaking sealing or demolition operations. A committee headed by the chief town planner has been constituted to scrutinise cases involving illegal commercial properties. The committee will comprise the chief IT officer, and directors of revenue, law and town planning. The committee will decide matters relating to the declaration of a property as illegally commercialised, issuance of notices and their withdrawal or correction, as well as subsequent enforcement action. “The committee will examine the complete planning, legal and revenue position of each property before reaching a decision. It will scrutinise the approved or unapproved building plans, temporary and permanent commercialisation and their legal status,” explained LDA Director General Tahir Farooq in a meeting held here on Monday. The complaints, inspection reports, court stay orders and injunctions concerning a property will also be taken into consideration, he said. Any previous approval, exemption, composition or regularisation granted by a competent authority will likewise be examined. The committee will also verify outstanding dues, fines, revenue records, digital data and site-related information. Its decisions, along with supporting documents, will be uploaded to the digital system. Any subsequent correction or modification will have to be made through the system’s audit trail, making the process traceable. Under the revised SOPs, property owners will be given 15 days to address unauthorised commercial use and five days in cases involving illegal construction before enforcement action is taken. The LDA has warned that negligence or non-compliance with the new procedures will invite departmental action against the officials concerned. Published in Dawn, September 8th, 2026

title: Iran threatens US Gulf energy infrastructure following clashes
author: Agencies
description: Warns Seoul against "involvement in Hormuz".
text: DUBAI/TEHRAN: Iran threatened on Monday to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets, warning that energy infrastructure across the Gulf, including US oil and gas interests, was vulnerable. “Strike our assets and you get struck,” Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said after US and Iranian strikes on shipping at the weekend that pushed oil prices up near six-week highs on Monday. The latest threat underscores the risks of further escalation after the sides traded blows again at the weekend, with no sign of progress towards a diplomatic breakthrough that could end more than six months of conflict and restore normal energy flows through the Gulf. Iran has tightened restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz , a critical artery for global oil and gas supplies, since the war began with US and Israeli strikes on Feb 28. Tehran warns Seoul against ‘involvement in Hormuz’ On Sunday, senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran would soon announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf and unveil a new shipping corridor through the strait. Rezaei said the zone would begin where a US naval blockade of Iran starts and extend into parts of the Gulf. Any vessel entering the area would be placed on an Iranian sanctions list. “We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they (the Americans) stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran,” Rezaei said. Qalibaf later reinforced Tehran’s warning in what appeared to be a response to US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who had described Iran’s oil tanker fleet as “defenceless”. “It’s simple: the oil and gas production chain here is sprawling, accessible, and exposed. American oil and gas companies across these waters and facilities share that exposure,” Qalibaf, who is Iran’s top negotiator, wrote on X. US President Donald Trump has yet to achieve the aims he set out when he launched “Operation Epic Fury” in February: to end Iran’s nuclear programme, halt its ability to attack its neighbours and create conditions for Iranians to topple their leadership. Tehran’s clerical rulers remain in power and aim to emerge from the war stronger than before. They continue to demand sanctions relief and hope eventually to collect fees from ships using the strait, which carried a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before the war. After a relative lull through much of August, hostilities have intensified again following the collapse of an interim ceasefire reached in June. Diplomatic efforts have made little headway. On Saturday, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island, Iran’s main oil export hub, according to US Central Command. The attacks followed strikes by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on US warships operating in the region. Tehran has demonstrated it can still attack US interests in neighbouring countries and disrupt oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Shipping data showed an average of just 10 commodity vessels per day transited the strait over the past 10 days, the lowest level since May. Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday warned South Korea against military deployment or involvement in US operations in the Strait of Hormuz, saying such a move would have “serious consequences”. On Friday, Seoul said it was considering “contributions” to US security efforts in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has largely controlled since the outbreak of war against the United States on Feb 28. South Korea said it would consider the move provided that its own military readiness was not compromised, but added that no decision had been made. On Monday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei warned South Korea against succumbing to what he called “US pressure and intimidation”. “Any military deployment or participation in operations by other countries in the Persian Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz can only be regarded as direct support for the party responsible for that aggression and will have serious consequences,” he said in a post on X. Iran and the United States have continued to trade fire in and around the Strait of Hormuz, even after an April ceasefire brought the initial intense bombardment campaign to an end. Negotiations between the two foes have stalled as they vied for control over Hormuz, which normally carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas exports. Since the war erupted, traffic through the vital waterway has been virtually paralysed, disrupting global energy markets. Iran has required vessels to seek permission to transit — a move opposed by Washington and several regional countries — insisting that there will be no return to the pre-war system of unrestricted navigation. title: Punjab Environment Protection launches real-time air quality dashboard
author: Imran Gabol
description: New system to track pollution hotspots and forecast air quality.
text: LAHORE: The Punjab Environment Protection and Climate Change Depa­rt­ment (EP&CCD) has launched new forecasting and satellite-based features for the province’s real-time air quality dashboard. The EP&CCD unveiled the new features in collaboration with the Inter­national Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) on the Interna­tional Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies. The AQI Punjab Dashboard is the first platform of its kind in Pakistan to receive international recognition from ICIMOD. The platform is fed data from 59 state-of-the-art air quality monitoring stations (AQMS) installed across Punjab and provides real-time air quality information aut­omatically, without human intervention. With the new integration, the dashboard will combine data from ground monitoring stations, satellites, weather information and air pollution forecasting systems. This will help the EP&CCD better understand the sources of pollution, identify pollution hotspots and predict how air quality may change in the coming hours and days across Punjab. New system to track pollution hotspots and forecast air quality Speaking at the launch, EPA Punjab Director General Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh said significant progress had been made over the past two years in strengthening environmental governance through modern technology, digital monitoring and science-based decision-making. He said the air quality monitoring network had been expanded from just three stations in Lahore in 2024 to 59 state-of-the-art AQMS across Punjab, with plans to further expand the network to 100 stations across the province. He added that monitoring was being complemented by practical measures to reduce pollution, including the deployment of mist cannons to suppress fugitive dust and enhanced sector-wise enforcement against major sources of emissions. He said accurate and timely air quality information was essential for taking effective action against pollution. He added that the new system would help government departments identify areas with high pollution levels, prepare for severe pollution episodes and take timely measures to control emissions. The initiative is expected to improve air pollution monitoring, forecasting, public information and government response, helping authorities take faster and better-informed action to improve air quality across Punjab. The initiative is supported by ICIMOD’s Himalayan Resilience Enabling Action Programme (HI-REAP), funded by the UK Department for International Deve­lopment through its Climate Action for a Resilient Asia (CARA) initiative. title: Karachi police briefly detain protesting family members of Pakistani sailors held hostage by Somali pirates
author: Shazia Hasan
description: One of the protesters alleges that when they went to the police station where other demonstrators were detained, police "misbehaved" with them.
text: KARACHI: Some of the family members of Pakistani sailors held hostage by Somali pirates aboard the MT Honour 25 for more than four months were briefly detained in the early hours of Monday while they were staging a sit-in near Karachi’s Sharea Faisal. The MT Honour 25, a Palau-flagged oil tanker, was hijacked by armed pirates off the coast of Puntland, Somalia, on April 21. Besides 10 crew members from Pakistan, the hostages include seamen from Indonesia, India and Sri Lanka. During more than four months of their captivity, no significant progress has been reported either in negotiations or in the payment of the ransom, said to be around $3 million, for their recovery. Their families have staged protests for their recovery multiple times. On Sunday, they began an overnight sit-in outside the Foreign Office near Sharea Faisal and planned to march to the Supreme Court registry on Monday morning. But police reached the protest site before that and detained some of them. They were later released, the wife of one of the hostages confirmed to Dawn in the afternoon. “They were taken to the police station and kept there for a long time, and the police were not allowing us to see them. The police misbehaved with us and told us to go away,” said Ayesha Ameen, whose husband, Ameen Bin Shams, was a fitter on the hijacked ship. “They were arrested around 7:45am,” added Ayesha, who was not detained by police. A police official, who requested anonymity, also confirmed that the detained individuals had been released. Dawn also contacted East senior superintendent of police and deputy inspector general, but they did not respond. Earlier, Ayesha recorded a video message at the protest site and said the families had been demanding the recovery of the hostages for four and a half months; however, “no one is listening to us”. She added that the protesters were not blocking any roads or engaged in illegal activity but were merely protesting peacefully. “We came here for the hostages’ release, not to become prisoners ourselves,” she added. Another protester recorded a video inside a vehicle that appeared to be a police van. Police personnel could be seen standing outside the van in the video, in which the maternal uncle of a second engineer on the ship decried the detention of the protesters. “We have been arrested — our women, elders and kids. It is shameful. “Bilawal Bhutto sahib, we did not expect this from you,” Talib Raza said, expressing disappointment. In another video, a woman was also seen inside a vehicle that appeared to be a police van. Meanwhile, another woman could be heard saying, “Look, we are being arrested. This is our government, and this is our police. We are being taken away only because we spoke up for ourselves.” Since the sailors’ hijacking, the crew has also made several emotional videos and audio appeals , while reporting that they have run out of clean water, food and medicine. The last message from them came on August 7, more than 100 days after being taken hostage by Somali pirates. In that video, they appealed directly to the Pakistani government for their release. They appeared to be in a state of extreme distress, with most looking sick and weak. The hostages requested that the Pakistani government talk to the Somali pirates and take steps to release them. The hostages are victims of an “ ownership crisis ” because it is not clear who owns the ship, and the man previously thought to be the owner was later revealed to be more likely a middleman who hired them. Last month, in a meeting with the International Maritime Organisation’s head, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar pressed for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of the Pakistani sailors. Earlier that month, he had also directed “stakeholders” to intensify diplomatic engagement with national and international partners to facilitate the release. The Foreign Office has also maintained that it remains “actively engaged” to secure the release of the seamen.

title: Board of Peace official says Gaza, West Bank escalation makes two-state solution 'impossible'
author: AFP
description: Nickolay Mladenov notes "no credible pathway forward to a political resolution" as over 50pc of Gaza under Israeli control, other parts under Hamas.
text: A top official within the US-backed Board of Peace said on Monday that a failure to move forward in Gaza paired with rising violence in the West Bank are making a two-state solution “impossible”. Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under the US-backed Board of Peace tasked with implementing an October 2025 ceasefire plan , was speaking at the Hili Forum in Abu Dhabi. “I would say that if Gaza continues the way it is now, or does not move into implementing… the plan that we have under the comprehensive plan, the two-state solution will become practically impossible,” he said. “Because, with everything that is happening in the West Bank, and with more than 50 per cent of Gaza now under the control of the Israeli army and less than 50 per cent under the control of Hamas, there is no credible pathway forward to a political resolution of the conflict,” he added. A roadmap agreed by Hamas on July 30 said that the decommissioning of weapons would be supervised by the International Stabilisation Force , the nascent unit that aims to deploy to Gaza if the situation calms. It is led by US Major General Jasper Jeffers. Hamas had pledged to hand over its weapons to a new Palestinian governing body, an arrangement that brought scepticism from Netanyahu but which Trump hailed as a breakthrough. The West Bank has also seen a surge in violence since Israel’s war on the Gaza Strip began following Hamas’s attack on Israel on Oct 7, 2023. More than 500,000 Israelis live in illegal settlements in the Palestinian territory, home to some three million Palestinians. “The only way that we can build back to that is if we have transitional governance, if we have decommissioning of weapons, if we have withdrawal in Gaza,” he said. On Sunday, Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a US envoy, told a press briefing in Kyiv that the upcoming Israeli elections were making Israeli leaders “a little irrational” on Gaza. “We agree with them on the end state,” Kushner said, referring to Israel. “They just have a crazy election and that makes them a little irrational in certain regards, but we’re very determined and we’re working through these things.” “You can’t go in if there’s guns,” he said, adding: “We’re now starting to understand the scope of the militarisation of Gaza. It is beyond your comprehension. And so demilitarising it is not going to be easy.”

title: NCCIA gets journalist Bilal Ghauri's 3-day physical remand in Peca case
author: Malik Asad
description: According to the NCCIA, the journalist disseminated "false narratives" about the recent appointment of the Nacta head.
text: ISLAMABAD: A judicial magistrate in Islamabad on Monday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) three-day physical remand of journalist Bilal Ghauri in a case registered under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). According to the first information report, seen by Dawn , the case was registered on Sept 6 on the state’s behalf through NCCIA Technical Assistant Muhammad Umair Warsi under Section 20 (offences against the dignity of a natural person) and 26-A (dissemination of false and fake information) of Peca. The FIR stated that Ghauri allegedly uploaded and disseminated content concerning the appointment of the National Counter Terrorism Authority’s (Nacta) head on Sept 5. “Prima facie, the material allegedly contained assertions and allegations concerning the process and circumstances relating to the appointment of the Nacta national coordinator,” the FIR stated. It said an inquiry into the matter concluded that Ghauri had “intentionally created, uploaded, transmitted and disseminated the false narratives through social media platforms”. The inquiry also found that the content was “false, misleading and presented without any lawful, factual or independently verifiable basis”, the FIR added. On Monday, Ghauri was produced before Judge Malik Aman, where the NCCIA sought his 10-day remand. Ghauri’s lawyer, Advocate Imran Shafiq, opposed the agency’s request and maintained that his client was arrested without being served any prior notice. He added that the vlog in which Ghauri was said to have made the remarks in question was uploaded on Sept 5, and that he was arrested the same night. He argued that there was not a single statement in the entire vlog that could be termed false or fabricated. Ghauri, too, contended that his remarks were not about an individual, but were about Nacta and the institution’s performance. Advocate Shafiq further argued that Ghauri had merely outlined the contents of a notification issued by the relevant authorities. The counsel questioned the prosecution’s allegation of false information and asked the NCCIA to identify exactly which statement in the vlog was false. After hearing arguments from both sides, the court rejected the NCCIA’s request for 10-day physical remand and instead handed Ghauri over to the agency on three-day remand for further investigation.

title: Hammad Azhar's mother moves LHC for his recovery amid reports of arrest
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
description: Petition claims PTI leader's family has no information on Azhar's whereabouts; seeks directives for him to be presented before court.
text: LAHORE: The mother of Hammad Azhar on Monday filed a habeas corpus petition in the Lahore High Court (LHC) seeking recovery of of the PTI leader from alleged police custody. A day earlier, PTI claimed that Azhar been arrested. While Multan and Lahore police officials said they were unaware of his arrest, party sources claimed the PTI leader was taken into custody in a case pertaining to the May 9, 2023 riots. Monday’s petition was filed by Azhar’s mother, Ishrat Azhar, through Barrister Abuzar Salman Niazi. It named the Punjab inspector general of police (IGP), the Lahore capital city police officer (CCPO), the Lahore deputy inspector general (operations), and the RA Bazaar station house officer (South Cantt) as respondents. The petition alleged that Azhar was arrested two days ago, but his family had no information about his whereabouts. It expressed concerns about his safety and maintained that no person could be kept in illegal detention. The petition requested the LHC to direct the respondents to produce Azhar before the court or any competent court and disclose the complete and lawful basis of his arrest and detention. The petition also sought immediate access for Azhar to his legal counsel and reasonable communication with his family members in accordance with law. The petition asked the court to declare any detention of Azhar that was not in accordance with the Constitution and law as unlawful and without lawful authority. Azhar, who is the son of late former Punjab governor Mian Muhammad Azhar , was wanted by Lahore police in connection with a case regarding an attack on the Govt Officers’ Residences (GOR-I) gate on May 9, 2023. He has been declared a proclaimed offender by multiple anti-terrorism courts for not joining the proceedings against him in cases related to the May 9 riots. Reports of Azhar’s arrest circulated widely on social media over the weekend, with different accounts emerging about where and when he was taken into custody. According to some reports circulating online on Sunday, the PTI leader was handed over to Lahore police. However, Lahore Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Investigations Muhammad Naveed said he had no confirmation about Azhar’s arrest or handover to Lahore police. In a statement on Sunday, the PTI had termed the former finance minister’s arrest “the worst example of political vengeance and fascism”. “Hammad Azhar is being continuously targeted with retaliatory actions on political grounds. The government is recklessly using state power to suppress political opponents and silence the voice of PTI,” it alleged. Azhar had reappeared in public on May 22, 2024, a year after he had gone into hiding when the state launched a crackdown against the party leadership following the violent incidents of May 9 . At the time, the PTI leader had evaded arrest when the Counter-Terrorism Department raided the party’s secretariat in Islamabad. In April 2025, Azhar had stepped down as the president of the party’s Punjab chapter for the third time, after his two previous resignations were rejected .

title: PCB launches internal disciplinary inquiry amid reports about Imam, Rizwan
author: Dawn Sport

text: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Monday confirmed that it had initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following reports “concerning discipline and conduct” as the media alleged that investigations involving former Test players Imamul Haq and Mohammad Rizwan have been widened. In a statement, PCB media director Amir Mir said the board was reviewing matters relating to “discipline and conduct” internally and that the process was being conducted under its regulations. “The PCB has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally,” he said. “The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration,” he added. The statement came after Geo News reported that the PCB had obtained data from the mobile phones of Imam and Rizwan as part of an investigation into their activities and contacts during the team’s stay in London. According to the report, the two players’ phones were taken into possession by the team’s security officer after Pakistan’s 194-run defeat by England in the second Test at Lord’s and were returned several hours later after their data was allegedly transferred elsewhere. The PCB has not confirmed that it took possession of the phones or obtained their data. Similar details have been carried by other outlets, citing reports. The PCB media director on Monday cautioned against treating unverified reports as established fact. “At this stage, any speculative reports or unverified claims circulating on certain platforms, particularly those originating from hostile external sources, should not be regarded as credible,” he said. The PCB declined to provide further details, saying it would not comment further while the process was under way. The development adds another layer to the turmoil surrounding Pakistan’s Test team after the side suffered two heavy defeats against England, resulting in the PCB making sweeping changes ahead of the third and final Test at Edgbaston, beginning on Wednesday. England won the opening Test at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs before inflicting a 194-run defeat on Pakistan at Lord’s to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. The PCB subsequently released seven players, including Imam and Rizwan, from the Test squad and replaced red-ball head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Mike Hesson on an interim basis. Imam’s absence from the Lord’s Test had already become a matter of scrutiny. The opener suffered what was described as a low-grade calf strain while fielding on the first day and did not bat in either innings as Pakistan were dismissed for 110 and 194. Aaqib Javed, a member of the national selection committee and PCB’s high-performance director, subsequently called for an inquiry into the matter . However, the PCB’s latest statement did not name Imam or Rizwan, nor did it disclose the nature of the investigation. It said stakeholders and the public should rely on official PCB communications regarding the matter.

title: Nepal holds day of mourning for victims of devastating floods as families pray missing still alive
author: AFP
description: Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet says rescue efforts continuing “with the same tempo we had on day one”.
text: Nepal held a national day of mourning on Monday for victims of devastating glacial floods, as families of missing hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels prayed rescuers might yet find them alive. The August 26 glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,398 people, with more than 5,500 missing, including around 800 foreigners. Flags flew at half-mast, with candlelight vigils planned later in the day, following traditional Hindu mourning rituals on the 13th day after death. Hundreds of hydropower workers are among the missing, but the rescue of three of them from deep inside tunnels — two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday — have buoyed hopes that more could still be alive. Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP on Monday that rescue efforts were continuing “with the same tempo we had on day one”. “Our focus is on search and rescue at three levels — on ground, by air, and in the tunnels,” he said. “We are making sure that no one is still stranded.” Entire communities have been swept away, roads destroyed, and homes demolished. But families of some of the missing workers who gathered in the capital, Kathmandu, said the government must move faster. “We have a lot of hope,” said Reena Amatya Shrestha, whose brother is among the missing. “They say they are doing rescue. If the rescue is there, where’s the result? We need the result.” Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, said the operation presented an unprecedented challenge. “We are facing something I have never faced before,” said Dix, president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association, in a post on social media. “Not one rescue, but multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties, and lives that may still be saved.” Foreign experts, including from China, India and South Korea, are aiding Nepali teams in rescue efforts. “We are measured not only by the lives we save, but by the lives we refuse to abandon,” said Dix, a key adviser during the Indian rescue of 41 men trapped for 17 days inside the collapsed Silkyara tunnel in Uttarakhand state in 2023. “Silkyara taught me never to confuse unlikely with impossible,” he said. With mortuaries overflowing, Nepal has buried hundreds of bodies in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification, according to police. Only around 100 bodies have been identified and handed over to families. While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melting worldwide, increasing the risk of such disasters. Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, says reconstruction could cost billions of dollars. Its economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale. The disaster has come just ahead of the anniversary of last year’s September 8-9 mass anti-corruption protests that toppled the government, and the young government now faces the enormous task of rebuilding communities and critical infrastructure. A UN preliminary assessment estimated building damage from Nepal’s floods at $158m alone, warning that total losses — including damage to roads and bridges, agricultural land and humanitarian costs — would be far higher. The United Nations has appealed for $50m to help more than 84,000 people. “My plea to the international community is — this is the time to help Nepal,” UN country chief Lila Pieters Yahia told AFP. In Nepal, rescuers have retrieved 1,355 bodies, while around 4,996 people are missing, according to the disaster agency. In China, the toll is 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media.

title: Pakistan rejects India's 'baseless' claims on status of occupied Kashmir
author: News Desk
description: “India’s so-called official maps and unilateral claims of sovereignty have no bearing on the status of the disputed territory,” FO spokesperson says.
text: The Foreign Office (FO) on Monday rejected Indian claims about the status of occupied Kashmir, saying that New Delhi’s “unilateral claims of sovereignty have no bearing on the internationally recognised disputed status of the territory”. The statement came after the United Nations voted on Friday to back a resolution spearheaded by several African countries aimed at “a more accurate representation” of continental landmasses, making their continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe. India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of the resolution. However, the Indian Ministry of External Affairs on Sunday issued a statement , saying that the resolution did not constitute the endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of natural boundaries. It also said that its territory, “including Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh”, must be depicted in accordance with its “official map”, adding that any deviation was “unacceptable”. In the statement issued on Monday, FO Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said: “Pakistan categorically rejects India’s baseless assertions regarding the status of Jammu and Kashmir which are contrary to internationally recognised facts.” “India’s unilateral actions and continued illegal occupation cannot alter the internationally recognised disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir,” he said. He added that the Kashmir issue remained one of the oldest unresolved internationally recognised disputes on the agenda of the United Nations (UN) Security Council. “The relevant UN resolutions stipulate that its final disposition must be made in accordance with the relevant Security Council resolutions and the will of the Kashmiri people, expressed through a free and impartial plebiscite under UN auspices,” he added. “The official UN maps, which depict Jammu and Kashmir as a disputed territory, remain the only cartographic representation of its current legal status,” he said. “India’s so-called official maps and unilateral claims of sovereignty have no bearing on the status of the disputed territory,” the FO spokesperson said. “Pakistan urged the international community to ensure that India immediately stops human rights violations in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, and fulfils its commitment towards the realisation of the right to self-determination of the Kashmiri people, in line with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions,” the FO spokesperson concluded. The UN resolution said the new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, “is a relevant option for improving the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world”. It urged member states to adopt the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection, which was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569. The United States had slammed the resolution, saying such moves are “the reason this institution is losing its credibility”.

Many within the US system realise that dragging the war further is useless; several top American generals have reportedly told their civilian bosses that escalation with Tehran is not advisable.
