title: Traffic bottlenecks on Lahore's Canal Road stretch near Harbanspura irk commuters
author: Khalid Hasnain
description: The issue that has been persisting for years has become a daily ordeal for the commuters, especially during peak hours, with little sign of relief by the authorities concerned.
text: LAHORE: Residents of various housing societies situated on both sides of the Canal Road stretch from Harbanspura onward and adjoining areas, have been facing persistent traffic bottlenecks due to the narrow road and bridge (culvert), as authorities concerned are turning a blind eye to the issue. The issue that has been persisting for years has become a daily ordeal for the commuters, especially during peak hours, with little sign of relief by the authorities concerned. On the other hand, the motorists from other parts of the city, who use this stretch of the Canal Road on a daily basis, have also criticised the government for doing nothing to resolve the critical issue. The road stretch, which also connects various housing colonies with the Canal Road, remains one of the busiest sections in the area. During school and office hours, long queues of vehicles are witnessed on both sides of the canal, leaving residents frustrated and exhausted. “It sometimes takes me half an hour just to get across the bridge,” says Mian Afzal, an area resident. “If there is a minor accident or a vehicle breaks down, the entire traffic clogs and we get stuck for even longer.” Many area residents argue that the situation has gone from bad to worse over the past decade, despite repeated promises from successive governments to resolve. During its previous tenure, the PML-N government in Punjab had approved a plan to widen the road stretch and construct U-turns from the Dharampura underpass to Jallo Morr on the Canal Road. The scheme was meant to ease traffic congestion and provide relief to thousands of daily commuters. The government also built the Beijing Underpass to ease constant traffic congestion at the Chaubacha railway crossings outside the Royal Palm Golf and Country Club. The Canal Road had been widened up to the Harbanspura police station. However, following the 2018 elections, when the PTI formed its government in Punjab, the project was shelved along with several other initiatives launched by the outgoing PML-N administration. Residents say that since then, their pleas have gone unheard. They say the section of the Canal Road from Harbanspura to Jallo Mor becomes a bottleneck, especially for the traffic coming from the Mall Road side. The PML-N’s return to power in Punjab after the 2024 elections raised hopes that the project would finally be revived. But the government has cited financial constraints, stating that funds are being spent on other development schemes, which are a priority. The affected residents, however, believe that political neglect is at the heart of the issue. “There’s no shortage of funds when it comes to building roads in elite housing societies or model towns,” says Syed Asif Ahmad, a daily commuter. “But when it comes to the housing societies along this particular stretch, the excuse of limited resources is always put forward.” The gravity of the situation can be measured by the fact that police squad vehicles remain deployed at the small bridges near Sahafi Colony and other neighbouring societies to ensure the smooth passage of the VIPs. “If traffic has to be controlled every day for the VIPs, you just imagine what the common people go through here without such arrangements,” a resident remarks. Shopkeepers and small traders along the stretch also complain that the chronic traffic mess has hurt business activity. Customers avoid stopping near such colonies due to traffic congestion, while delivery vehicles face frequent delays. “The entire commercial activity in this belt is slowing down because of the road problem,” says Farhan Aziz, who runs a general store in the area. Civil society activists argue that the expansion of this section of the Canal Road is no longer a matter of convenience but a necessity. With a growing population in the Harbanspura area, including the Lahore Press Club Housing Scheme (known as Sahafi Colony), Hajvery Housing Scheme and Lahore Medical and Dental College Housing Scheme, the pressure on the narrow bridge has far exceeded its capacity. Residents have urged the Punjab government to immediately revive and execute the stalled project, warning that further delay will only worsen the situation. title: Iran warns of 'more painful response' if US launches further attacks
author: AFP
description: Ghalibaf's remarks come after US military claimed to have hit three oil tankers linked to Iran.
text: Iran’s top negotiator on Sunday threatened a more forceful response to any further US attacks after Tehran targeted American warships in their latest round of clashes. The exchanges of fire, which began with US raids last week, come amid a deadlock in the six-month war between the two foes. Iran has maintained its stranglehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz while Washington continues a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Washington is also seeking to choke Iran’s economy, rolling out sanctions on entities with financial links to the country in a bid to force it into submission. “The Americans must have understood that the era of proportionate responses has come to an end,” said Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has acted as chief negotiator in talks to end the war. “Any aggression against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, more intense and more painful response,” he added, in a speech carried by state media. On Saturday, US Central Command (Centcom), which oversees American military operations in the region, said Iran had unsuccessfully fired at two American warships — an aircraft carrier and a destroyer. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said the warships had been “forced to retreat” after “suffering damage”, but Centcom said they successfully evaded the attacks. In response, the US military said it struck three oil tankers linked to the Iranian Guards. Centcom said it had “permanently disabled” one ship off the coast of the oil hub of Kharg Island and another near Jask, and “completely destroyed” a third vessel in the Gulf of Oman. Video posted by the military showed large fireballs and billowing flames after projectiles slammed into the ships. The three vessels were “part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies”, Centcom said. Iran quickly retaliated, with the Guards saying their naval forces “targeted three oil tankers on the unauthorised route of the Strait of Hormuz and three vessels affiliated with the child-killing America in other areas”. It warned ships not to attempt to transit the key trade waterway via routes unapproved by Tehran. Early on Sunday, Iran’s IRGC also said it attacked a US naval drone trying to enter the strait, according to a statement carried by state television. Centcom spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins, however, called the claim “a complete lie”. “No US vessels have been attacked today,” he said. Centcom commander Admiral Brad Cooper had said after the exchange of strikes: “If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours.” The Iranian foreign ministry condemned the attacks on its oil tankers as “illegal and aggressive actions”. The administration of US President Donald Trump has tried to downplay the significance of the six-month conflict, which has proven increasingly unpopular at home as midterm elections near. US Vice President JD Vance has gone so far as to say that he “wouldn’t call it a war”. Trump reiterated that view on Friday, calling the war “small potatoes” for Washington. Iranian officials have so far maintained their defiant tone, but US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ABC ’s “This Week” programme on Sunday that Iran was “doing everything they can to cling on to something”. “They know their nuclear programme’s coming to an end. Their navy has come to an end. Their air force has come to an end. They’re clinging on to power,” he said. A fragile ceasefire between the two sides collapsed in July after attacks on commercial ships in the Hormuz strait, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed. Trump has in recent weeks repeatedly threatened to claim sovereignty over the strait, even posting a map showing it as “new US territory”. Vance has insisted the US will not reopen talks with Iran until it ends attacks on commercial shipping in the strait.

title: NA speaker's ruling on employee records cannot restrict citizen's right to information, PIC rules
author: Ikram Junaidi
description: Pakistan Information Commission decides two appeals filed by journalist Saddia Mazhar against the NA Secretariat.
text: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) has ruled that the National Assembly speaker’s decision to classify certain records cannot restrict citizens’ right to information (RTI) unless the ruling gives reasons showing that the harm from disclosure outweighs the public interest. The PIC issued the ruling while deciding two appeals filed by journalist Saddia Mazhar against the NA Secretariat. One of the appeals sought information about officers who had joined the NA Secretariat on deputation from January 2018 onwards, including their parent departments, grades, appointment dates, promotions and records relating to their induction into the secretariat. The NA Secretariat had argued that minutes of meetings, official file notes and recommendations relating to the employees had been classified under the speaker’s ruling of Oct 4, 2022, issued under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, 2007 . The speaker’s ruling had declared various records, including committee minutes, briefing material, working papers and certain personal records of employees, as classified for the purposes of the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017 . The PIC held that the speaker, being the head of the National Assembly Secretariat, could exercise the powers under Section 7(f) of the Right of Access to Information Act, despite the provision specifically referring to the minister-in-charge of a public body. However, the PIC stressed that such power was subject to the statutory requirements of the law. “[The] ruling does not contain reasons as to why the harm from disclosure of information outweighs the public interest,” the PIC observed, concluding that it therefore could not operate to classify the records. It further held that the speaker’s ruling was neither prospectively nor retrospectively operative because it failed to meet the legal criteria required for classification under Section 7(f) of the Act. Regarding the employees’ records sought by the applicant, it noted that appointment and promotion notifications were already published in the official Gazette. It therefore found no legal basis for withholding the information. The PIC also dismissed the secretariat’s preliminary objections regarding the non-provision of a copy of the applicant’s computerised national identity card (CNIC) and her non-appearance in person, declaring both grounds legally unsustainable under the Act. It noted that information already published in the official Gazette or otherwise publicly accessible cannot be withheld. The commission directed the NA’s deputy secretary, or a designated officer, to provide the applicant with a specific link to information available on the secretariat’s website and furnish certified copies of the remaining requested information, including Gazette-notified records, within 10 days of receiving the order. The ruling also emphasised that the 2017 RTI Act takes precedence over inconsistent provisions contained in other laws under Section 25 of the Act. In a 2025 policy brief, the Free and Fair Election Network (Fafen) noted that the RTI regime in Pakistan was stifled by institutional inertia and deep-rooted secrecy norms despite advanced legal provisions. It had called for comprehensive legal reforms to strengthen the implementation of the RTI law.

title: Germany's far-right AfD emerges as landslide winner in eastern state vote
author: AFP
description: A first-ever AfD state govt would be a shock for many in Germany, which has been at pains to atone for its history of World War II and the Holocaust.
text: Germany’s far-right AfD won a landslide victory in a key regional election Sunday in the ex-communist east, taking at least 44 per cent of the vote according to exit polls by two public broadcasters. “We have made history today,” said a jubilant Ulrich Siegmund, the 35-year-old lead candidate of the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in Saxony-Anhalt state. It was, however, too early to tell whether the AfD will have enough votes for an absolute majority that would allow it to govern a state alone for the first time. The centre-right CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz came a distant second, winning around 18.5pc, according to exit polls by broadcasters ARD and ZDF . Depending on the eventual count, the CDU’s state premier Sven Schulze would hope to still be able to form a new multi-party coalition to block the AfD from power. All major parties have so far maintained a “firewall” of non-cooperation with the Moscow-friendly AfD, whose state branch is categorised as “right-wing extremist” by Germany’s domestic intelligence agency. A first-ever AfD state government would be a shock for many in Germany, which has been at pains to atone for its dark history of World War II and the Holocaust and so far kept extremist parties at bay. The spectre of a far-right state government drew thousands of the AfD’s opponents to a rally on Saturday in Magdeburg, the regional capital, with banners saying “life is better without Nazis”. “I’m very worried,” demonstrator Laura Saalfeld told AFP . “Whatever the results, the atmosphere will change. Far-right sympathisers will show themselves more openly on the streets.” Siegmund, the AfD’s telegenic top candidate, has ambitions to lead a political revolution from Saxony-Anhalt that would propel the party to national victory in 2029. On the campaign trail, Siegmund — a former entrepreneur with a sharp undercut hairstyle and a huge social media following — has been mobbed by adoring fans, many wearing T-shirts bearing his likeness. The party has tapped into a sense of nostalgia for communist East Germany as well as lingering resentment about an enduring wealth gap with the west decades after the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall. In line with the sometimes defiant sense of local “Ossie pride”, Siegmund has often ridden the iconic local Simson bike, including to the polling booth on Sunday in his hometown of Tangermünde. While Siegmund has been dubbed the friendly face of the AfD, his campaign promises have been radical, including targeting irregular migrants with a “remigration and deportation offensive” from day one. The party’s anti-“woke” agenda also includes vows to replace LGBTQ pride rainbow flags at public schools with the German standard, and to change history teaching to lessen the emphasis on the Third Reich. In order to replace migrant workers, the AfD wants to lure back German expatriates, while offering “baby bonuses” for families to reverse the shrinking of the population in the small state of 2.1 million people. The German Economic Institute has warned the AfD’s immigration policy would be “ruinous” for Saxony-Anhalt, which is highly reliant on foreign-born workers, especially in the health sector. Others have voiced fears that an AfD-run state security apparatus could leak sensitive information to Russia, which Moscow could use to destabilise Germany. The Kremlin “makes no secret of the fact that the AfD is the most important instrument for destabilising Germany for (Russian President Vladimir) Putin”, Thuringia state interior minister Georg Maier told the Handelsblatt daily. The strong AfD win also heaps pressure on Merz , who has vowed to reboot a stagnant economy and restrict irregular immigration, but has seen his party beaten by the AfD in national surveys too. Political scientist Wolfgang Schroeder of Kassel University said that after an AfD win in Saxony-Anhalt, “Merz’s critics will become even more vocal, and calls for better leadership will become impossible to ignore”.

title: PTI claims Hammad Azhar arrested in Punjab
author: Imran Gabol
description: Lahore, Multan police deny arrest; PTI insists former minister is "being continuously targeted with retaliatory actions on political grounds".
text: The PTI on Sunday claimed that its leader Hammad Azhar has been arrested, denouncing the action as “political vengeance”. title: FO condemns mosque demolition in India's Uttar Pradesh, terms it part of 'drive to erase Islamic heritage'
author: News Desk
description: Calls on international community to take note of India's continued desecration and destruction of places of worship "under state patronage".
text: Pakistan on Sunday condemned the demolition of a century-old mosque in India’s Uttar Pradesh, describing it as part of an “Islamophobic and Hindutva-driven campaign to erase the Islamic heritage” in the country. Responding to media queries regarding the demolition, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan condemned the move and described it as “a reprehensible action against a historic Islamic place of worship”. He recalled that the demolition of the Babri Mosque in 1992 was an “enduring symbol of this ideology of religious intolerance, prejudice and hatred”. “Pakistan calls upon the international community to take immediate cognisance of the systematic persecution of Muslims by Indian authorities,” the statement said, highlighting the “continued desecration and destruction of their places of worship under state patronage”. Khan called for accountability of Indian authorities for actions against the religious freedom and cultural heritage of all minorities, particularly Muslims. According to The Indian Express , the mosque, which was located inside a Collectorate in Saharanpur, was demolished a day earlier. The demolition came three days after a district court had dismissed an appeal against an order holding that the structure stood on government land and was unauthorised. The September 2 order did not itself mention demolition. The Indian Express quoted mosque staff member Tanveer Ahmed as saying that the order was for eviction, not demolition. He claimed the mosque was around 150 years old, and maintained that the land was recorded in their names. All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen president and Hyderabad lawmaker Asaduddin Owaisi condemned the demolition and questioned whether the constitutional guarantee of freedom of religion applied to Muslims, NDTV reported. According to Owaisi, the mosque dated back to 1911, claiming that the Collectorate itself was constructed later. In 2024, the Akhonji mosque, which was over 600 years old, was razed to the ground without any prior notice in Delhi’s Mehrauli district. In 1992, a Hindu mob destroyed the famous Babri mosque, triggering riots that killed about 2,000 people across India, most of them Muslims.

title: Pakistan dispatches humanitarian aid to Nepal after deadly floods, landslides
author: News Desk | AFP
description: Nepal rescuers face challenging conditions as search operations enter 12th day.
text: Pakistan on Sunday dispatched 100 tonnes of humanitarian assistance to Nepal to support relief efforts following the recent deadly floods and landslides. The glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,384 people and left more than 5,500 missing across the two countries. In Nepal, rescuers have retrieved 1,341 bodies, while around 4,996 people remain missing. The humanitarian aid from Pakistan was coordinated by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and sent by a chartered flight from Islamabad to Kathmandu, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement. “The relief consignment comprised tents, blankets, mats, hygiene kits and medicines for the affected communities,” FO said. The send-off ceremony for the humanitarian assistance was held at the Islamabad airport, and was attended by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Nepal’s Ambassador Rita Dhital, along with senior FO and NDMA officials. “The assistance reflects Pakistan’s solidarity with the government and people of Nepal during this difficult time,” FO noted. Sharing the development on X, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said: “Our thoughts and prayers are with the bereaved families and all those affected. Pakistan stands in solidarity with the Government and people of Nepal and remains ready to extend all possible support in this difficult hour.” In Nepal, rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations after catastrophic floods entered a 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescues of four survivors. Rescuers found two more people alive on Saturday, joining two saved the day before in what have been described as miraculous tales of survival. Three of those have been found in hydropower tunnels where the government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive. “Search and rescue is going on at the tunnels despite geography, adverse weather and lack of connectivity,” Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha told AFP . Rescue workers were experiencing “multiple challenges”, he said. The wall of icy water and debris tore through mountain districts on August 26, destroying roads, bridges and other infrastructure. On Saturday, rescuers pulled a Chinese man alive from deep inside a hydropower tunnel, and a 64-year-old Nepali woman, Chandrika Shrestha, from her mud-covered home. Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the latter rescue had “given hope to the entire nation”. A day earlier, two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continue alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects affected. Other examples of remarkable fortitude have emerged from Nepal, including Rajendra Dawadi, a school principal who quickly ordered an evacuation as the torrent approached, saving hundreds of students’ lives. “If the information was wrong, we would lose a day of schooling,” he told AFP . “But if it was true, we were going to lose our lives.” Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said work was continuing to restore electricity in several areas. “Places that have unreachable, we’ve tried to restore power with solar,” he told AFP . Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has called the disaster a “Himalayan tsunami” and has warned reconstruction costs could run into the billions of dollars. The United Nations has said the magnitude of the destruction makes delivering aid an immense challenge, and has launched a $50 million appeal to help more than 84,000 people. With mortuaries overflowing, Nepal has buried hundreds of bodies in mass graves, after taking DNA samples for future identification, according to the police. Only around 100 bodies have been identified and handed over to families. Nepal will hold a national day of mourning on Monday, the 13th day since the disaster, in line with a traditional period of mourning in Hindu rituals. While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melting worldwide, increasing the risk of such disasters.

Some social media users praised the beating while others denounced the police officers’ actions, with several X users saying the man had yet to be found guilty of the crime. title: Scuffle in Karachi's DHA: Fresh case registered after inquiry report finds first FIR unsubstantiated
author: Imtiaz Ali
description: Case registered on complaint of woman who was assaulted as previous FIR, which implicated her, disposed of.
text: KARACHI: A resident of Karachi’s Defence Housing Authority (DHA) has sought action against her neighbours and police personnel for allegedly beating her in a fresh case registered in connection with a scuffle outside her apartment last month, it emerged on Sunday. The matter came to light when the CCTV footage of the physical altercation at an apartment building in DHA’s Phase 6 surfaced on social media last week. The footage showed police officials restraining a woman as another woman with a dumbbell attacked her. However, the initial first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered against the woman who was assaulted and her brother. But an inquiry report later said that the allegations in the FIR were “not substantiated” by the findings and also recommended departmental action against police officials involved in the incident. The report also said the first FIR should be disposed of, and subsequently, another was registered at the Darakhshan police station on September 5. In the second FIR, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the complainant said she was a resident of a third-floor apartment in DHA, Phase 6. The FIR quoted her as saying that on August 20 at 11:45pm, she was at her house with her brother and mother when a police officer rang the apartment’s doorbell and told her that her neighbour was calling them to the ground floor. Shortly after, the complainant continued, her neighbour came upstairs while hurling curses and started banging on the door. “When I opened the door, she dragged me by the hair, snatched my phone, and threw it down,” she alleged. “When my mother came out, she grabbed her by the hair as well and beat her,” the complainant claimed, adding that her neighbour then pinned her to a wall. The neighbour then went to her apartment and came back with her daughter and some police officials and “attempted to take away our phones, […] and her daughter, who was carrying a dumbbell, hit us”, she alleged. She further stated that she, along with her family, ran inside the house and called the police. “Meanwhile, the police officials outside broke the CCTV camera and later, the Darakhshan police broke into our house and took my and my brother’s cellphones away,” the FIR said. The complainant sought action against the suspects for “beating me, stealing our mobile phones and damaging the security camera”. The case was registered under Sections 147 (punishment for rioting), 148(rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 379 (punishment for theft), 427(mischief causing damage to the amount of fifty rupees), and 337A(i) (whoever, by doing any act with the intention of thereby causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt to any person) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). Meanwhile, Darakhshan Police Sub-Inspector Imran Khan was suspended with pay on Sunday, pending an inquiry into his conduct in the DHA scuffle case. “He is shifted to PHQ Garden, South Zone Karachi, where he will attend daily roll call/parade, accordingly,” the suspension notice dated Sept 6 said, a copy of which is available with Dawn . A show-cause notice issued to Imran by South Investigation Superintendent of Police (SP) Touheed Rehman Memon observed that Khan had “failed to collect the tangible evidence, video footage of the incident and conduct [an] impartial investigation purely on merit”. His conduct reflected “a lack of professional diligence, negligence and dereliction of duty”, the notice stated, a copy of which is available with Dawn . Appropriate punishment for the negligence could include removal from service, the notice stated. An inquiry report into the incident had previously found that the investigating officer, identified as SIP Imran, had undertaken “no serious efforts” to collect evidence and did not independently apply his mind to investigate the case. In the CCTV footage of the incident, a woman can be seen rushing down a flight of stairs with a dumbbell in her hand and charging at another woman before using it to hit her. The video also showed two individuals in what appeared to be police uniforms restraining the woman being assaulted, and a man who came up the stairs shortly after and began arguing with the woman with the dumbbell. At one point, the man and woman being assaulted managed to go inside what appeared to be their home, following which the woman with a dumbbell and another man began banging on their door and yelling obscenities. At the end, a man in a shalwar kameez was seen using a weapon, provided by one of the people in uniform, to smash the CCTV camera. An inquiry report, which was issued on Friday, found that the incident was sparked by a parking dispute between the mother-in-law of Korangi Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Fida Hussain Janwari and another resident. It identified the police officials visible in the CCTV footage as constables Saqib and Haider Sultan. It further added that the plainclothes man who destroyed the CCTV camera in the footage was Constable Taimoor Ahmed, while the official who handed over his weapon for this purpose was Constable Amir Sohail. “All were detailed for duty at the private bungalow of the Korangi SSP,” it said, adding that strict departmental action should be taken against them. It further said that the on-the-spot arrests in the case without justifiable evidence by Darakhshan Station House Officer Rashid Ali and Assistant Sub-inspector Aftab Mangi were not justifiable and spoke of the officials’ “tilt towards the aggressive party”. It said that the investigating officer, identified as Sub Inspector Imran, also undertook “no serious efforts” to collect evidence and did not independently apply his mind to investigate the case. “Hence, all three officials of District South are recommended to be strictly proceeded against departmentally for miscarriage of justice,” it said. It further said that the “lapse of supervision and lack of control over his subordinates is evident on the part of the Korangi SSP”. It called for examining his overall conduct in light of Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020 and to take further action in this regard. The report also said that an FIR should be registered against the SSP’s mother-in-law and her daughter and son, as well as the police officials present at the time of the incident, while the “victim family shall be encouraged to initiate legal action at free will against them”.

title: KP CM says won't leave Sindh without holding Karachi rally as PTI convoy en route to city
author: Mohammad Hussain Khan | News Desk
description: Roads around Mazar-i-Quaid closed to traffic as police say no gathering will be allowed; PTI alleges hurdles, arrests despite "welcome" from Bilawal.
text: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday said he would not leave Sindh without holding a planned PTI gathering in Karachi, as his convoy made its way to the city from Hyderabad. The KP CM, accompanied by PTI’s provincial President Junaid Akbar, has been on a five-day public mobilisation campaign in Sindh for the party’s September 27 nationwide protest for the release of its founder Imran Khan and his immediate medical treatment at Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital. Speaking to reporters at night while en route to Karachi, Afridi said he would stay in Sindh until he held a rally in the provincial capital. “If we cannot reach Karachi today, God willing, we will hold the rally tomorrow; if not tomorrow, then the day after. “I will not take a single step out of Sindh without launching a street movement in Karachi. I will stay here until the objective is achieved.” Referring to Saturday’s comments by PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, the KP CM said, “We are welcomed on social media, while on the other hand, roadblocks are being erected along our route. “I have already asked Bilawal that if he is not having all this done, then he should tell us who is doing it. Bring their names forward, then we will see what they do and what we do. “The people of Sindh will question you, because the government and police are all under your watch. If the police are not doing this, then remove the police from the scene and let whoever is responsible come forward,” Afridi contended. In a social media post on X, shared at around 11:15pm, PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh said the caravan would “reach Karachi in any way by defying all the hurdles”. In a post at 9:44pm, Sheikh said, “We are present at extremely deserted, raw paths in the interior. God willing, we will definitely reach Karachi.” In earlier posts on his X account, Sheikh said he was “clearing obstacles” that his convoy faced on Kotri bridge on the way out of Hyderabad. Karachi’s District East police, in a statement, said that “no public gatherings, rallies or processions will be allowed around Mazar-i-Quaid”, located at Shahrah-i-Quaideen, where the PTI has planned its rally. “If any gathering is held despite the lack of permission, legal action will be taken in accordance with the law,” it warned. Security arrangements at Mazar-i-Quaid had been “further strengthened in view of the current threat situation”, the police statement added, noting the deployment of additional police personnel. “Surveillance at the entry and exit points of Mazar-i-Quaid has also been further tightened.” While the Karachi Traffic Police cited “security” for closing some routes around Mazar-i-Quaid, a senior police officer told Dawn that the closures had nothing to do with the PTI rally. The officer, who wished not to be named, said the roads leading to Mazar-i-Quaid were closed with containers as security agencies had issued a security threat. The police officer said that the district administration had not given permission to the political party to hold a rally at the Mazar-i-Quaid because of the security threat. However, the party may hold a rally on the Super Highway at Toll Plaza or near Jail Chowrangi as there were no “restrictions” on them for holding the same at the said venues. The senior officer said several party supporters were detained when they attempted to reach the Mazar-i-Quaid on Sunday evening. He said around 150-200 workers of the PTI gathered, adding that the police tried to stop them but they “resorted to attacking the policemen with stones, resulting in injuries to one policeman”. “The law enforcers resorted to shelling to disperse them,” the police officer said, adding that a few party workers were also detained during the action. A traffic police official, who wished to remain anonymous, also told Dawn that certain roads had been blocked in the metropolis because of a “red alert” issued by law enforcement authorities. As of 6pm, the traffic police said both sides of Shahrah-i-Quaideen had been closed to traffic for “security”. As an alternative, traffic from Noorani Chowrangi was being diverted towards Khalid Bin Waleed Road, while traffic approaching Allah Wali Chowrangi was being diverted towards Tariq Road. Shortly after 4pm, New MA Jinnah Road and the road near the Corridor-III parking plaza towards PP Chowrangi and Jail Chowrangi had been closed to traffic from both sides for security. Traffic was being diverted from Saddar Dawakhana towards the Star Gate side, while traffic from Jail Chowrangi was being diverted towards Kashmir Road and Tariq Road. Earlier in the day, CM Afridi addressed a huge welcome rally at Hyder Chowk in Hyderabad. “Who does Hyderabad belong to?”, Afridi roared amidst applause from the crowd, whom he thanked for turning up to welcome him. PTI leaders Aminulalh Musakhel, Mohsin Ghulam, Faisal Mughal and Usama Hafeez were among those present. “There are only two families ruling Pakistan – one from Sindh and the other from Punjab – but it was only PTI whose leader Imran Khan chose me, an ordinary worker, to be the KP CM,” Afridi said, referring to the PPP and PML-N. “Tomorrow another worker is to become chief minister from PTI,” he added. He urged youth to rise for their country and for themselves. “September 27 would mark a historic date and change the destiny of Pakistan,” he asserted, referring to the planned countrywide protest. He assailed Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz for her recent remarks regarding other provinces and demanded an apology from her. Maryam had said on Saturday that Punjab faced a greater security threat from its neighbouring provinces than it did from India. “Please tell us who is right,” the KP CM said, addressing the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) director general as he highlighted the military’s stance that India backed terrorist groups’ activities in Pakistan. Accusing the Sharif family of tax evasion and having properties abroad, Afridi said, “These people were sincere neither in the past nor today and they will not be sincere tomorrow.” Addressing the gathering, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said that his party had faced enough cases, contending that courts’ doors have been shut on it. Raja described September 27 as the day of “true freedom” for people. The PTI confirmed shortly after 5:30pm that the central leadership’s convoy led by CM Afridi had entered Hyderabad district. Earlier, on his way to Hyderabad, Afridi addressed PTI workers in Tando Allahyar. While thanking PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari for welcoming him to Sindh on social media, Afridi alleged that hurdles were being created for his convoy. “My message for Bilawal Bhutto is that obstructions are being raised in our way,” the KP CM said, affirming that people were still with PTI despite those hurdles. “Containers are being placed and craters are being dug,” he claimed. “Is this being done by your [PPP] government or by someone else?” Afridi asked. “Will they host their guests in this manner?” he added. The PTI leader urged party supporters and workers to join the planned September 27 rallies across the country. In a video shared on X, CM Afridi said that it was “possible they might have created some hurdles in the way”, but the party convoy would defy them to reach Hyderabad, and then finally Karachi. Thanking the people from Umerkot for their support yesterday, the PTI leader also asked the people of Hyderabad to be prepared for the PTI caravan. “After Hyderabad, we will be in Karachi by the evening,” the KP CM declared. In a statement, the PTI condemned the alleged blocking of its caravan travelling from Hyderabad to Karachi and also claimed its party workers in multiple cities of Sindh had been taken into custody. The statement marked a turn from Saturday’s cordial exchange on social media between CM Afridi and Bilawal. “On the one hand, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari welcomes Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and PTI’s visit to Sindh on social media; on the other hand, the Sindh government, under his influence, is using the police to block roads and arrest PTI workers,” the PTI said. It termed the alleged actions a “manifestation of the PPP’s blatant political hypocrisy and fear”. “If the PPP truly believes in democracy and political freedom, then why is it so afraid of a peaceful PTI political rally?” PTI asked. PTI asserted that the police deployments, barriers and arrests could not prevent its party workers and the people of Sindh from exercising their political rights. “The PTI leadership made it clear that the people of Sindh are not slaves to feudal or dynastic politics. They have the right to welcome leaders of the political party of their choice, voice their concerns and express their political opinion,” the party maintained. It demanded that the PPP chairman direct his Sindh government to ensure “political freedom in practice”. “If the welcome is limited to Twitter while police arrest workers on the ground, this is not democracy but political theatrics.” The party also demanded the immediate release of all workers allegedly taken into custody in Hyderabad, Karachi and other parts of Sindh, as well as an end to any obstruction to the PTI’s political activities. PTI Sindh President Haleem Adil Sheikh, who was accompanying the KP CM, shared a video of him driving a truck, which he claimed was placed to block his convoy’s route in Tando Allahyar. Sheikh later shared videos of what he described as the people of Hyderabad welcoming the PTI convoy. On Saturday night, Afridi thanked Bilawal after the latter wished him the best for the rest of his visit to Sindh. In a post on X, the PPP leader welcomed Afridi to the “city of martyrs” after the KP chief minister reached Larkana. “Best wishes for the remainder of your tour across Sindh. We must ultimately return to a politics of tolerance, respect and coexistence, the foundation of any democracy,” Bilawal wrote. In response, Afridi thanked him and noted that the “beauty of democracy is in freedom of politics and expression, independence of judiciary, acceptance of public mandate, an independent parliament and press being free”. He also expressed hope that a large crowd would come out on the PTI’s call in Karachi and Hyderabad, where he is due today. Last time Afridi was in Sindh to mobilise people for a street movement, he had initially praised the PPP-led Sindh government’s reception, saying the democratic legacy of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto still thrived in the province. However, he had later accused the Sindh government of not upholding the honour of the ajrak and topi and criticised its treatment of its “guests”. Ahead of Afridi’s rally in Karachi on January 11, the party had alleged that the KP CM had to face obstacles on his way to the metropolis. The party also accused the authorities of violence against its workers and supporters.

title: Iranian tankers hit after IRGC ‘attack on US ships’
author: Agencies
description: Iran vows to carry out more severe strikes against military vessels if "blockade" continues; Hegseth says Tehran’s oil tanker fleet "defenceless".
text: • Iran vows to carry out more severe strikes against military vessels if ‘blockade’ continues • Hegseth says Tehran’s oil tanker fleet ‘defenceless’ • US citizens in Bahrain urged to ‘exercise heightened vigilance’ DUBAI: US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday, US Central Command said, including one off the coast of Kharg Island, near Iran’s key oil export hub. The strikes were carried out after Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two US Navy ships, Central Command said. “Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” said Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command. Tasnim , the semi-official Iranian news agency, reported earlier that four US missiles hit a tanker in the area of Kharg’s anchorage. Tasnim quoted local sources as saying there were no casualties and the tanker’s crew was being evacuated. No American personnel were harmed, Central Command said. In a statement on X, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said that Iran’s oil tanker fleet was “defenceless” after American forces struck three of them today. In a post on X, Hegseth reiterated the US claim that Iran had no navy or air force, writing, “It’s simple: if Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers. All they have to do is not shoot at [the US Navy]. He added that US submarines, warships and warplanes could “strike them all” within the Central Command and Pacific Command areas of responsibility. A spokesperson for the Iranian military’s Khatam al-Anbiya Central Head­quarters has warned that if the US continues its naval blockade and “harassment of Iranian ships”, then Iran will carry out more severe and potentially expanded strikes targeting American military vessels, Al Jazeera reported, citing a statement. The statement, carried by Iranian broadcaster IRIB , comes after the US claimed to have hit three Iranian oil tankers. The exchange of attacks followed an escalation in the past week that threatened to deepen a conflict that had dragged on since the US launched strikes on Iran in February, disrupting global energy supplies and drawing opposition from a majority of Americans before congressional elections in November. Meanwhile, the US embassy in Bahrain urged citizens to ‘exercise heightened vigilance’ in a security alert. “The US embassy reminds American citizens that Iran has previously targeted civilian infrastructure in Bahrain, including hotels in Manama,” the alert said, instructing US nationals to prepare for “potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions”. US President Donald Trump said on August 31 in a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video that Kharg Island was being “blown to smithereens”. Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked. Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90 per cent of its crude via Kharg Island before the war, but flows have been disrupted since a US blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April. Trump said on June 11 that he wanted to take over Kharg Island, but then said a threatened US military operation there was off the table for now, days before Tehran and Washington signed an interim agreement aimed at ending the war on June 17. A US attack on Kharg would further pressure Iran’s oil industry and its wider economy, which is already reeling from the US naval blockade. Published in Dawn, September 6th, 2026

title: Three girls suffer burns in gas leak explosion in Chishtian
author: Our Correspondent
description: District officer says gas accumulated due to a leak, caused powerful explosion that engulfed the entire house.
text: BAHAWALNAGAR: Three teenage girls suffered burns after a powerful explosion caused by a gas leak ignited a fire in their home in Chishtian on Saturday noon. District Officer (Emergency) Rao Sharafat told Dawn that the incident occurred in Farooq Colony at 1:48pm when the occupants of the house lit a match to cook something in the kitchen. He said the gas that had accumulated due to a leak, caused a powerful explosion that engulfed the entire house. As a result, Hadia Yousuf (16), Sadia Yousuf (17), and Fatima Ramzan (18) suffered burn injuries in the incident. According to rescue personnel, the injured were taken to the Chishtian THQ Hospital and were undergoing treatment. Health CEO Dr Shaukat Ali informed Dawn that the girls had suffered burns on 40 to 60 percent of their bodies and had been transferred to Multan’s burn unit due to their serious condition. Rescue 1122 has issued a public advisory recommending that if the smell of gas was detected anywhere in the home, open the windows immediately, avoid using any open flames or electrical switches, and inform 1122 right away. INJURED: Five schoolgirls and their attendant were injured when a motorcycle rickshaw overturned when they were on their way home from school in Minchinabad on Saturday noon. According to rescue officials, at around 2:13pm, a motorcycle rickshaw transporting schoolgirls flipped over near the Sunyaron Wali Sadki area in Minchinabad, injuring five girls aged seven to fifteen and their attendant. The injured were immediately taken to the Minchinabad THQ Hospital. Published in Dawn, September 6th, 2026

title: Falak Javed granted post-arrest bail in ‘police attack’ case
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
description: Defence says investigation completed, no justification for keeping her behind bars; anti-terrorism court extends pre-arrest bail of Imran Khan’s sisters.
text: LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court on Saturday granted post-arrest bail to Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf social media activist Falak Javed in a case of alleged attack on Islamabad police team outside Zaman Park residence of former prime minister Imran Khan. Judge Malik Abid Hussain allowed bail application of the activist and directed her to furnish surety bonds worth Rs100,000. The prosecution produced the case record before the court while the suspect’s counsel completed his arguments on the bail petition. The defence counsel argued that Ms Javed was a woman and had a legal right to be released on bail. He said the investigation had been completed and there was no justification for keeping her behind bars. Opposing the bail plea, a state counsel alleged that the suspect was involved in an attack on Islamabad police officials outside Zaman Park. He claimed that a petrol bomb had also been recovered from her during the investigation. According to the prosecution, Islamabad police had gone to the residence of PTI founding chairman Imran Khan to serve summons. The prosecution alleged that enraged party workers hurled petrol bombs at the police and injured several officers. Racecourse police had registered FIR No. 410/2023 in connection with the alleged attack on police. BAIL:An anti-terrorism court on Saturday extended pre-arrest bail of PTI founding chairman Imran Khan’s sisters – Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan – and other party leaders in multiple cases of violence including May 9 riots. Both sisters, former federal ministers Asad Umar, Azam Swati and Fawad Chaudhry appeared before the court on expiry of their bail period. The court extended the bail till Oct 6. title: Fire in SZMCH during operation triggers panic
author: Irfanul Haq
description: DC seeks detailed report containing the facts and findings of the incident.
text: RAHIM YAR KHAN: A fire broke out in the operating theatre of Sheikh Zayed Medical College Hospital (SZMCH) during a surgical procedure on Saturday morning, triggering panic among patients and hospital staff. Reports said some doctors and members of the paramedical staff were performing an operation in one of the hospital’s operating theatres during the early hours of Saturday when a fire broke out in the electrical wiring, causing smoke to spread throughout the theatre. The doctors and paramedical staff immediately suspended the procedure and shifted the patient to a safer location. A senior doctor at SZMCH, requesting anonymity, told this correspondent that a fire had broken out in the same theatre in Phase-II around 10 days ago, but the incident was not disclosed. The doctor said that the same shift of doctors and paramedical staff had been performing their duties in the theatre at the time of that incident as well. The doctor further alleged that the latest fire incident might have been the result of a conspiracy due to internal differences between the hospital administration and the medical college administration. SZMCH focal person and Deputy Medical Superintendent Rana Ilyas Ahmed said the fire was caused by a short circuit. He said the hospital staff responded immediately and adopted an appropriate strategy to control the blaze. He added that, immediately after the incident occurred, security personnel, with the assistance of doctors and paramedical staff, demonstrated a professional and vigilant response and brought the fire under control using firefighting equipment. Meanwhile, Deputy Commissioner (DC) Zaheer Anwar Jappa took notice of the incident and directed Assistant Commissioner Abdul Hannan Khan to ascertain the cause of the fire. The DC also sought a detailed report containing the facts and findings of the incident. Later, the DC convened a meeting with district administration officers, the CEO of the District Health Authority, and representatives of other relevant departments to review arrangements for dealing with emergency situations in government hospitals across the district. The DC directed the officers to ensure regular monitoring of firefighting equipment, emergency response mechanisms, staff training, sanitation, and other administrative arrangements to ensure preparedness for emergencies. LIVESTOCK: Ten livestock, including cows and buffalo calves, died while around 25 were said to be critical in a farm at Chak 96-P on Saturday. According to unconfirmed reports, the animals were affected when they were vaccinated by a local livestock vaccinator. The DC sought a detailed report on the issue from the livestock additional director who started the initial investigations after reaching village 96-P with a mobile laboratory and a team of doctors. title: Forecast for flooding of low-lying areas in seven Punjab cities
author: Khalid Hasnain
description: Heavy downpours may disrupt routine life in Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, Faisalabad, Sargodha, Jhang and Okara, forecast says.
text: LAHORE: The Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological Department on Saturday warned of inundation of the low-lying areas of seven Punjab cities due to possible rainfall on Sunday (today). The forecast for Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, Faisalabad, Sargodha, Jhang and Okara says that heavy downpours may disrupt routine life and movement in these cities. According to the FFD, the flow at Guddu Barrage is expected to reach the low-flood level while moderate increases in flows are also expected in the Indus, Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi rivers and their associated tributaries. The division has also warned of possible urban flooding in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujrat and Gujranwala and flash flooding in streams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and tributaries of the Kabul River. The FFD also warns of increased flows in the major rivers and associated rainwater drains amid the ongoing spell of the monsoon. According to the information provided by it, Tarbela reservoir is currently at its maximum conservation level while Mangla reservoir is 79% filled. The cities include Lahore, Faisalabad and Sargodha The River Indus at Kalabagh and Chashma is currently at low flood level while all other major rivers are flowing in their normal flows at other gauging stations. title: Huge support for PTI in Sindh a challenge to PPP’s traditional dominance: Sohail Afridi
author: Zulfiqar Memon
description: KP chief minister leads party’s campaign for Sept 27 nationwide protest to Nawabshah.
text: NAWABSHAH: Embol­dened by a big turnout of supporters in a city like Nawabshah, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Secret­ary General Salman Akram Raja on Saturday said that the huge gathering, like similar ones in many other cities over the last three days, effectively posed a challenge to the Pakistan Peoples Party. They were addressing the crowd of PTI supporters who had thronged Nawabshah from various areas of the Benazirabad district to welcome the party’s convoy. The KP CM accompanied by PTI’s provincial President Junaid Akber has been on a five-day public mobilisation campaign in Sindh for the party’s Sept 27 nationwide protest for the release of its founder Imran Khan and his immediate medical treatment at the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad. Other senior PTI leaders, including its Sindh President, Haleem Adil Sheikh, are also part of the whirlwind tour. CM Afridi acknowledged perseverance of the people, especially women, who endured a long wait for the arrival of the PTI leaders from Naushahro Feroze and other towns, where the latter received warm welcome by their supporters in large numbers. KP chief minister leads party’s campaign for Sept 27 nationwide protest to Nawabshah “The fervor for PTI and Imran Khan across Sindh demonstrates a big change in the political dynamics in this province and challenges the traditional political dominance of PPP in the region,” Sohail Afridi said. He criticised dynastic politics at the federal and provincial levels, asserting that a true leadership emerges from people’s vote, not from the backdoors under certain arrangements. Commenting on the country’s state of economy, Mr Afridi pointed out that the national debt had surged from Rs43 trillion until PTI’s tenure to over Rs97 trillion now which shows the performance of the current dispensation. He accused the ruling parties and their leaders of having plundered taxpayers’ money and said the leaders were buying luxury properties abroad for themselves while neglecting even basic amenities for the ordinary people. Highlighting the treatment being meted out to Imran Khan in his unlawful incarceration, he condemned the government for repeatedly defying even judicial orders to allow him to have proper medical treatment at the Shifa International Hospital. He urged the masses to demonstrate their support to Imran Khan by joining the September 27 protests across the country. He said the demonstration was also for the release of all political prisoners and withdrawal of false cases against them, besides restoration of a genuine judiciary. The ongoing campaign, he said, would remain steadfast despite all threats and obstacles. In his speech, Barrister Salman Akram Raja told the crowd that Imran Khan’s struggle was aimed at securing the country’s democratic future and protecting people’s rights. He urged the masses across Sindh to actively participate in the September 27 protest, saying that it would be a critical turning point in the struggle for the rights of people. Haleem Adil Sheikh, Sardar Sher Mohammed Rind and other PTI leaders were also present. Published in Dawn, September 6th, 2026

title: PTI volunteer unit to provide security to Sept 27 long march

description: A group of ideological workers of PTI has announced the formation of a volunteer unit “Pasdaran-e-Azm Imran Khan Pakistan".
text: PESHAWAR: A group of ideological workers of the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has announced the formation of a volunteer unit, “Pasdaran-e-Azm Imran Khan Pakistan,” to provide assistance and protection to party workers for the September 27 long march being organised for the release of PTI founder Imran Khan. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Afridi said that Pasdaran-e-Azm Imran Khan Pakistan was a voluntary unit comprising ideological PTI workers and would play a leading role in providing assistance to participants of the September 27 caravan. He said the volunteers would operate within the constitutional and legal framework and would not allow anyone to take the law into their own hands. The unit, he added, would also try to prevent workers from engaging in any unconstitutional or unlawful activity. Mr Afridi said the volunteers would provide first-aid assistance to people injured during possible shelling and extend their voluntary services wherever needed during the march. He said the unit required proper protective equipment and appealed to the party leadership to provide volunteers with first-aid kits, helmets, protective masks, shoes and uniforms. He also urged Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to encourage volunteers and facilitate them with the required protective and first-aid equipment. Mr Afridi said efforts were under way to recruit more volunteers from other districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to expand its services during the long march. He said the volunteers would work to remove obstacles encountered along the route while remaining within the law. title: War has made Tehran more confident, say US intelligence agencies
author: Anwar Iqbal
description: Intelligence assessments also indicate that reaching an agreement to end the war could prove difficult.
text: WASHINGTON: Intelli­gence agencies in the United States believe that six months of war may have made Iran more, not less, confident in its ability to withstand American pressure and continue the conflict. A New York Times report, published on Friday, says “Iran has grown more confident in its ability to attack targets in the Middle East and appears determined to continue the conflict for months to frustrate the United States”. The assessment comes as clashes resumed this week. “The new exchanges have been limited so far. But the intelligence reports, according to people who have read them, suggest that Iran’s hardline government might be contemplating a significant escalation,” the newspaper reported. The intelligence assessments also indicate that reaching an agreement to end the war could prove difficult. Current and former US officials told the NYT that there are few indications Tehran is ready to make a deal with Washington. Some officials believe Tehran may seek to prolong the conflict until at least the US mid-term elections in November, calculating that continued warfare and high energy prices could create difficulties for President Trump and Republicans. The report notes Donald Trump is currently not pursuing negotiations as he believes that economic pressure can force Tehran to make concessions concerning its control of the Strait of Hormuz and, eventually, its nuclear programme. But officials familiar with the intelligence told the NYT that sanctions could provoke further escalation. Iran’s military calculations appear shaped by its growing missile and drone capability and by its understanding of how to use the Strait of Hormuz as leverage. The strait carried roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil before the war. Representative Jason Crow, a Colorado Democrat and member of the House Intelligence Committee, described the Iranian leadership as increasingly confident. “Iranians are feeling pretty bullish about their position,” he said. But at the same time he acknowledged that Iran has suffered substantial damage. Other officials briefed on the intelligence said Iran may also believe that the United States will be constrained in launching major new attacks as its ammunition stocks decline. Representative Josh Gottheimer, a New Jersey Democrat and Intelligence Committee member, said: “The Iranians think they have maximum leverage.” He suggested that, from Tehran’s perspective, continuing to pressure the Trump administration could serve its interests. The conflict has also opened a cyber front. According to the Times , US officials believe Iran-linked hackers were probably responsible for attacks on more than 100 American water systems in late July. The attacks did not appear to make drinking water unsafe, although some caused disruptions requiring manual overrides and precautionary boil-water advisories. Officials said Iranian hackers have also shown interest in US oil and gas infrastructure. The New York Times reported that Iranian-linked cyber hackers may have regrouped after suffering losses early in the war. Former intelligence officials and cybersecurity experts said such attacks could remain attractive to Tehran because even limited disruptions might weaken American public support for a conflict with no clear end. Alex Orleans, a former US government cybersecurity contractor who tracks Iranian hacking groups, said Iran’s cyberoperators probably feel emboldened. He warned that even unsuccessful attacks could serve a broader purpose by exhausting public patience with the conflict. The report also describes Iranian efforts to influence US politics, including propaganda and social-media activity focused on mid-term elections. Meta recently identified a small network of Iran-based accounts on Facebook and Instagram that posted material concerning US politics. Taken together, the intelligence assessments present a picture of an Iranian government that has been damaged but does not regard itself as defeated. Six months of warfare may have strengthened Tehran’s belief that it can absorb punishment, retain important military capabilities and continue imposing costs on the United States and its allies. title: Economy faces downside risks: FPCCI
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
description: Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry warns that costly energy and high interest rates are crippling industrial and export sectors.
text: KARACHI: Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) President Atif Ikram Sheikh has voiced concern over the widening of the trade deficit during 2MFY27 by 18.1 per cent to $7.1 billion from $6.025bn. While acknowledging a slight recovery in overall economic activity, he said the increase in exports has been drastically outpaced by a surge in imports, warning that the resulting trade deficit poses an immediate threat to the country’s macroeconomic stability and foreign exchange reserves. In a statement, he said the failure of exports to keep pace with rising imports is not due to a lack of industrial capacity or entrepreneurial intent, but is the direct result of the crippling cost of doing business. Export-oriented industries are being pushed to the wall, rendering them entirely uncompetitive against regional peers in global markets, he added. Warns costly energy, high interest rates crippling industrial, export sectors Outlining bottlenecks behind the devastating decline in industrial productivity, he said the central bank’s exceptionally high policy rate remains an absolute barrier to the smooth functioning of trade and industry. No industry can achieve a profit margin high enough to service such expensive loans, which has stalled private-sector credit growth and prevented manufacturers from securing working capital or investing in essential long-term modernisation, he added. Upward revisions in electricity tariffs, driven by massive capacity charges and cross-subsidisation burdens, have made it impossible for factories to scale up production, the FPCCI chief said, stressing that without a regionally competitive power tariff, key export sectors will continue to underperform and lose global market share. The disruptions and cost of gas supply have eroded the narrow profit margins exporters rely on to secure international orders. Additionally, elevated petroleum prices continue to pose a major hurdle, triggering a multiplier effect on inland logistics, supply chains, and goods transportation — thereby heavily inflating the final cost of exportable goods before they even reach the ports, Mr Atif said. The domestic industries are burdened by the highest regional interest rates and exorbitant energy costs. Local manufacturing shrinks, and the economy inevitably pivots to expensive imports to meet domestic demand. This vicious cycle will lead to a wider trade deficit, a decline in export orders, and intense pressure on our national exchequer, he added. He urged the prime minister, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Commerce, and the State Bank of Pakistan to immediately sit down with the business community to devise a crisis-response strategy to avert widespread industrial closures and rescue the FY27 export targets. He also demanded an aggressive reduction in the policy rate to provide affordable capital for industrial production, immediate rationalisation of electricity and gas tariffs to bring them in line with regional competitors, and targeted relief on petroleum levies for goods transport to reduce domestic supply chain costs. title: Iran buries wedding attack victims as missiles fly in Gulf
author: Agencies
description: Washington says strike incident is under investigation, denies targeting civilians.
text: • Washington says strike incident is under investigation, denies targeting civilians • Tehran launches missile, drone retaliation at American bases in Kuwait; says Hormuz will not open without its consent • US extends Middle East troop deployment; Trump dismisses ammunition concerns KUHESTAK: Iranian mourners carried caskets on Thursday for victims of a United States air strike that reportedly struck a wedding, as Tehran launched overnight retaliatory missile and drone attacks at US bases in Kuwait, despite threats of further strikes from President Donald Trump. Mourners assembled late on Thursday afternoon outside the village of Kuhestak in Sirik county, along a coastal stretch of the Strait of Hormuz hit by heavy US air strikes. Iranian officials say four people died and nearly 70 were wounded when a strike hit a home during a wedding ceremony. State television reported that a fifth person, a 22-year-old woman, died in hospital. “This is the body of martyr Amir-Mohammad Karimi, a 4-year-old child who was martyred in an attack on the country’s south by the criminal American regime,” a reporter from Iran’s Mehr news agency said in footage showing a flag-draped coffin beneath palm fronds. In other footage, mourners threw petals into the air as doleful music played. A casket was carried past a row of soldiers standing at attention. “If it was a military location, it wouldn’t be so painful. This was a wedding ceremony, but they turned people’s joy into mourning,” the semi-official Tasnim news agency quoted a local man as saying. US Vice President JD Vance said the incident is under investigation. “What I can say with 100 per cent confidence is that unlike the IRGC, the United States never targets civilians in combat,” Vance said, referring to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Despite Trump threatening that the US military is prepared to attack Iran “any time we want”, Tehran retaliated with strikes across the Middle East. Iran’s army said it hit the Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait with missiles and drones early on Thursday. Kuwait’s military said its air defences intercepted the attack, which it called a direct threat to its security and a grave breach of international law. Amid the escalating conflict, Iran’s parliamentary National Security and Foreign Policy Commission head Ebrahim Azizi declared that the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened without Iran’s consent. Azizi emphasised that Tehran has proven its ability to make its threats credible to the United States. Vance disputed this, asserting Iran is losing its grip over the strategic waterway as more oil and gas exit the strait. However, the vice president blamed Iran’s continued attacks on commercial shipping for high domestic gasoline prices, stating Washington will not hold talks with Tehran unless the attacks stop. Meanwhile, the United States is extending the deployment of thousands of American troops and military assets across the Middle East into 2027, signalling Washington is preparing for a prolonged conflict. The extensions, ordered by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, will affect Army units, air defence forces, fighter squadrons and Navy personnel. According to a letter sent to soldiers’ families, elements of the Army’s 82nd Airborne Division could remain in the region well into 2027. The US military currently has roughly 50,000 troops in the Middle East. Hegseth initially presented the operation as a swift military action, but six months into the war, the Pentagon is preparing for extended deployments lasting a year or longer. Trump took to Truth Social on Thursday to deny reports of dwindling US ammunition stores, claiming the military has a “virtually unlimited” stockpile. He also confirmed 18 US service members were killed in Iran, clarifying remarks made by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported the deaths of six more naval personnel from US strikes this week, bringing the Iranian military death toll to at least 13 since Tuesday. Anwar Iqbal in Washington also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, September 4th, 2026

title: Pakistan issues demarche to US over Kashmir remarks by American ambassador to India
author: News Desk
description: Protest lodged over “factually incorrect remarks of US ambassador to India regarding status of Jammu and Kashmir during his visit” to the region.
text: The Foreign Office (FO) on Wednesday summoned the US charge d’affaires in Islamabad and lodged a “strong demarche” over “factually incorrect remarks” by the US ambassador to India regarding the status of Jammu and Kashmir during his visit to disputed region. “Pakistan strongly condemned and categorically rejected the characterisation of Jammu and Kashmir as a ‘part of India’,” said the FO statement. “It was underscored that Jammu and Kashmir is an internationally recognised disputed territory, awaiting final disposition in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people,” the statement added. It was further highlighted that the “irresponsible statement” by the US ambassador “negated the long-standing and well-documented position of the United States on the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, and also ran contrary to the US commitment to the supremacy of international law and the UN Charter,” it said. Pakistan appreciated US President Donald Trump’s offer to mediate between Pakistan and India to resolve the Kashmir dispute in the aftermath of Marka-i-Haq . However, the US side was urged to ensure that its public statements remained consistent with the disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir, the FO concluded. Kashmir is a disputed territory claimed in full by both Pakistan and India. The two countries fought their first war over the region in 1948, after which the liberated areas were declared Azad Jammu and Kashmir. A United Nations Security Council resolution passed in 1949 affirmed Kashmiris’ right to decide their future through a UN-sponsored plebiscite. The vote has yet to take place. In August 2019, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government revoked occupied Kashmir’s special status and autonomy by repealing Article 370 of the Indian Constitution. India’s Supreme Court upheld the move in December 2023. US President Donald Trump has offered to mediate the dispute between the nuclear-armed rivals as far back as his first term. In 2019, Trump told reporters he was willing to intervene , but a decision would be up to the leaders of both countries. “But if they wanted somebody to intervene, to help them […] and I spoke with Pakistan about that and I spoke frankly in India about it […] that battle has been going on for a long time. If I can, if they wanted me to, I would certainly intervene,” Trump said. He was informed that India rejected the offer, to which he replied, “It is really up to Prime Minister [Narendra] Modi.” In 2025, following Marka-i-Haq , the US State Department reiterated Trump’s offer and said each step that he takes “is made to solve generational differences between countries”. Trump had offered to work on the Kashmir issue after he brokered a ceasefire between Pakistan and India after the two nations’ most intense military confrontation in decades. In a message lauding the countries’ leaders for achieving peace, he remarked, “I will work with both of you to see if, after a ‘thousand years’, a solution can be arrived at concerning Kashmir.” Responding to a question on the steps US plans to take in the wake of Trump’s offer, State Department’s spokesperson Tammy Bruce during a White House press briefing noted, “So, while I can’t speak to his plans, the world knows his nature, and I can’t speak to any details of what he might have in that regard,” adding that the White House would have plenty to say about the matter. She further said, “[Trump] has been the only one to bring certain people to the table to have conversations that nobody thought was possible,” remaining hopeful that the Kashmir issue can also get resolved.

title: Stability paves way for sustainable growth: SBP chief
author: Shahid Iqbal
description: Hopes GDP growth remains between 3.5 and 4.5pc in FY27.
text: KARACHI: State Bank of Pakistan Governor Jameel Ahmad has said that the country is continuing to move from economic stabilisation towards sustainable growth and will achieve up to 4.5 per cent GDP growth in FY27. Addressing a gathering to commemorate the Independence Day with a flag-hoisting ceremony, Mr Ahmad said that the economy has made important progress towards stability during the past year, supported by greater economic discipline. He said that prudent fiscal and monetary policies facilitated economic expansion of 3.7pc in FY26. GDP growth is expected to remain between 3.5 and 4.5pc in FY27, he hoped. “This is an encouraging indication that the economy is continuing to move towards sustainable growth following a period of stabilisation,” said the governor. Sees inflation ranging between 5pc and 7pc Referring to developments in the external sector, Mr Ahmad said that overseas Pakistanis have expressed their confidence in the country’s economic progress through record remittances, which exceeded $41bn in FY26 and are ‘expected to reach $44bn in FY27.’ The increase in remittances and a low current account deficit are contributing to the improvement in the country’s foreign exchange reserves, which reached $18.4bn by the end of FY26. “SBP reserves are expected to exceed $21bn during FY27,” he said. Highlighting developments in price stability, the governor noted that average inflation during FY26 was 7.1pc. He said that SBP’s assessment is that the current monetary policy stance remains appropriate to maintain inflation within the 5-7pc medium-term target, while providing adequate room for economic activity, investment, and job creation. Mr Ahmad also highlighted the steps taken by the central bank during the past year to strengthen and modernise the financial system. He said that the successful launch of PRISM+ has brought the country’s payment infrastructure closer to international standards by making large-value payments and settlements faster, safer, and more efficient. He further noted that SBP’s measures to promote digital payments have contributed to a significant increase in the use of digital channels, with the number of retail digital transactions rising from around 10bn to 12bn in FY26. He said that the growth of digital payments is not only a reflection of greater technology adoption but also an important step towards a more documented, transparent, and efficient economy. Emphasising the importance of financial inclusion, he said that SBP remains committed to ensuring that all segments of society have access to the formal financial system. In this regard, the SBP has launched InvestPak to facilitate convenient, secure, and transparent investment opportunities for the public. He also highlighted SBP’s continued efforts to promote Islamic banking, green finance, cybersecurity, and financial technology to ensure that Pakistan’s financial system remains secure, resilient, and aligned with future requirements. He stressed that economic self-reliance, strong institutions, adherence to the rule of law, and national unity remain essential to realising the true spirit of independence. He said that while the SBP has made significant progress during the past year, challenges remain and require continued diligence, commitment, and resolve. The governor said that SBP’s focus will remain on price stability, policy reforms, and the creation of a conducive economic environment for higher productivity, export growth, and job creation. He emphasised that these priorities are essential for transforming economic stability into sustainable development and laying the foundation for a stronger and more prosperous Pakistan. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026
