title: The era of new alliances
author: HAMMAD SARFRAZ
description: The SCO offers a glimpse of an emerging international system that Washington is helping shape but may no longer lead
text: The most revealing development at this year’s Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit was not another declaration about the need for a multipolar world, it was Tayyip Erdogan’s suggestion that Turkey could seek full membership of an organisation whose two dominant powers are China and Russia. Turkey remains a member of Nato and Erdogan was careful to say that closer ties with the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) would not mean abandoning the West. But that is precisely what makes his statement so significant. A Nato member no longer sees participation in an institution led by Beijing and Moscow as something that requires an either-or choice. That would have been difficult to imagine when the post-Cold War order was at its peak. Washington’s alliances were not simply military arrangements, they helped shape the balance of power and the way countries dealt with one another. They could disagree with the US, trade with its competitors and pursue their own interests, but the basic understanding remained that the principal architecture of global security, finance and diplomacy would be shaped in Washington and its allied capitals across the West. That assumption has started to fade, not because countries have suddenly decided to join a bloc created by China, but because fewer of them see any reason to organise their foreign policies around a single centre of power that is the US. Ashok Swain, professor of Peace and Conflict at Uppsala University, views Trump’s “America First” policies as accelerating this shift. He argues that attacks on alliances, hostility toward multilateral institutions, unpredictable tariffs and the transactional treatment of even close partners have made the US look increasingly unreliable. Countries that once depended on Washington, he said, are therefore looking for other relationships and institutions. Russia benefits from the divisions within Europe and Nato, while China, he argues, stands to gain even more by presenting itself as a stable economic and diplomatic partner as the US relinquishes influence. “Trump may believe he is making America stronger,” Swain said, “but he is accelerating the decline of US global leadership and making the emergence of a China-led order easier.” The SCO summit in Bishkek offered a snapshot of what is emerging. The organisation now brings together China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran and the Central Asian republics, as well as Belarus, and its wider network includes countries that have very different relationships with Washington. It is not a military alliance and its members have serious disputes with one another. India and China remain at odds, India and Pakistan have a perennially antagonistic relationship, and Russia and China are partners without being formal allies. But all of them have found value in belonging to the same institution without having to resolve those differences or adopt the same relationship with the West. At the summit in Kyrgyzstan’s capital, President Xi Jinping carefully calibrated his speech to preserve that flexibility, describing the SCO’s experience as one based on non-alignment, non-confrontation and a refusal to target any third party, even as he argued that the organisation should play a more active role in shaping international affairs. He called multipolarity an irreversible trend and urged greater representation for the Global South, a more democratic international system and a stronger role for the United Nations. The language, by the Chinese leader’s standards, was familiar. The substance, however, is becoming increasingly practical. Beijing wants the countries gathered around the SCO to have more trade, investment, transport, energy, technology and financial links with one another, creating a strong network of relationships that does not depend on any one Western institution or country. Swain argues that the SCO has considerable potential precisely because it brings together China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Belarus and the Central Asian states. “It provides a platform for security cooperation, trade, energy, connectivity and resistance to Western political pressure.” In that sense, he sees the organisation as developing a parallel system of cooperation, although not yet an alternative global order. “The SCO is not a military alliance,” he explained, and its members have “serious internal contradictions”, from the rivalry between India and Pakistan to India’s distrust of China and the differing interests and ambitions of its members. Those contradictions could make enlargement both a source of strength and a constraint, making the organisation more representative while making consensus harder. But Swain believes the balance of power within the SCO will matter increasingly. Over time, he argues, it is likely to become more China-centric because Beijing has the greatest economic and political weight. Russia will remain important, but its position could gradually come to resemble that of Europe in the former US-led order, an influential but unequal partner operating under the shadow of the dominant power. For its part, it appears, Beijing is already putting resources behind its wider ambitions. President Xi announced plans for an international AI application cooperation centre for SCO members, a China-SCO port economic cooperation centre in Tianjin and 100 technological cooperation projects over the next three years. He presented the organisation as a priority platform for high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and called for deeper collaboration in the digital economy, green industries, energy and resources. These initiatives may sound bureaucratic compared with declarations about a new world order, but institutions, experts argue, are built through precisely such arrangements. Putin’s parallel proposal In Bishkek, Vladimir Putin took the financial argument further, describing the SCO as an independent and influential centre of the emerging multipolar world. Russia’s trade with SCO members, he said, had exceeded $400 billion in the previous year, while national currencies accounted for more than 98% of Russia’s transactions with them. He also backed the creation of an SCO development bank, arguing that it should be independent of financial systems belonging to states that use economic instruments as political weapons. For Russia, given its financial troubles, the push makes sense. Western sanctions have made access to the dollar-based financial system a challenge, and Moscow has spent years looking for ways to bypass it. But the same parallel financial arrangements, experts believe, can serve many countries that have no intention of confronting the West or the US. China, according to them, appears to be in a far stronger position than Russia to provide that financial system. Moscow has energy, military presence, natural resources and diplomatic reach, but its economic base is weak. China, on the other hand, has manufacturing capacity, capital, technology, a huge domestic market and an extensive network of commercial relationships across Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe. It produces much of the world’s solar equipment, dominates important parts of the EV and battery supply chains and has spent years financing projects and industrial zones through the Belt and Road Initiative. The SCO therefore gives Beijing something more useful than an anti-American alliance would, it provides a political space in which countries can increase cooperation without signing up to a common ideological programme or accepting China’s leadership as a condition of participation. On the other hand, the SCO cannot simply translate its impressive population and economic statistics into collective power. The body may be growing, but growth cannot be confused with long-term cohesion. That said, cohesion is not necessarily what Beijing needs at this point. The SCO operates according to a different logic and offers a structure of cooperation among countries that do not share the same interests on every issue, allowing them to build ties in particular areas without resolving their larger disagreements. That model, experts argue, fits the foreign policy of many middle powers better than the old demand to choose sides. And Turkey is perhaps the clearest example. Erdogan’s government wants to retain Nato membership and its relationship with Europe and the United States, while maintaining close economic and energy ties with Russia and expanding its connections across Central Asia and with China. Ankara, according to experts, has no obvious interest in exchanging one dependency for another, its ambition is to make sure that it has enough relationships to avoid being dependent on any single power. Writing off Washington Washington’s own policies have contributed to a shift that is leading nations, if not to abandon its orbit, then to move further away from it. In that environment, the SCO offers an increasingly useful option. The Trump administration’s 2026 National Defense Strategy places the defence of the US homeland first, calls for stronger deterrence of China in the Indo-Pacific and asks allies to assume greater responsibility for their own security. For Europe, a staunch US ally, the document shows a very scaled back US involvement in keeping the continent safe. The problem is that allies do not respond only to what Washington intends, they also respond to what they believe Washington might do next. And under Trump, at least for now, no one really knows what is coming next. If American commitments appear more conditional or transactional, governments have a reason to look for alternatives before they need them. That does not necessarily mean buying fewer American weapons or completely ending decades of security cooperation with the US. It can mean joining another organisation, signing another trade agreement, developing another payment system, cultivating another source of investment or building another diplomatic relationship and, in short, making the US-led architecture less of a necessity in the broader scheme. Experts argue that American power has benefited for decades from a network effect. The more countries that used US-led institutions, the more valuable and influential those institutions became. China is trying to build a similar web of relationships, but it does not need to create a Chinese version of every American institution. Instead, it can link the organisations and arrangements that are already taking shape around it. The SCO provides a platform for that political and security cooperation, the Belt and Road Initiative connects infrastructure and trade, BRICS offers a forum for economic coordination, bilateral currency arrangements can facilitate payments outside the dollar, and Chinese technology and industrial capacity can support alternative supply chains. None of these mechanisms, experts argue, need to replace the Western system on their own to weaken its dominance. Together, however, they give governments around the world more ways to operate outside the traditional Western system. Bishkek showed how those alternatives can extend beyond economics, creating space for political alignment as well. Iran, a US adversary, for example, had a seat at the table, and SCO members voiced concerns over the actions against it, including India, which had previously been more restrained in its response. That political alignment was also evident in how the leaders spoke about the international system itself. President Xi focused on global governance, the Global South and the need for a more representative international system. Uzbekistan’s President, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, went further, arguing that the wider SCO could contribute to a new global governance architecture while retaining the United Nations as the central coordinating institution. The rhetoric, experts argue, is meant to appeal to countries that have long complained that institutions created after the Second World War no longer reflect the distribution of economic and political power. All that said, none of this means that the US is about to disappear from the centre of global affairs. Washington can still, if not shape the future of global alliances, at least influence what they look like in the near term. It may be weaker and somewhat isolated, but it still has an extensive alliance network, considerable influence over the global financial system and other advantages that its main rival cannot easily replicate. According to experts, a less predictable American commitment encourages hedging, which creates demand for alternative institutions. China, unlike any other potential rival, has the economic potential to help build them. The contest ahead, experts argue, may therefore be less about which country convinces the world to join its camp than about which country becomes indispensable to the choices other countries make. China has spent years preparing for that competition, often through projects that appeared commercial rather than strategic at the time. The result is a growing web of ports, railways, factories, energy links, digital infrastructure, financial arrangements and diplomatic forums in which Beijing is already present. The SCO, Swain argues, is an important part of that effort. Its members, he explained, are not forming a Nato-style alliance but building flexible networks in which countries can cooperate on some issues while disagreeing on others. “Russia is using these relationships to escape Western isolation, China to expand its influence, while countries such as India and Turkey use them to hedge between competing centres of power,” the Sweden-based academic added. “The world is no longer organized around one unquestioned center of power,” Swain noted. The US-led order, he said, is weakening while new and often flexible partnerships are emerging across Asia and the Global South. The SCO’s Bishkek summit, Swain said, showed both the importance and the limitations of that shift. Multipolarity is emerging, but Swain sees it as “a transitional stage toward a more China-centered order” — a shift he believes is being accelerated by Trump’s erosion of American credibility and influence.

title: Coles named Zimbabwe women’s coach
author: Sports Desk
description: New Zealander takes charge ahead of five-match T20I series against South Africa
text: Zimbabwe Cricket has appointed Mark Coles as the substantive head coach of the Zimbabwe women’s national cricket team following a rigorous recruitment process. Coles brings extensive international coaching and high-performance experience to the role, having previously served as head coach of the Pakistan and Scotland women’s teams. He has also worked with Scotland’s men’s side, served as High Performance Manager at Cricket Papua New Guinea and held coaching consultancy roles in Australia. The experienced coach will begin his tenure ahead of Zimbabwe’s five-match T20I series against South Africa, which starts at Queens Sports Club on Friday. His appointment comes at a pivotal moment for Zimbabwe women’s cricket following the team’s historic entry into the ICC Women’s Championship earlier this year under an interim coaching set-up. Zimbabwe opened their Women’s Championship campaign with away assignments against New Zealand and Pakistan. The team will continue its four-year campaign with tours of India and Bangladesh, while also hosting South Africa, West Indies, Sri Lanka and Ireland. The ICC Women’s Championship serves as the qualification pathway for the 2029 Women’s Cricket World Cup. Coles will work with an established backroom team comprising Rangarirai Manyande as assistant coach for batting, Trevor Phiri as fielding coach, Faith Dube as strength and conditioning coach, Farai Mabasa as physiotherapist, Keith Kulinga as analyst and Mary-Anne Musonda as team manager. Zimbabwe Cricket has also retained Travor Garwe as head coach of the Under-19 women’s national team. He will be assisted by Nonhlanhla Kamuteku, who will oversee batting, bowling coach Malcolm Chikuwa and team manager Susan Kudzibatira. The board also confirmed the Zimbabwe women’s selection panel, with Julia Chibhabha continuing as convener. Emily Jinjika and Thandowenkosi Mlilo remain selectors, while Ishmael Senzere joins as the fourth member of the panel. Zimbabwe Cricket chairman Tavengwa Mukuhlani said the appointments would help create a sustainable high-performance structure for the women’s game. “Women’s cricket is entering an exciting new chapter in Zimbabwe following our admission into the ICC Women’s Championship and it is vital that we have the right people in place to guide that journey,” Mukuhlani said. “Mark Coles brings extensive international coaching and high-performance experience, as well as a strong understanding of the demands of the women’s game.” Mukuhlani added that the board believed the new coaching and support structure could help Zimbabwe build a competitive side and establish a pathway for sustained success. “Together with the technical and support staff appointed across our senior and Under-19 structures, we believe he will help us build a competitive team and establish a clear pathway for sustained success,” he said. “We are confident that this group will help Zimbabwe women’s cricket continue to grow and compete strongly on the international stage.”

title: Sri Lanka edge Bangladesh to reach Asia Cup semi-finals
author: Sports Desk
description: Samarawickrama’s unbeaten 48 steers Sri Lanka to a four-wicket win
text: Harshitha Samarawickrama held her nerve before launching a late attack as Sri Lanka overcame Bangladesh by four wickets on Sunday to book their place in the Asia Cup semi-finals. Chasing 115, Sri Lanka suffered an early setback when Marufa Akter dismissed captain Chamari Athapaththu for one before removing Imesha Dulani for 12. Sultana Khatun then bowled Sanjana Kavindi for nine, while Vishmi Gunaratne fell to Ritu Moni and Kavisha Dilhari was run out as Bangladesh tightened the pressure. Harshitha steadied the innings alongside Nilakshika Silva, keeping Sri Lanka within reach of the target through a tense middle period. Bangladesh appeared to regain control when Marufa returned to dismiss Nilakshika for 18, leaving Sri Lanka needing 33 from the final four overs. Harshitha responded by attacking Ritu Moni, hitting a four and six in the 18th over. She added 11 in the next over, including another six from the final ball, to put Sri Lanka firmly in control. They completed the chase with four wickets and four balls remaining, with Harshitha unbeaten on 48. Earlier, Bangladesh made a brisk start after being put into bat, with Juairiya Ferdous and Dilara Akter taking the score to around 30 without loss after five overs. Sugandika Kumari broke the opening stand by dismissing Ferdous, while Chamudi Praboda removed Dilara for 25. Kavisha Dilhari then trapped Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana Joty leg before wicket for four before Sobhana Mostary offered resistance with 34. Praboda eventually stumped Mostary and later dismissed Shorna Akter to finish with three for 21. Bangladesh crossed 100 but struggled to accelerate in the closing overs, scoring just 12 runs between the 17th and 19th overs before Fahima Khatun’s late hitting took them to 114. Sri Lanka’s victory gives them four wins from four group matches and a place in the semi-finals. Bangladesh will face the United Arab Emirates next, knowing a victory could keep their hopes of reaching the knockout stage alive.

title: Labuschagne named in Australia squad
author: AFP
description: Right-hander has not scored a century since 2023
text: Out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne can "still make a positive contribution", chief Australia selector George Bailey said Monday, after the struggling batsman was thrown a lifeline for the Test tour of South Africa. Number three Labuschagne has failed to score a century since 2023 and flopped again in two home Tests against Bangladesh last month with scores of one, 31 and four. He was subsequently axed from Australia's squad for three one-dayers in Zimbabwe and another three in South Africa preceding the Tests. But selectors opted against a red-ball change for what will be the team's first Test series in South Africa since the infamous "Sandpapergate" ball-tampering scandal in 2018. "(We're) not shying away from the fact that we'd like some more runs from Marn... but we're also confident that he can still make a positive contribution to that squad," Bailey said. "Our batting group in its entirety, not just Marn, probably hasn't been functioning as successfully as we would like." Asked if the South Africa series would be Labuschagne's last chance, Bailey dodged the question. "No, I wouldn't say that. But again, it's a hypothetical, isn't it?" he said. Cooper Connolly, Matthew Kuhnemann and Michael Neser were also included in a 16-man squad which was otherwise unchanged form the last Bangladesh Test. All-rounder Connolly's selection is another indication that the 23-year-old is seen as a long-term prospect while Kuhnemann was preferred to Todd Murphy as the second spinner behind Nathan Lyon. Neser, who like Labuschagne was born in South Africa, provides back-up for the pace trio of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc. Bailey said Connolly was primarily chosen for his batting, most likely as a middle order option but potentially as high as three. "His overall development will continue to expand his ability to bat in a range of positions," he said. Australia travel to Durban for the first Test on October 9 before the series moves to Gqeberha and Cape Town. Only Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood, Lyon, Steve Smith and Matt Renshaw survive from their last Test series in South Africa, when Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were all sent home in shame. Smith was banned for a year and sacked as captain after conspiring to alter the ball using sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town, while the now-retired Warner, considered the ringleader, was suspended for 12 months and stripped of all leadership roles. title: Fire breaks out in Bannu hospital, no casualties reported
author: Nasruminallah
description: Blaze in Urology Ward initially caused by electric spark, controlled within 10 minutes by Rescue 1122
text: A fire broke out in the Urology Ward of Khalifa Gul Nawaz Hospital in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Bannu on Monday, but patients were safely evacuated and the blaze was brought under control within minutes, Rescue 1122 said. Rescue 1122 Bannu said its fire rescue team reached the hospital about five minutes after receiving an emergency call and immediately began firefighting and rescue operations. The blaze was brought under control within about 10 minutes using modern firefighting techniques, the rescue service said. “All patients present in the ward were safely evacuated to a secure location,” Rescue 1122 said, adding that no loss of life was reported. According to Medical Teaching Institute (MTI) Bannu spokesperson Mohammad Noman, the fire was initially caused by an electrical spark. The spokesperson added that hospital staff and rescue teams immediately evacuated patients and began efforts to extinguish the fire, while Rescue 1122 was informed without delay. “The timely and effective response of the hospital staff prevented the fire from spreading further and helped bring the situation under control,” Noman said. He also noted that MTI Bannu staff had recently received special training in firefighting, handling fire emergencies and responding quickly to such incidents following the fire at Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS). “The training was put into practical use during today’s incident,” Noman said. Read: Fire safety crackdown puts fuel stations on the block He added that the staff’s training, rapid response and coordination with rescue teams had played a key role in preventing what could have been a major accident. On August 26, 14 newborns were killed after a fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital at PIMS, triggering widespread outrage and demands from people and political parties for action against those responsible. The fire at PIMS prompted authorities across Pakistan to review fire-safety arrangements at healthcare facilities and other public buildings. The tragedy also led to increased inspections and enforcement in Islamabad. The CDA sealed three buildings over fire-safety violations and later conducted a fire drill at Parliament House, while the Islamabad High Court sought a government report on fire-safety audits and mandatory NOCs for buildings in the capital. In Sindh, a fire-safety assessment of 22 government hospitals found widespread shortcomings, including a lack of fire alarms, sprinklers and adequate firefighting equipment. The provincial chief secretary subsequently gave departments 15 days to certify that public buildings under their control complied with fire-safety regulations. Punjab also ordered fresh safety checks following the fire at PIMS. The provincial health regulator directed public and private hospitals to strengthen emergency preparedness, conduct fire-safety audits and hold regular drills, while Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz ordered reviews of firefighting equipment, emergency exits, hydrants and electrical systems at public health facilities.

title: Barca thrash Valencia
author: AFP
description: Yamal scores twice to maintain their 100 percent start in La Liga
text: Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100 percent start in La Liga. The reigning champions moved two points clear at the top of La Liga, after Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday. Unbeaten Alaves rose to second place with a thumping 5-2 victory over Osasuna. As well as Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick's swaggering Barca on a hot afternoon on Spain's east coast. Yamal did not take part in the team training session on Saturday after a knock but showed no signs of it during a dazzling display against Carlos Corberan's side. Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia's fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium. Los Che are bottom and yet to win this season. "We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant and this is what I want from the team," said Flick. "We stay calm and then if it's possible to score we try to do it -- it was a fantastic game for us. "Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it's perfect then you can stop working." Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Lopez dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star. The 19-year-old slammed home at the near post for what he thought was Barca's second goal but the goal was disallowed for a tight offside after a VAR review. Lopez netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up. Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric Garcia had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with team-mate Rodri's shoulder, on the midfielder's first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City. Yamal fired narrowly wide and Lopez struck the post as Flick's side continued to dominate. Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia made a smart save to thwart Arnaut Danjuma at his near post before the break. Raphinha, starting again as the team's centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Lopez fed him. title: Palestinian football marks return
author: AFP
description: The tournament features over 200 teams from the West Bank, Gaza and refugee camps in Lebanon
text: Palestinian sports commentator Khalil Jadallah has spent the past three years mourning the athletes killed in the Gaza war. As Palestinian football officially resumed this week, his return to the stadium proved bittersweet. Palestinian professional sports were brought to a halt after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel and the ensuing war in Gaza, in which 1,014 Palestinian athletes were killed, according to the Palestinian Football Association's tally. On Friday, Jadallah was back at Faisal Al-Husseini Stadium in Al-Ram in the West Bank to call the opening match of the first tournament organised by the association in three years. "We lost players... fans, administrators and referees," Jadallah told AFP. '1,000 Martyrs Cup' The football association named the comeback tournament -- which includes over 200 teams from the occupied West Bank, Gaza, and refugee camps in Lebanon -- the "1,000 Martyrs Cup". Throughout the war, Palestinian football authorities have accused Israel of killing football players and damaging Gaza's sporting infrastructure. Israel has said 12 Palestinian football figures that it killed in Gaza, including a FIFA-registered referee, were members of militant groups, an allegation the football association has rejected. Large numbers of Palestinian security forces were deployed for the event, an unusual sight in the town more accustomed to Israeli military raids. Before the game, pitting Jabal Al-Mukaber Club against Shabab Al-Khaleel SC, children carried a Palestinian flag wrapped to resemble a dead body, before unfurling it across the centre circle as a band played the Palestinian national anthem. The sport authority also unveiled a memorial bearing the names of the killed Palestinian athletes outside the stadium, which stands in Al-Ram, not far from the West Bank separation barrier. "Football has become more important than politics today," he said. "The proof of that is the following the World Cup has had." "Sport in general is the culture of the people," he added, saying that Palestinians had "the right to practice sport normally and in all its forms, not just football". At the 10-minute, 14-second mark, the referee ordered the game to stop for a minute of silence for the dead before the crowd grew loud again. "Football returns to Palestine," read electronic screens around the stadium. Thousands of mainly young people attended the game, with families, women and children seated in a separate section. Maysan Suleiman, a 35-year-old from Al-Ram, said she came to commemorate "the martyrs". 'Football returns to Palestine' "I don't support either team," she said. "I came to support the idea (of the tournament) itself. After all, they're all sons of Palestine." The tournament opened simultaneously in Gaza, where Israeli strikes have left much of the territory in ruins and some football fields have been turned into makeshift camps for those displaced by the war. The opening match there was held in Deir al-Balah between Khadamat Rafah and Shabab Rafah as fans sat on plastic chairs around the small field lined with palm trees. "Football represented life for us before the war, and after the war the lives of players stopped altogether," said Khalil Matar, a Khadamat Rafah player. Matar said holding the cup simultaneously in the West Bank, Gaza and refugee camps in Lebanon reflected "national unity" for Palestinians. But the West Bank teams are set to face major logistical hurdles as they travel between cities and Israeli military checkpoints in the occupied territory. "Still, we're determined to continue sporting activities and developing our young people," said Abdullah Abu Ghassan of the Shabab Jaba team competing in the tournament.

title: Infantino to run for FIFA presidency
author: AFP
description: The 56-year-old Swiss seeks to stay on until 2031 amid criticism
text: Gianni Infantino will stand in next March's FIFA presidential election, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the World Cup, football's global governing body announced Sunday. "The FIFA President announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027," a FIFA spokesperson said. "Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election." The 56-year-old Swiss has taken a pummelling since the announcement in late July of his short-lived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to bring private investment into FIFA events. But now for the first time since the plan became public, FIFA has reiterated Infantino's intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year's elections. Should he be re-elected, he will continue to serve as head of world football until 2031. Infantino is in Poland for the Women's Under-20 World Cup, but refused to answer queries about his future when questioned by journalists on Saturday. European body UEFA has accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" over the scheme and was the ringleader of the initial fightback to the announcement, including threatening to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups, if it was not shelved. But it has also found solid support from North American body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino -- UEFA boss Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out. Montagliani, a FIFA vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed FIFA's purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss. However, Infantino is not without friends -- 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football's governing body CAF and South America's CONMEBOL also supportive. As the only declared candidate so far for the election due to take place in March 2027, Infantino will need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to FIFA to extend his term of office, which began in 2016 and was renewed in 2023. Candidate nominations for next year's election must be submitted by November 18.

title: Six killed in Delhi building collapse, rescuers search through rubble
author: Reuters
description: NEW DELHI: At least six people were killed and several others injured after a building housing students in India’s capital Delhi, collapsed, the city-state’s chief minister said on Monday, as rescuers searched for anyone still trapped in the debris. The building, located in the southern part of the city near colleges and universities, had a basement and five upper floors and was being used to house students, local media reported. “It is certain that there was water in the building’s basement, and due to accumulation of water, due to ongoing repair work, the old building collapsed,” Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta told reporters. Visuals after the collapse on Sunday showed heaps of bricks and broken concrete pillars at the site, with police, rescuers and locals searching for trapped survivors. Six people, who were taken to a nearby hospital after being rescued alive, were stable, Gupta said. Fire in Delhi hotel kills at least 21, police say Police were searching for the owner of the building, television channels reported. Building collapses occur frequently in India, especially in crowded urban neighbourhoods where unauthorised construction is widespread and law enforcement is weak.

title: Kremlin says it does not rule out restart of peace talks with Ukraine and US
author: Reuters
description: MOSCOW: The Kremlin said on Monday that it did not rule out the resumption of peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States, but said it was too early to say when and where such talks might take place. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov made the comments when asked about a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner who are trying to breathe new life into stalled talks designed to find a way to end the war in Ukraine. “As for the resumption of the trilateral format, you heard the statement from Kyiv yesterday. Mr Kushner made such statements. We, too, do not rule out the resumption of this trilateral format, but it is still too early to speak of the venue and exact dates,” Peskov told reporters when asked if three-way peace talks would resume. Peskov, who declined to discuss in detail the content of the latest U.S. peace proposals or what the hardest outstanding issues to solve are, said the Kremlin did not rule out a phone call between Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump to discuss the U.S. envoys’ trip. title: Pietersen back in England colours as mentor in build-up to 2027 World Cup
author: Reuters
description: Kevin Pietersen will return to the England setup for the first time since retiring in 2014 after being appointed specialist mentor to the white-ball teams ahead of next year’s World Cup in southern Africa, the England Cricket Board said on Monday. The former Ashes and T20 World Cup-winning batter will join Brendon McCullum’s coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka coming up later this month, working alongside Marcus Trescothick, Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor. The 46-year-old Pietersen’s involvement extends through England’s white-ball tours to Australia and South Africa and the home series against Pakistan and New Zealand next summer, before the one-day international (ODI) World Cup itself. “I am immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa. Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment,” Pietersen said. “We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential. “To be a part of Brendon’s think tank over the next 12 months is a fantastic opportunity, and I cannot wait to get started.” An explosive middle-order batter, Pietersen scored nearly 14,000 runs across all three formats for England, who last won the ODI World Cup in 2019 on home soil. However, his England career ended controversially in 2014 in the aftermath of the 5-0 Ashes whitewash in Australia, amid reported tensions within the dressing room and between the batsman and team management. Pietersen was the team’s top scorer in the series and, despite remaining keen to play for England, was told he was no longer part of the plans, bringing an acrimonious end to his international career. Pietersen’s South African upbringing could prove particularly valuable as England prepare for the World Cup which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2027. “I’m particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him,” McCullum said. “KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players. “We’ve always respected each other and had a strong appreciation for what the other brings to the game, so I’m really looking forward to working together.”

title: Alternative-fuel car sales in India top petrol on cost, E20 concerns, dealers' body says
author: Reuters
description: Sales of alternative-fuel passenger vehicles outpaced petrol-powered cars in India in August for the first time, an auto dealers’ body said on Monday, as the Middle East war raised oil prices and a public backlash against higher-ethanol-content fuel simmered. Alternative-fuel models, including compressed natural gas, hybrid and electric models, accounted for nearly 42% of passenger-vehicle sales, while petrol vehicles stood at about 41%, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), which represents dealers of major car and two-wheeler makers. “This shift was bound to happen,” Sai Giridhar, FADA vice president, told Reuters. While E20-related concerns may have initially accelerated buyers’ move away from petrol, the trend was being sustained by a wider choice of alternative-fuel models, improved EV range and a gradual expansion of charging infrastructure, he said. The world’s third-largest car market’s transition to E20 petrol, which contains 20% ethanol, from E10 is aimed at reducing reliance on imported crude but has drawn criticism from owners of older vehicles, who are concerned that the blend could reduce fuel economy. India’s E20 petrol rollout pushes buyers towards alternative-fuel vehicles The government earlier dismissed the backlash, calling it “wild claims” and asking people to not “fall for the rage bait”. Record august sales India’s automobile retail sales rose 17.5% year-on-year in August to 2.4 million, a record for the month. This was despite leading auto companies rolling out price hikes this year to cope with elevated input costs. Giridhar, however, warned that further price hikes risked eroding gains from last year’s tax reforms introduced to fuel consumption. The country’s largest carmaker, Maruti Suzuki India on Monday said it will raise prices of select models by up to 20,000 rupees ($211.80) from September, its third hike since May. India is heading into its annual festive season, a period that typically spurs big-ticket purchases. Giridhar said despite inflationary pressures and price increases, dealers remain optimistic about sales. Passenger-vehicle inventory increased by five days from end-July levels to about 38–40 days, FADA said.

title: Indian central bank unloaded at least $8 billion last week to anchor rupee, bankers say
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: The Reserve Bank of India ramped up its FX intervention last week, selling at least $8 billion to bolster the rupee, six bankers said, as a deluge of policy-driven dollar inflows gave the central bank more room to support the currency. The bankers estimated the RBI’s market presence at between $8 billion and $15 billion, with sustained interventions helping lift the rupee to an over two-month high of 94.2850 on September 3. The central bank’s discounted hedging facility for overseas borrowings by state-run firms and banks, alongside a free-of-cost hedging facility for banks to raise overseas FX deposits have drawn in more than $136 billion. These inflows have likely given the RBI more room to conduct sizeable interventions, one of the bankers familiar with the RBI’s market interventions said, though their estimates of the scale of dollar sales varied. This banker estimated the RBI’s dollar sales last week at around $15 billion. Another banker at a state-run lender quantified it at nearly $10 billion to $11 billion for the week to September 4, at least three times the amount in the previous week. India’s RBI likely used dollar deposit surge to cut record FX forward book, economists say All the bankers requested anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to the media. The RBI did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment. The RBI’s dollar-selling interventions also drain rupee liquidity from the banking system, which had recently hit a record high. Excess liquidity can push interbank borrowing costs below the policy rate, blunting monetary policy transmission. FX war chest Through August 21, India’s FX reserves stood at an all-time peak of $740.8 billion, while J.P. Morgan said that figure has since likely risen past $750 billion. “Increased near-term ammunition, in turn, explains the more aggressive intervention by the RBI in recent days, to try and push the rupee stronger, and bring exporters into the market,” the firm said in a Friday note. Persistent rupee weakness concerns have kept hedging flows skewed toward dollars, with importers stepping up forward purchases to guard against depreciation while exporters hold back on dollar sales, waiting for better levels, bankers said. The rupee’s rebound, from a low of 96.96 in May, is unlikely to mark the start of a broader appreciation cycle, analysts say. Goldman Sachs sees the currency in a narrow range in the medium term, saying that stronger external balances are unlikely to lead to a sustained upside. It expects the RBI to use future inflows to pare its forward FX liabilities, which three other economists estimate have likely crossed $200 billion.

Morgan said that figure has since likely risen past $750 billion. “Increased near-term ammunition, in turn, explains the more aggressive intervention by the RBI in recent days, to try and push the rupee stronger, and bring exporters into the market,” the firm said in a Friday note. title: Saudi PIF launches firm to develop tourism, residential area on Gulf coast
author: Reuters
description: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) said on Monday it has launched a real estate company to develop tourism on the Al-Khafji coastline on the Gulf, as the sovereign wealth fund pours billions of dollars into infrastructure projects. Saudi Arabia is investing in infrastructure as part of its plans to transform the economy and reduce the kingdom’s reliance on oil revenue. The new real estate company, called the Gulf Coast Development Company, in partnership with the private sector, will create an integrated tourist and residential destination on the Al-Khafji area bordering Kuwait on the Gulf. The project, spanning around 20 square kilometres (7.7 sq. miles) with a 10-km waterfront, is expected to accommodate more than 16,000 housing units alongside hotels and other commercial facilities. There was no immediate clarity on the value of the project, whose first phase is scheduled to be completed in 2030. Saudi Arabia real estate gigaproject developer replaces chief executive PIF’s gross assets under management (AUM) totalled 3.396 trillion riyals ($904.54 billion) in 2025 compared to 3.434 trillion riyals the previous year. Local investments represented 76% of total AUM in 2025. PIF, which is spearheading the economic transformation plan, recently shifted strategy, moving away from some investments, including scaling back so-called infrastructure giga-projects in the kingdom. Saudi Arabia is also developing its Red Sea coast, where PIF’s firm Red Sea Global is planning to open 27 resorts by year-end.

title: India's vegetable oil imports strain port storage, delaying unloading
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: India’s aggressive vegetable-oil buying has led to congestion at major ports, delaying vessel unloading by as much as 10 days as shore tanks fill and refiners struggle to clear incoming cargo, industry officials told Reuters. The congestion is expected to prompt Indian refiners to scale back purchases of soyoil and palm oil for October shipments, potentially boosting inventories in top producers Indonesia, Malaysia and Argentina and weighing on benchmark palm oil futures and soyoil futures. “Shore tanks are full, and the lack of storage space is delaying the unloading of vessels carrying edible oils,” said Sandeep Bajoria, chief executive of vegetable oil brokerage Sunvin Group. “At least nine vessels carrying 300,000 metric tons of edible oils are waiting to discharge at Kandla port.” Kandla, in the western state of Gujarat, is India’s largest gateway for edible oil imports, handling nearly a third of the country’s total arrivals. India’s soyoil imports hit record high in August and palm six-month peak, dealers say Haldia, the second-biggest gateway for edible oil imports on the east coast, is also facing congestion, although to a lesser extent than Kandla, dealers said. The South Asian country’s edible oil imports in August jumped to an 11-month high of 1.54 million tons and a similar quantity is likely to be imported in September as well, they said. As edible oils for prompt delivery were cheaper than contracts for later months, Indian refiners increased their purchases for August and September delivery, causing a glut at ports, said Rajesh Patel, managing partner at trader GGN Research in Rajkot city in the western state of Gujarat. Refiners imported heavily in anticipation of strong festival demand, but consumption has not increased as expected, slowing the movement of cargo from port-based refineries, Patel said. India celebrates a series of festivals between August and November, when demand for edible oils typically peaks. The build-up in inventories is now prompting refiners to reduce purchases for October to December shipment, Bajoria said. India sources most of its palm oil from Indonesia and Malaysia, while soyoil and sunflower oil are imported mainly from Argentina, Brazil, Russia and Ukraine.

title: Indian rupee ends flat, hemmed in by RBI intervention, oil pangs
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: The Indian rupee traded in a narrow range on Monday, wedged between sustained market intervention by the Reserve Bank of India and a rise in oil prices as strikes on vessels sailing through the Strait of Hormuz stoked worries over energy flows. The Indian rupee closed at 94.4850 per dollar, unchanged from its closing level on Friday. The currency spent the session in about a 10-paisa trading range with bankers pointing to consistent dollar sales from state-run banks, most likely on behalf of the RBI. The intervention echoed the pattern traders have seen over the last two weeks, where consistent central bank dollar selling anchored the rupee. Bankers estimate that the RBI sold at least $8 billion to bolster the rupee last week. The dollar sales have helped the rupee hold its ground even as oil prices continue to linger near 6-week highs. Brent crude oil futures were last at $96.6 per barrel. Goldman Sachs sees them rising to as much as $120 per barrel if attacks on shipping increase. Iran said it will announce a new restricted zone in the Persian Gulf in the coming days, along with maps of a new shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts at ING reckon that higher energy prices and limited current market pricing of interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve could lend some support to the dollar in the near term. Traders have priced in a roughly 57% chance the Federal Reserve will hike rates this month, following stronger-than-expected labour market data. Market focus now turns to inflation data on Friday. On the day, the dollar index was down 0.2% to 98.9 while Asian currencies traded mixed. Indian stocks fell 0.6% even as MSCI’s gauge of Asian stocks jumped nearly 2%, boosted by a rise in stocks linked to the artificial intelligence theme.

title: Copper heads towards record high, focus on tight supplies outside US
author: Reuters
description: LONDON: Copper prices headed towards a record high on Monday, as the prospect of shortages outside the U.S. spurred buying, while the softer dollar reinforced positive sentiment. Traders said a U.S. holiday meant volumes were likely to be muted, but added that focus was firmly on copper and zinc. Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.1% at $14,430 a metric ton at 0931 GMT, the highest since the all-time peak of $14,527.50 hit in January. Traders and producers have been shipping copper to the U.S. since President Donald Trump mooted import tariffs in February last year. Comex copper stocks stood at a record high of 766,795 short tons, or 695,624 metric tons. Elevated premiums or backwardations for nearby contracts against longer-dated forwards have attracted some copper back to the LME. But cancelled warrants or metal earmarked for delivery at 51% indicate more than 121,000 tons of copper are likely to leave the LME system over the coming days and weeks. The premium for the cash over the three-month forward climbed above $430 a ton in the middle of August, the highest since 2021. It closed around $74 on Friday. Another sign of tight supplies outside the U.S. is stocks in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange at 63,000 tons, down 85% since the middle of March and at their lowest since January 2024. Copper prices on ShFE are also in backwardation suggesting the industry in top consumer China is also worried about supplies. Elsewhere, zinc, supported by tight supplies and low LME stocks was up 0.8% at $3,976 a ton, close to the $3,990 a ton hit at the start of the month, the highest since May 2022. A softer U.S. currency, which makes dollar-priced metals cheaper for holders of other currencies, supported base metals overall. Aluminium was up 0.1% at $3,298, lead rose 0.3% to $1,914, tin gained 0.3% to $55,030, while nickel slipped 0.5% to $16,755.

title: Palm extends gains, hits two-week high on stronger Dalian palm olein
author: Reuters
description: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian palm oil futures climbed to a two-week high on Monday, extending gains for a second consecutive session, supported by stronger Dalian palm olein prices. The benchmark palm oil contract for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange was up 50 ringgit, or 1.01%, at 4,979 ringgit ($1,231.21) a metric ton, the highest closing price since August 21. “Strength in Dalian palm olein provided support to crude palm oil prices, keeping the market in positive territory towards the midday close,” a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said. Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract rose 0.31%, while its palm oil contract added 1.39%. The Chicago Board of Trade is closed for a public holiday. Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market. Oil prices were near six-week highs as tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas kept crude oil flows in the Middle East low. Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock. The ringgit, palm’s currency of trade, weakened 0.07% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies. Meanwhile, India’s aggressive vegetable-oil buying has led to congestion at major ports, delaying vessel unloading by as much as 10 days as shore tanks fill and refiners struggle to clear incoming cargo, industry officials told Reuters.

title: Indian stocks slip to six-week low as IT slides, oil worries mount
author: Reuters
description: Indian shares slipped to their lowest levels in six weeks on Monday, pressured by IT stocks, as escalating tensions in the Middle East and rising expectations of a U.S. rate hike dented risk sentiment. The Nifty 50 ended 0.5% lower at 23,779.15 and the BSE Sensex shed 0.5% to 76,132.81. Nifty and Sensex have already shed 2.7% and 2.5%, respectively, over the past four weeks as higher oil prices and global bond yields pressured equities. “Market instability with a downward bias will continue in the short term due to periodic conflicts and higher crude oil prices,” said G Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at Equinomics Research. Weaker rainfall and liquidity pressures from a rush of IPOs could also weigh on markets despite supportive domestic macroeconomic conditions, he added. On Monday, fourteen of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The IT sub-index fell 2.3% tracking broader weakness after stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data reinforced expectations of a September Federal Reserve rate hike. Higher U.S. rates could curb client spending and weigh on Indian IT firms that generate a significant share of their revenue from the United States. Meanwhile, Brent crude futures rose 0.6% to $96.8 a barrel after U.S. and Iran struck vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas in the latest escalation of Mideast tensions, which could further disrupt energy supply and intensify inflation fears. Broader small-caps were flat, while mid-caps fell 0.5%. Among individual stocks, PVR Inox slid 6.1% on reports that an internal investigation flagged alleged 2 billion rupee kickbacks by an executive linked to cinema property projects. The company said preliminary examination did not indicate any evidence of kickbacks. Shares of Zee Entertainment fell 6.4% after media reports said India’s premier investigating agency filed an FIR against founder and Chairman Emeritus Subhash Chandra and some other individuals for allegedly defrauding LIC Housing Finance. Chandra’s office did not immediately respond to a request for clarification.

title: Bank of Maharashtra, Canara Bank eye dollar debt issuance this month, bankers say
author: Reuters
description: MUMBAI: Two Indian state-run lenders, Canara Bank and Bank of Maharashtra, are set to raise $500 million each through the sale of U.S. dollar-denominated bonds over the next few days, two merchant bankers said on Monday. Both the lenders will look to raise funds through a sale of three-year or five-year papers, or a combination of both, under the central bank’s concessional swap window, which lowers the cost of hedging the risk of unfavourable currency moves, the bankers added. title: Rupee registers gain against US dollar
author: Recorder Report
description: The Pakistani rupee extended its marginal gains against the US dollar on Monday. The local unit closed the day at 277.40, a gain of Re0.01 against the greenback. On Friday , the Pakistani rupee settled at 277.41 against the dollar. Internationally, the US dollar was on shaky ground on Monday, despite a ramp-up in US rate hike bets as Middle East tensions raised the prospect of broader inflationary pressures that could force global central banks to tighten policy in tandem. A shift in sentiment towards the Japanese yen and worries about ever-growing US debt and policy uncertainties also weighed on the greenback. Moves in currencies were largely subdued in early Asia trade with US markets closed for a holiday, though the dollar struggled to sustain a brief lift it received from Friday’s blowout U.S. jobs report. The euro was up marginally at $1.1618, while sterling was little changed at $1.3519. Against a basket of currencies, the dollar fell 0.07% to 99.09, not far from its recent low of 98.558. Traders moved to price in a roughly 57% chance the Federal Reserve will hike rates this month in the wake of the nonfarm payrolls release, with much now depending on Friday’s inflation data. Oil prices were near six-week highs on Monday, creeping closer to $100 a barrel, as tit-for-tat strikes between the U.S. and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas kept crude oil flows in the Middle East low. Brent crude futures rose $1.19, or 1.2% to $97.47 a barrel by 1214 GMT, having earlier hit their highest point since July 24 at $97.93. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude also hovered near a recent six-week high at $92.26 a barrel, up 78 cents. title: Defence Day event in Karachi honours fallen soldiers and military heroes
author: Press Release
description: A Defence Day event at Iqra University has paid tribute to Pakistan’s armed forces and national heroes, while urging young people to contribute to the country’s development. The event, organised by the Sindh government’s Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, marked 6 September, commemorating the 1965 war between Pakistan and India. Speakers recalled the events of the 1965 war; the role of the armed forces and the sacrifices made in the defence of the country. A panel discussion featured retired military officers including Vice Admiral Shah Sohail Masood, Air Vice Marshal Usaid-ur-Rehman Usmani, Brigadier Syed Karrar Hussain Shah, Colonel Mukhtar Butt, Squadron Leader Nafees Ahmed Rabbani and Commander Dr Muhammad Tahir. The panellists discussed the historical context of the 1965 war and the contribution of the armed forces, while encouraging students to play a constructive role in Pakistan’s future. Director General of the Press Information Department Mrs. Iram Tanveer, attended as guest of honour and paid tribute to those who had lost their lives in the defence of the country. Munawar Ali Mahesar, Sindh secretary for sports and youth affairs, said Defence Day represented more than the commemoration of a historical event, describing it as a reminder of national unity, sacrifice, determination and patriotism. He urged young people to contribute to national development through education, skills and responsible conduct. Additional Secretary Dr Asad Ishaq also addressed the gathering, while Syed Habibullah, deputy director of the Directorate of Youth Affairs Sindh, said the department sought to use national commemorations to familiarise younger generations with Pakistan’s history and the sacrifices associated with its creation and defence. Certificates were presented to students at the conclusion of the event, while commemorative shields were given to speakers and other participants. The organizers said the event was intended to strengthen young people’s understanding of national history and encourage them to contribute to the country as responsible and active citizens.

title: Third-degree fire breaks out at factory in Landhi Export Processing Zone
author: Baseer Ahmed
description: A third-degree fire broke out at a factory in the Landhi Export Processing Zone on Monday, following which Rescue 1122 teams, fire brigade vehicles and ambulances were deployed for rescue activities. Rescue 1122 Spokesperson Hassaan Khan said the emergency response team was dispatched to the site immediately after the Central Command and Control Centre received information about the blaze. Fire could not be doused despite hours long firefighting efforts. No casualties were reported, and all workers were safely evacuated from the factory, the spokesperson told Business Recorder . Three people were temporarily trapped inside the building and suffered suffocation due to thick smoke, but rescue teams safely brought them out as well, he added. The fire later spread to an adjoining factory, as per the Rescue 1122 spokesperson. The official said a portion of the factory building collapsed due to the fire, while rescue teams were present at the scene and operations were under way. A thick cloud of smoke from the blaze severely reduced visibility inside the building, complicating rescue efforts. Rescue teams were working to control the fire and assess the situation. Meanwhile, the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KW&SC) said the fire brigade had requested immediate assistance. On the directives of KW&SC Chief Executive Officer Ahmed Ali Siddiqui, emergency measures were activated at the Landhi and Sherpao hydrants, the corporation’s spokesperson said. Water tankers were promptly dispatched to the site, while the in-charge of the hydrants cell remained in contact with fire brigade and rescue officials. The CEO’s focal person for hydrants cell operations was personally monitoring the response, the spokesperson said. He added that an uninterrupted water supply was being ensured to the fire brigade during firefighting operations. “The water corporation would continue supplying water tankers until the fire was completely extinguished,” he said, adding that the corporation was extending all possible cooperation to rescue agencies to protect citizens’ lives and property.

title: Japan to provide $16.4mn to strengthen flood protection in Pakistan
author: BR Web Desk
description: Japan has agreed to provide Pakistan a $16.4 million grant to strengthen flood protection infrastructure in Sindh, with the project focused on improving and reinforcing the Old Abad Bund along the right bank of the Indus River in Larkana, Sindh. The development came during a ceremony between the Government of Pakistan and the Government of Japan on Monday, which signed the Exchange of Notes, Record of Discussion and Grant Agreement for the “Project for Flood Protection and Dike Improvement on Indus River in Sindh Province”, aimed at strengthening flood protection infrastructure and enhancing the resilience of vulnerable communities in Sindh. According to a statement, the agreements were signed and exchanged by Muhammad Humair Karim Kidwai, Secretary, Ministry of Economic Affairs and Akamatsu Shuichi, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan on behalf of their respective governments. Under the agreement, the Government of Japan is providing a grant of JPY 2.58 billion, approximately $16.4 million, for the implementation of the project. The project will focus on the improvement and strengthening of the Old Abad Bund in Larkana, along the right bank of the Indus River. The Secretary, Ministry of Economic Affairs, expressed appreciation to the government and the people of Japan for their continued friendship, generous development assistance and steadfast commitment to Pakistan’s socio-economic development. He also acknowledged the longstanding role of the Japanese government as a valued development partner and appreciated JICA’s technical expertise, knowledge and continued engagement with Pakistan across various sectors. Akamatsu Shuichi, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Japan to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, assured the commitment of his government to work closely with the Government of Pakistan to further strengthen the friendly ties and bilateral cooperation. Sugawara Takayuki, senior representative of JICA, appreciated the Government of Sindh and the Government of Pakistan for bringing the project to a signing stage and indicated JICA’s commitment towards strengthening flood protection infrastructure in flood-prone areas of Sindh.

title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanese town kill 11, state news agency says
author: Reuters
description: BEIRUT: Israeli strikes on a southern Lebanese town early on Monday killed at least 11 people including two children and two medics, Lebanon’s state news agency said. Israel has intensified its bombardment of south Lebanon in recent days despite a June ceasefire that was meant to halt fighting between the Israeli military and Lebanese armed group Hezbollah. At least seven people were killed in Israeli strikes on Sunday. Just after midnight, Israeli warplanes hit a residential building in the town of Kfar Rumman in southern Lebanon, killing nine people including two children, and wounding five more, Lebanon’s National News Agency reported. A separate Israeli drone strike on a civilian vehicle in the town killed two medics inside the car, it said. The strikes on the town came without an online evacuation warning from the Israeli military. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Reuters’ questions on the strikes, including whether it was aware of the presence of medics and children at the strike locations and why no evacuation warning was issued. A spokesperson for the Israeli military issued a separate evacuation warning just after 2:00 a.m. local time (2300 GMT on Sunday) for areas around a building in another town in southern Lebanon where it said it would strike Hezbollah facilities. Israeli strikes on Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since Hezbollah launched rockets at Israel on March 2 — two days after the start of US and Israeli strikes on Iran — triggering an Israeli air and ground offensive. The ceasefire saw violence decrease dramatically, but Israeli troops occupying swathes of southern Lebanon have continued razing villages in the self-declared security zone. Israel’s military has continued carrying out strikes both within the zone and to its north, mostly without evacuation warnings.

title: North Korea and Russia open their first road bridge, a symbol of expanding ties, TASS reports
author: Reuters
description: MOSCOW: North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge on Monday, Russia’s TASS state news agency reported, a structure which spans the Tumen river and which both sides cast as an important milestone in their strategic partnership. The bridge is located near the existing “Friendship Bridge”, a rail bridge which was commissioned in 1959 after the Korean war. There are already direct air and rail links between Moscow and Pyongyang. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said the bridge should spur development between the two countries in various spheres - including tourism - and create new jobs. “I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation,” TASS cited Mishustin as saying at the bridge’s opening ceremony via video link. Construction of the new bridge, which had been under discussion for years, began in April last year after its construction was agreed during a visit by President Vladimir Putin to North Korea in 2024. title: PCB begins disciplinary probe amid reports of conduct issues in Test squad
author: BR Web Desk
description: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning alleged issues of discipline and conduct within the Pakistan Test squad. In a statement on Monday, the PCB said the reports were being reviewed internally and that the matter was being handled under the board’s standard procedures and regulations. “The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration,” the board said. The PCB did not specify which reports prompted the inquiry, nor did it name any players or confirm the allegations being circulated in the media. The board also cautioned against treating speculative or unverified claims as credible, particularly those it said were originating from “hostile external sources.” “The PCB will not comment further at this time,” the statement said, while advising stakeholders and the public to rely on the board’s official communications. The inquiry appears to follow recent media reports concerning alleged discipline and conduct issues involving members of Pakistan’s Test squad during the ongoing England tour. Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq have been mentioned in some reports in connection with alleged off-field conduct issues, although the PCB has not publicly linked either player to the inquiry or confirmed any of the allegations. At this stage, the PCB has confirmed only that an internal inquiry is underway; the specific allegations and individuals involved remain officially unconfirmed.

title: Huawei launches new foldable smartphone as competition with Xiaomi, Apple heats up
author: Reuters
description: GUANGZHOU/BEIJING: Huawei launched a new version of its flagship foldable smartphone on Monday as it seeks to defend its lead in the Chinese market for premium handsets against Apple and Xiaomi, both of which are also unveiling new products. The new Mate XT2 folds out twice to open into a tablet-sized screen and features Huawei’s new Kirin 9050 Pro chip. Huawei says the chip’s design allows it to deliver more computing power while using less electricity, helping the company overcome US restrictions on access to advanced technology. Xiaomi launches a rival foldable phone later on Monday, while Apple unveils its latest iPhone series on Wednesday, with expectations high that it too will be unveiling a foldable phone. China’s Q2 smartphone shipments down 2.4%, says Counterpoint The Mate XT2 features a redesigned folding mechanism, improved water resistance as well as an optional screen that prevents people nearby from seeing what is displayed. It also has upgraded cameras and delivers 42% better overall performance than its predecessor, based on company tests. Huawei, which does not sell in the US due to sanctions, leads China’s smartphone market with a 22.6% share in the second quarter, ahead of Apple’s 18.1%, according to consultancy IDC. Xiaomi has 12.4% of the market. Huawei is even more dominant in folding phones, accounting for 68% of shipments in China in the second quarter, according to Smart Analytics Global, a US-based research company.

title: European shares dip as rise in oil prices weighs; Novartis slips
author: Reuters
description: European shares were subdued on Monday as rising oil prices following fresh US-Iran attacks stoked inflation concerns and reinforced expectations that the European Central Bank could raise interest rates later this week. The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 0.1% to 649.17 points by 0711 GMT. The Swiss main index dropped 1.2%. Heavyweight Novartis fell 3.3% after its experimental drug pelacarsen missed a key goal in a late-stage trial. Germany’s DAX was flat, largely in line with other regional bourses. Over the weekend, the country’s far-right AfD topped state elections in Saxony-Anhalt with 44% of the vote, exit polls showed, dealing a major blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Energy stocks advanced 1.2%, tracking higher oil prices. Brent crude futures rose more than $1 a barrel as tit-for-tat strikes between the US and Iran on vessels sailing in the Strait of Hormuz and other areas heightened concerns of a prolonged supply disruption. Higher oil prices have fuelled inflation concerns, strengthening the case for further policy tightening. The ECB is widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points on Thursday, while US CPI data later this week comes into focus after a strong jobs report boosted expectations of a rate hike by the Federal Reserve this month. Investors will also monitor second-quarter euro zone economic data due later in the day. Trading volumes could be lighter than usual with US stock markets closed for a public holiday.

title: South African rand subdued ahead of key economic releases this week
author: Reuters
description: JOHANNESBURG: The South African rand was subdued in early trade on Monday, as investors awaited a raft of economic data this week, including gross domestic product, current account, mining and manufacturing figures, for clues on the health of the economy. At 0655 GMT, the rand traded at 15.9675 against the dollar , little changed from its previous close, with the market largely shrugging off reserves data. South Africa’s net foreign reserves rose to $73.69 billion at the end of August from $71.76 billion in July, central bank data showed on Monday. Focus will now turn to second-quarter GDP data due on Tuesday, followed by current account, mining and manufacturing figures on Thursday. The greenback last traded flat against a basket of currencies despite a ramp-up in US rate-hike bets, as tension in the Middle East heightened inflation risks that could force global central banks to tighten policy in tandem. South Africa’s benchmark 2035 government bond weakened slightly in early deals, as the yield rose 1 basis point to 8.53%.
