title: Iran to announce new restricted zone in the Gulf in the coming days
author: Reuters
description: DUBAI: Iran said it will announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf in the coming days, along with maps of a new shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz , as a weekend exchange of strikes on shipping sent oil prices higher on Monday. The new restricted zone will begin from where the US blockade of Iran begins and extend into areas of the Gulf, Mohsen Rezaei , the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said on Sunday in an interview with state TV. Few details were provided on the plan, but Rezaei said any ship entering the new zone would be added to a sanctions list. Iran says will tackle economic problems created by sanctions In addition, maps detailing passage routes for the Strait of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit largely closed to tanker traffic, would also be approved soon, Rezaei said. “The maps of a new international corridor which lies in Iranian and Omani waters and in which Iran will have management have been agreed and should be signed in the coming days,” he said. “We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they (the Americans) stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran,” Rezaei added. Six months after US-Israeli strikes on Iran sparked the war, the conflict appears to be at a stalemate. A preliminary ceasefire accord reached in June has unravelled, and little progress has been made in diplomatic efforts to get the peace process back on track. After a pause in military action for much of August, tit-for-tat strikes have resumed. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday , US Central Command said, including one off Kharg Island , Iran’s key oil export hub, following attacks by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on US warships in the region. Tehran has shown it retains the capability to attack U.S. interests in neighbouring countries and to shut down oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil supplies flowed prior to the conflict. An average of 10 commodity ships transited the Strait per day in the past 10 days, the lowest since May, according to shipping data on Monday. That helped oil prices extend last week’s big gains, with Brent crude up 0.8% above $97 a barrel. Sanctions, oil blockade squeeze economy Iran has said it will step up efforts to tackle problems created by U.S. sanctions that are crippling its economy. However, the US campaign to throttle Iran’s economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly difficult to withstand, three senior Iranian sources have said. Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Sunday that the U.S. should understand that the rules of the game have changed “before it is too late”. “From now on, any attack against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response,” he said in a speech published on his Telegram channel. Qalibaf said that alongside the military front, Iran’s main battle was now over production and people’s livelihoods. He cited sharp currency fluctuations, inflation, unemployment and market management as major challenges, adding Iranians could tolerate hardship but not mismanagement or inaction and expected the government to act quickly. Iran’s Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran planned to respond to US economic pressure with reforms and rejected the notion that sanctions would cause it to change course, according to state media on Sunday. “They speak of economic pressure and isolation, of breaking off financial ties and they think that by pressuring the economy of a country they can change the decisions of its people,” Madanizadeh said. “I have to clarify one point: The responsibility of reforming Iran’s economy is with its government and people, not with the U.S. Treasury.“ Kharg Island hit 550 times in prior months, Iran says Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90% of its crude via its Kharg Island export hub before the war. Flows have been disrupted since a US blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April. US Central Command said on X that as of Sunday it had redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two to ensure strict compliance with its blockade. On August 31, US President Donald Trump issued a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video depicting Kharg Island being “blown to smithereens.” Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked. In an interview aired on state TV on Sunday, Iran’s Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad said the island had been hit around 550 times in previous months but continued to operate. Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed up fuel prices, weighing on Trump’s popularity as his Republican Party heads into elections in November when control of Congress is at stake. However, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said oil was getting through the waterway. “Our transits through the Strait are averaging over 9 million barrels a day now, and with the access pipelines that go around the strait, we’re probably two-thirds or more of pre-conflict flows. So Iranians are still causing trouble, but the United States Navy is winning that battle,“ he told CNN .

title: Still on court after 20 years, the Honey Deuce keeps winning at the US Open
author: Reuters
description: NEW YORK: The Honey Deuce has become as much a part of the US Open as tennis itself, with the tournament’s signature cocktail celebrating its 20th year and drawing fans across Flushing Meadows, from the outer courts to the luxury suites. While Wimbledon has Pimm’s Cup and the Kentucky Derby has the mint julep, the USOpen has made the Grey Goose vodka-laced treat its own, as the cocktail’s rise has coincided with the rapid adoption of social media since its debut in 2007. A key part of the drink’s popularity is its collectible plastic glass, which is printed each year with the names of every past US Open champion in ever-smaller font as the roll call of title winners grows. The glasses have become sought-after souvenirs, regularly appearing for sale on eBay and often selling out before the tournament ends. The drink owes its inspiration, in part, to the mint julep, after USTA National Tennis Center’s COO Danny Zausner took a trip to the first race in the famed Triple Crown series. Only woman director of Venice fiction film says industry remains unequal “I saw women with their gorgeous hats and four-inch heels and they’d literally be walking around with a half a dozen glasses because they were mementos,” said Zausner. “There was not a real social media presence then but for them that meant you arrived - you were at the Derby.” In 2007, the cocktail – a blend of vodka, lemonade and raspberry liqueur – sold out its initial run of 25,000 drinks, which were priced at $12 each. Last year, that number climbed to around 800,000, now costing $23 a pop. Each drink is topped with three honeydew melon balls, a garnish selected by restaurateur Nick Mautone, who created the recipe and said they were intended to resemble tennis balls. A dedicated team is responsible for scooping anywhere between 2.5 million to 3 million balls of melon to ensure more than enough are available for the tournament, while the tournament’s hospitality partners Levy pre-mix the cocktails. “Levy has a team whose sole purpose is to take these casks, pretty much the equivalent of a beer keg on a slightly smaller scale, and pre-batch the exact amount,” said Zausner. The advent of social media has only accelerated the drink’s popularity. The U.S. Open accredited around 100 creators this year, with 20 specifically dedicated to food and beverages. The Australian Open and Grey Goose hoped to recreate the success with the launch of another cocktail in 2025 - the Grey Goose Lemon Ace - selling more than 100,000 units sold in the inaugural year. “I’d be lying if I said I had the foresight to think that 25,000 was going to turn into 800,000,” said Zausner.

title: Only woman director of Venice fiction film says industry remains unequal
author: Reuters
description: VENICE: The scarcity of women competing for the Venice Film Festival’s top prize reflects a structural problem in the film industry, Danish director May el-Toukhy said on Sunday as she unveiled her gritty drama “Woman Unknown”. El-Toukhy is the only woman directing a fiction film among the 21 contenders for the Golden Lion. Just one other competition entry, a documentary, has a female co-director, fuelling debate about women’s representation in cinema. “It is a structural problem, and it’s a structural problem that I have encountered throughout my own career,” the Danish-Egyptian filmmaker told a news conference ahead of the premiere of her latest movie. “It was very, very hard to get my first film done after graduating from film school. I think it took me six or seven years, whereas my male peers were much faster than me.” Venice film shows Murdoch shaking up hidebound Britain Festival director Alberto Barbera has defended this year’s line-up, noting that women directed just 24% of submitted films, down from 30% a year earlier, and saying selection decisions were based on artistic quality. El-Toukhy said securing financing remained more difficult for women directors, affecting everything from budgets to casting opportunities and, ultimately, a film’s chances of reaching major festivals. ‘The invisibility of women’ Set in the aftermath of World War Two, “Woman Unknown” follows Marie, a Danish housemaid preparing to marry her wealthy employer when a past relationship with a German soldier threatens to destroy her future. The film unfolds against the backdrop of a newly liberated Denmark, where women accused of fraternising with occupying German forces were often subjected to public humiliation and vigilante justice. El-Toukhy said the story’s themes echoed her comments about representation. “My film is about the invisibility of women,” she said. “It’s about being objectified on one hand and on the other hand being unseen and voiceless.” While grateful for the attention generated by her presence in competition, she said she would prefer to be joined by more female filmmakers. “Of course, I would love to have more female colleagues in competition beside me,” she said. “After MeToo, all of us were really aware of this gender imbalance, and something has happened over the course of the last couple of years where we’re kind of returning to what it used to be.” Actor Mathilde Arcel, who plays Marie, said the film shed light on women who carried the stigma of wartime relationships for decades. “There are women who never even told their families that they experienced these things,” she said. “Even today, when Denmark celebrates Liberation Day, some are still afraid and still ashamed.”

title: Pegula powers past Cirstea as Romanian bids farewell to US Open
author: Reuters
description: NEW YORK: American Jessica Pegula clinched a resounding 6-3 6-4 win over Sorana Cirstea on Sunday to reach the US Open quarter-finals, as the Romanian player made her final Grand Slam appearance. The 2024 runner-up kept alive her bid for a maiden major title, overcoming a resurgent Cirstea who had enjoyed a late-career renaissance, reaching a career-high top-20 ranking, before retiring at the end of the season. There was little between the two on serve in a scrappy opening set, with only three holds between them. Pegula repeatedly handed Cirstea openings, including when she double-faulted while serving for the set, and then squandered four set points before finally converting the fifth as the 16th seed dropped serve again. Pegula, who had needed three sets to overcome fellow US Open finalist Leylah Fernandez in the previous round, gained the upper hand in a second set that followed a similar pattern, with the American securing one more break than Cirstea to create the difference. The victory was Pegula’s second over Cirstea in three weeks after she edged the Romanian in the Cincinnati Open Round of 16. “I have a lot of respect for her. She’s such a great competitor,” Pegula said on the Louis Armstrong court. “We actually hadn’t played in a while up until the last few weeks. They were two really tough matches. It was definitely really intense.” Pegula will face the winner of the late-night clash between compatriot Emma Navarro and Russia’s Anna Kalinskaya for a place in her third straight U.S. Open semi-final.

title: Pakistan rejects India’s ‘baseless’ assertions regarding status of disputed Jammu, Kashmir
author: BR Web Desk
description: Pakistan on Monday “categorically” rejected India’s “baseless assertions” regarding the status of Jammu and Kashmir, saying these are contrary to internationally recognised facts. Responding to media queries regarding the statement issued by India’s Ministry of External Affairs on the map of disputed Jammu and Kashmir region, Foreign Office Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said India’s unilateral actions and continued illegal occupation cannot alter the internationally recognized disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir. The development comes a day after India said that any “inaccurate” or “misleading” depiction of the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh on a world map supported by the United Nations would not be acceptable to the country. The FO spokesperson said Jammu and Kashmir dispute remains one of the oldest unresolved, internationally recognized disputes on the agenda of the United Nations Security Council. The relevant UN resolutions stipulate that its final disposition must be made in accordance with the relevant Security Council resolutions and the will of the Kashmiri people, expressed through a free and impartial plebiscite under UN auspices, he said. He said the official United Nations maps, which depict Jammu and Kashmir as a disputed territory, remain the only cartographic representation of its current legal status. “India’s so-called official maps and unilateral claims of sovereignty have no bearing on the status of the disputed territory,” he stated. The spokesperson urged the international community to ensure that India immediately stops human rights violations in the Indian Illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir and fulfils its commitment towards the realisation of the right to self-determination of the Kashmiri people, in line with the relevant UNSC resolutions.

text: The annual West Indian American Day Parade and J’Ouvert festivities kick off Monday, September 7, drawing hundreds of thousands to Crown Heights for one of New York City’s largest celebrations of Caribbean culture. The parade is commonly referred to as the Labour Day Parade, as it is always held on Labour Day. J'Ouvert marks the start of celebrations on Monday morning from 6 a.m. to 11 a.m., although the viewing begins at 2 a.m. The major West Indian American Day Parade starts at 11 a.m. from Eastern Parkway and Rochester Avenue. This year, the parade will end at 5:30 p.m. sharp, "in light of the violence that has occurred on and around the parade route in the past," according to organizers. Eastern Parkway starts the parade journey from Rochester Avenue to Grand Army Plaza. J'Ouvert follows the path along Empire Boulevard and Nostrand Avenue from Flatbush Avenue to Rutland Road. Street closures for J'Ouvert will commence from 11:30 p.m. on Sunday until 11 a.m. on Monday, and these will cover Flatbush Avenue between Grand Army Plaza and Empire Boulevard; Empire Boulevard between Flatbush Avenue and Nostrand Avenue; and Nostrand Avenue from Empire Boulevard to Rutland Road. Other additional closures during the procession will start at 6 a.m. Monday, growing around 10:30 a.m., and will close Eastern Parkway from Utica Avenue to Grand Army Plaza. The full closure will also include Grand Army Plaza, as well as Washington, Bedford, Rochester, Buffalo, Ralph, Ocean, Lincoln and Rockaway Parkways, among others. NYC officials advise people to make use of public transportation if they plan to travel in the vicinity. As stated by Mayor Zohran Mamdani during Friday’s briefing, there are no "known specific or credible threats" to any of the planned celebrations; however, thousands of NYPD officers will be patrolling the streets and the subway as part of one of the largest law enforcement operations in a year. Helicopters and drones will be monitoring the festivities overhead. 13 entry points are set along the route for spectators who will be thoroughly screened by NYPD personnel with magnetometers. Prohibited items include drones, alcohol, weapons, large bags, backpacks, blankets, bicycles, scooters, and large banners or flags that can obstruct views.

title: Saudi Arabia preparing to grant IAEA more intrusive powers: nuclear watchdog chief
author: Reuters
description: US and Saudi signed 123 agreement in July.Deal doesn't include Saudi signing Additional Protocol.IAEA's Grossi says elements in the works come close.A planned US-Saudi atomic deal does not include Riyadh signing the Additional Protocol that...
text: A planned US-Saudi atomic deal does not include Riyadh signing the Additional Protocol that gives the UN nuclear watchdog sweeping inspection powers, but something close to it on some points is in the works, the agency's chief said on Monday. The US and Saudi Arabia reached an agreement on civil nuclear power cooperation in July that would let Riyadh enrich uranium and build nuclear reactors using US technology. Non-proliferation groups, such as the Arms Control Association, have criticised the planned "123 agreement" for not including the Additional Protocol, which grants the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) extra powers such as the ability to carry out snap inspections at undeclared locations. Iran implemented the Additional Protocol from 2016 to 2021 under a nuclear deal with major powers that unravelled after the US pulled out in 2018. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said that while the Additional Protocol would be the "ideal setup", Riyadh was preparing to go beyond its core obligations under its Comprehensive Safeguards Agreement governing relations with the IAEA. "What is important is that in the consultations, in the preparation process, it has been possible to introduce a number of provisions to the bilateral agreement that will give the agency additional verification and monitoring authorisations," he told a press conference. Those would be in relation to activities such as uranium enrichment and the step preceding it known as uranium conversion, as well as reprocessing, which can separate plutonium from spent reactor fuel. "These are sensitive activities, as we all know. So for those we are going to have authorisations and capacities which are very, very similar to those that you may find in an Additional Protocol," he said, without elaborating. Once the details are finalised, the bilateral agreement between the IAEA and Saudi Arabia will be presented to the IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors, Grossi said.

text: A former senior U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) official and his accomplice have been arrested and charged in an alleged bribery scheme that accumulated around $960,000 in exchange for manipulating the citizenship application process. The federal prosecutors confirmed his identity as Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu, who was appointed as a Senior Immigration Services Officer in Dallas, and his accomplice as Adeniyi Akeem Somoye. Both were arrested on September 2 on charges of conspiracy to receive illegal gratuities by a public official. According to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas, the two individuals communicated extensively via WhatsApp from December 2019 to March 2026 in relation to their scheme. Prosecutors say Ganiyu bypassed the process by dodging criminal background checks, interviews, and supervision to fast-track applications made by bribers. Ganiyu allegedly abused his position at USCIS to take control of field office applications in Minneapolis, Charlotte, and Houston, approving them on his own, without the knowledge of any of the local supervisors. He even reportedly fast-tracked citizenship for Somoye and approved residency for Somoye's wife and kid before him. Court documents have shown that Ganiyu received about $671,438 through Zelle and Cash App, and another $287,830 in cash deposits aimed at hiding the origin of funds. Somoye processed approximately $1.7 million in transactions and took a cut of the transaction as a bribe. The inquiry started when USCIS got a tip in May 2025. Ganiyu resigned in March 2026, citing "personal reasons." Each of them faces up to five years in federal prison and a $250,000 fine. Most affected applications reportedly involved citizens from African countries.

"We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they [the Americans] stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran," Rezaei said. Underlining Iran's defiance, Ghalibaf issued a new threat to respond to any US strikes, in what appeared to be a response to a warning by US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth that Iran’s oil tanker fleet was "defenceless". "It’s simple: the oil and gas production chain here is sprawling, accessible, and exposed. American oil and gas companies across these waters and facilities share that exposure," Ghalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, wrote on X. "Strike our assets and you get struck. We’ve already proven it. Ask the bases that are no longer viable," referring to Iranian attacks on US military bases in the region throughout the conflict. US President Donald Trump has yet to achieve the aims he set out when he launched "Operation Epic Fury" in February: to end Iran's nuclear programme, halt its ability to attack its neighbours and create conditions for Iranians to topple their leadership. Tehran's rulers remain in power and aim to emerge from the war stronger than before, demanding the lifting of sanctions and hoping to collect fees from ships that use the strait, which carried a fifth of global oil and gas shipments before the war. After a pause in military action for much of August, tit-for-tat strikes have resumed following the unravelling of an interim ceasefire deal that was reached in June, and there has been little progress on getting the peace process back on track. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday, US Central Command said, including one off Kharg Island, Iran's key oil export hub, following attacks by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on US warships in the region. Tehran has shown it retains the capability to attack US interests in neighbouring countries and to shut down oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. An average of 10 commodity ships transited the Strait per day in the past 10 days, the lowest since May, according to shipping data on Monday. That contributed to a rise in oil prices on Monday, with Brent crude futures LCOc1 hitting their highest point since July 24 at $97.93 a barrel before slipping back to $96.19. Iran has said it will step up efforts to tackle problems created by U.S. sanctions that are crippling its economy. However, the US campaign to throttle Iran's economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly difficult to withstand, three senior Iranian sources have said. Ghalibaf said at the weekend that, alongside the military front, Iran’s main battle was now over production and people’s livelihoods, citing currency fluctuations, inflation, unemployment and market management as big challenges. The conflict has also impacted oil-producing Gulf Arab states such as the United Arab Emirates, which has come under fire from Iranian missiles and suffered attacks on its oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on Monday the country was building alternative routes for its energy exports and trade to ensure they are not "held hostage" by the war. The impact of Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on energy supplies has also been felt in the US as fuel prices have increased. The increase has weighed on Trump's popularity as his Republican Party heads into elections in November when control of Congress is at stake.

title: 'Products of Form-47': PPP leader takes aim at federal ministers over new provinces

description: Federal ministers have artificial mandate, says Memon.PTI urges against contentious legislation over provinces.Asif says this is a national issue, should not be opposed.Sindh Information Minister Sharjeel Memon on Monday slammed...
text: Sindh Information Minister Sharjeel Memon on Monday slammed federal ministers seeking the establishment of new provinces, calling them products of “Form-47”, a term used by political rivals to question the legitimacy of lawmakers elected in the 2024 general elections. Rejecting their mandate, the PPP leader, whose party is an ally in the Centre with the ruling PML-N, called such federal ministers “unelected representatives”. The decades-long debate over new provinces began after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the current system had collapsed, and later, some federal ministers — including Ahsan Iqbal and Mustafa Kamal — also said that new provinces or administrative units should be set up. While the PML-N is yet to take a firm position, the PPP has said that if the people deem it fit, new provinces should be established, but the Sindh Assembly, where the PPP is in power, passed a resolution recently rejecting the idea of creating new provinces. Meanwhile, the MQM-P has fully backed the idea of creating new provinces. “Those lecturing us on the 18th Amendment are the products of Form-47; those who have secured an artificial or handed-out mandate cannot make decisions for the nation,” the senior provincial minister said during his speech in the Sindh Assembly. Memon said if Iqbal, Kamal, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif have any concerns, they can raise them in parliament. “Decisions should be taken by those [lawmakers] who secured the public’s mandate. These federal ministers should first secure a genuine mandate, then they may speak on such issues,” he said. Talking about delivery, he said that the federal government builds motorways in Punjab but “does injustice” to Sindh. Meanwhile, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar has called for 18th Amendment-like consultations over the issue of new provinces. “Making a decision on new provinces in haste would undermine the unity of the federation, he said. He added that dividing Sindh, Punjab and Balochistan without the input of the public and their representatives would create complications. “No contentious legislation should be done on new provinces,” he added. Speaking to Geo News , Defence Minister Asif said he has no information related to the establishment of new provinces, adding that he welcomes the proposal for changing the governance system of Islamabad. “It is good that an independent institution would be established in Islamabad. You may call it an assembly as well or a provincial government or the government of the capital,” he said. Drawing comparisons with other global capitals, he said that neighbouring India has an independent government in New Delhi. “There’s nothing to be hesitant about,” the defence czar said. He further said that Afghanistan had a few provinces earlier but now they had 34-35, and mentioned that in a meeting with ousted president Ashraf Ghani, he told him that it made governance better. “This is a national issue, and there should be no opposition to it. This will strengthen the federation and the provinces,” he said, adding: “Maybe people are getting confused with the term provinces; we should use administrative units.”

text: KARACHI: The judicial commission, formed to investigate the death of businessman Mir Raza Ali, issued a notice to investigation team head DIG Amir Farooqi on Monday, seeking clarification over the alleged withholding of records. The commission, headed by Sindh High Court Justice Omar Sial, observed that the records appeared to have been deliberately withheld from it and that the deceased's parents were raising valid concerns. It made the observation while examining the statement of Mir Raza's friend Raziq, saying the seven-line statement presented before it was missing critical information. Raziq told the commission that a receipt found in the room indicated that Mir Raza had met someone named Ahmed Raja in the evening, a detail his fiancée had also shared. The commission noted that this information was absent from the police record. The focal person gave assurances that video statements of witnesses would be submitted by Tuesday, prompting the commission to adjourn further proceedings until the following day. Meanwhile, the commission also questioned SHO Gulistan-e-Jauhar Kamran Qureshi over multiple procedural failures. When Qureshi claimed the body had been found in his jurisdiction and he was merely assisting the relevant police, the commission questioned what investigation he had actually conducted and pointed out that immoral activities were being carried out at a guesthouse in his area, asking how the area's watchman knew about them but the SHO did not. "Your claim of ignorance is unbelievable," the commission said, adding, "It appears you were not assisting but covering yourself." The commission asked who had authorised Qureshi to view CCTV footage and pointed out that his movement details would be in the daily register. It directed the Sindh government's focal person to seal the daily registers of Ferozabad and Gulistan-e-Jauhar police stations and present them before the commission. The commission also questioned how the body had been transferred without a memo being prepared at the scene, and without the crime scene unit being present. Qureshi said the location had been difficult to access but the commission pointed out that Edhi volunteers had managed to reach the body while police had not. "Edhi volunteers could make their way up but police could not?" it remarked. In a damning exchange, the commission asked Qureshi why he had gone to the crime scene without the investigation officer's authorisation, and whether he had gone to plant or remove evidence. "You seem suspicious to us," the commission told him. When Qureshi said a gun holster had been found in his presence 48 hours after the incident during a metal detector search, the commission asked how the holster had suddenly appeared so late, noting all other officers were present but the investigation officer was not. The commission also questioned Qureshi over the burning of the crime scene, with Qureshi saying the CIA team had set fire to the grass to search for evidence. The commission asked if this was standard protocol and issued instructions to also serve notice on the SSP CIA. It further issued notices to ASP Jamshed, SHO Site Super Highway and SHO Aziz Bhutto over their unexplained presence at the crime scene. When asked how many people had been taken into custody, Qureshi said no one had been formally detained — only drug addicts had been questioned and released. He said a person visible in CCTV footage near the body at 7am had returned an hour later and approached closer, but he could not confirm whether the person had seen the body due to grass and bushes at the location. The commission said it was difficult to believe the person had not seen the body. Family lawyer Jibran Nasir, speaking to the media after proceedings, said SHO Adil Afzal had told Mir Raza's three friends not to go to the family's home, claiming it would damage the investigation, and had also told them not to attend protests. Nasir said the business partner had attempted to defame Mir Raza while other friends had provided detailed accounts to the commission. He said two people had gone to arrange bail while the rest remained present. Nasir said the SHO of Gulistan-e-Jauhar had done the most damage to the case, and that SHO Adil Afzal and the head clerk were due to appear the following day. He said every witness who had appeared so far had confirmed that the parents' account was correct, and not a single witness had disputed it. He said he had footage of a fire at the scene and would provide it if denied. He accused police of making a film instead of conducting an investigation, saying they had included year-old matters in witness statements. He said all forensic reports had been completed and demanded they be presented before the commission.

text: Huawei launched its new flagship foldable smartphone series on Monday as it seeks to defend its lead in the Chinese market for premium handsets against Apple and Xiaomi, both of which are also unveiling new products. Phones in the new Mate XT2 series, which fold out twice to open into a tablet-sized screen, feature Huawei's new Kirin 9050 Pro chip. But they are not cheap. Prices start from ¥19,999 ($2,980) with the most expensive version costing ¥24,999 ($3,725). Sales will start on September 12. "Pricing right now is a real challenge, because memory costs have risen sharply. We adopted a lot of new technology, and the cost pressure has been enormous," Huawei Executive Director Richard Yu told a press conference. Huawei says the new chip's design allows it to deliver more computing power while using less electricity. The design architecture, called LogicFolding, is part of the "Tau Scaling Law" principle Huawei unveiled in May to help the company overcome US restrictions on access to advanced technology. Xiaomi launches a rival foldable phone later on Monday, while Apple unveils its latest iPhone series on Wednesday, with expectations high that it too will be unveiling a foldable phone. Huawei is currently the only major brand to sell a so-called tri-fold phone. The Chinese tech giant is, however, barred from selling in the US as Washington has deemed the company a national security risk. South Korea's Samsung Electronics, currently the world's biggest seller of foldable phones, launched a tri-fold in December but reportedly discontinued sales after three months. It expanded its line-up of foldable offerings in July to include a passport-sized foldable phone. Huawei's Mate XT2 phones feature a redesigned folding mechanism, improved water resistance as well as a screen feature that prevents people nearby from seeing what is displayed. They also have upgraded cameras and deliver 42% better overall performance than their predecessor series based on company tests. Shares in Xiaomi sank 3% in afternoon trade after Huawei unveiled the new series. Huawei leads China's smartphone market with a 22.6% share in the second quarter, ahead of Apple's 18.1%, according to consultancy IDC. Xiaomi has 12.4% of the market. Huawei is even more dominant in folding phones, accounting for 68% of shipments in China in the second quarter, according to Smart Analytics Global, a US-based research company.

description: Kevin Pietersen will return to the England setup for the first time since retiring in 2014 after being appointed specialist mentor to the white-ball teams ahead of next year's World Cup in southern Africa, the England Cricket Board said on...
text: Kevin Pietersen will return to the England setup for the first time since retiring in 2014 after being appointed specialist mentor to the white-ball teams ahead of next year's World Cup in southern Africa, the England Cricket Board (ECB) said on Monday. The former Ashes and T20 World Cup-winning batter will join Brendon McCullum's coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka coming up later this month, working alongside Marcus Trescothick, Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor. The 46-year-old Pietersen's involvement extends through England's white-ball tours to Australia and South Africa and the home series against Pakistan and New Zealand next summer, before the one-day international (ODI) World Cup itself. "I am immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa. Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment," Pietersen said. "We have an incredibly talented white-ball squad and I am excited to get in the trenches and work relentlessly hard with these players to maximise their potential. "To be a part of Brendon's think tank over the next 12 months is a fantastic opportunity, and I cannot wait to get started." An explosive middle-order batter, Pietersen scored nearly 14,000 runs across all three formats for England, who last won the ODI World Cup in 2019 on home soil. However, his England career ended controversially in 2014 in the aftermath of the 5-0 Ashes whitewash in Australia, amid reported tensions within the dressing room and between the batsman and team management. Pietersen was the team's top scorer in the series and, despite remaining keen to play for England, was told he was no longer part of the plans, bringing an acrimonious end to his international career. Pietersen's South African upbringing could prove particularly valuable as England prepare for the World Cup, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia from October 2027. "I'm particularly excited for our batters to get the opportunity to work with him," McCullum said. "KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players. "We've always respected each other and had a strong appreciation for what the other brings to the game, so I'm really looking forward to working together."

title: Why did officials call off historic Nebraska-Missouri volleyball showdown at Wrigley Field?
author: Web Desk
description: At the iconic Wrigley Field, over 43 thousand people were in attendance to witness the historic showdown volleyball game between Nebraska and Missouri on Sunday, September 6, 2026.But officials dashed their hopes by...
text: At the iconic Wrigley Field, over 43 thousand people were in attendance to witness the historic showdown volleyball game between Nebraska and Missouri on Sunday, September 6, 2026. But officials dashed their hopes by calling off the match, after stadium staff along with players on both sides, did everything they could to get the playable court. The historic women’s college volleyball match at Wrigley Field was delayed twice before finally being suspended. Due to the weather conditions that caused excessive moisture on the court, the staff mopped the court several times between the matches, but it made little difference. The first delay in the Nebraska-Missou match came after just three points into the match. This time, not just workers but also players from both sides got on their hands and knees with towels in an effort to mop up the playing surface. But all in vain. At this point, several Nebraska players took a break for a brief dance party when the court sound system began playing Justin Bieber’s Baby before they got back to the task of getting the court mop-up. The match resumed after about 20 minutes only to be paused again after another 15 points were played. The situation led to both coaches, Busboom Kelly and Dawn Sullivan, surrounding the officials, discussing the scenarios that led to the decision to suspend the match. After just 10 points of play, the officials called off the match due to the excessive moisture on the court. “It was on its way to being a very, very epic moment for our sport. Unfortunately, the weather didn’t cooperate,' said the Nebraska coach Kelly. The historic match was part of the Big Ten/SEC Volleyball Challenge and was the inaugural volleyball game ever played at the iconic baseball stadium: Wrigley Field.

title: Austrian headscarf ban for under-14s faces first test as schools reopen
author: Reuters
description: The legislation proposing the ban was passed in parliament last year, in December
text: Austria's ban on headscarves for under-14s faces an initial test on Monday as schools reopen in Vienna and other states, with groups including the country's main Muslim organisation denouncing it as discriminatory and legal challenges likely. Austria's ruling coalition of three centrist parties proposed the ban in schools, arguing it was acting to protect girls' freedom. The legislation was passed in parliament in December with the support of the far-right Freedom Party. Only the smallest party in parliament, the left-wing Greens, opposed it. The group that formally represents Austria's Muslims, the Islamic Religious Community in Austria (IGGO), has said the move was an infringement of fundamental rights, pledging to fight it before the Constitutional Court, which rejected challenges in July because the legislation had not yet gone into force. The court ruled in 2020 that a previous ban, which applied to under-10s in schools, was illegal because it discriminated against Muslims and the state had a duty to be religiously neutral. Going against that principle requires special justification, it held. Read: Islamic banks told to scrap abaya dress code Asked by national broadcaster ORF if the court would overturn the new ban, Education Minister Christoph Wiederkehr said, "You can never be completely certain." "We in the government carried out very intensive consultations, and we in the education ministry tried very hard to write a law that complies with the constitution," Wiederkehr said in the interview broadcast on Monday. Left-wing pupils' organisations have called for protests. The new school year starts on Monday in three of Austria's nine states — Vienna, the surrounding state of Lower Austria, and Burgenland, all in the east — with the rest following next week. The legislation stipulates that a school must hold discussions with any pupil defying the ban, after which a fine of between €150 and €800 ($175-$930) can be imposed.

title: Pietersen makes England return as white-ball mentor
author: Sports Desk
description: Former England star rejoins the national set-up as a specialist mentor ahead of the 2027 World Cup
text: Kevin Pietersen has joined England's white-ball coaching team as a "specialist mentor" in the build-up to next year's World Cup in southern Africa. Pietersen’s role with Brendon McCullum’s coaching staff begins later this month when England face Sri Lanka in three T20 internationals and three ODIs. The former England batter has previously worked as a mentor with Delhi Capitals in the Indian Premier League and briefly assisted England’s batters during an ODI series in South Africa in 2023. Pietersen has largely worked as a broadcaster since retiring from professional cricket in 2018, but has remained outspoken about England’s approach. He criticised McCullum’s team for what he described as a relaxed training culture during their tour of India in early 2025, comments McCullum rejected as “factually incorrect”. Pietersen will miss England’s ODI tri-series in Pakistan in October but will work with the squad on tours of Australia and South Africa over the winter. He will then be involved in home series against Pakistan and New Zealand before the 2027 World Cup, which will be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. The England and Wales Cricket Board said Pietersen’s experience of growing up in South Africa would provide valuable local knowledge ahead of the tournament. He joins former England team-mate Marcus Trescothick, as well as Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor, in McCullum’s coaching staff. Pietersen’s return marks a striking reversal from 2014, when England ended his international career amid what then director of cricket Andrew Strauss described as a “massive trust issue” between the player and the ECB. Strauss had also revealed at the time that Pietersen declined an offer to become a white-ball adviser – a role similar to the one he has now accepted. Despite the acrimonious ending, Pietersen has remained popular among several England players, including Harry Brook, Tom Banton and Will Jacks. “I am immensely proud to have been asked to help this team on their journey to win a World Cup in South Africa,” Pietersen said. “Putting on the England uniform again for the first time since 2014 is a profound honour and a deeply special moment.” Pietersen and McCullum faced each other 24 times in international cricket between 2007 and 2013 and later spent two seasons together at Pakistan Super League side Quetta Gladiators. McCullum welcomed the reunion, saying Pietersen’s experience and understanding of elite cricket would be particularly valuable to England’s batters. “KP has a unique understanding of what it takes to perform at the highest level, which will be hugely valuable to our players,” McCullum said. “We’ve always respected each other and had a strong appreciation for what the other brings to the game, so I’m really looking forward to working together.”

A building that housed a boys' paying guest hostel in New Delhi’s Satya Niketan area collapsed around noon Sunday, triggering a massive rescue operation by different teams. On Monday, a statement by the All India Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in New Delhi confirmed six fatalities. Narendra Bundela, a senior officer of the National Disaster Response Force, which is involved in the rescue, told reporters that "six were declared dead, and five were admitted to hospitals", while “one body is yet to be extricated”. The deaths came as heavy rainfall paralysed parts of the city, with the India Meteorological Department recording more than 200 millimetres of rain within 24 hours on July 7. Before that, in April, seven people died after a 2.5-metre wall at a hospital complex collapsed in the southern Indian city of Bengaluru. The collapse killed a child and four street vendors, as well as two other people from the state of Kerala, DK Shivakumar, the deputy chief minister of the southern state of Karnataka, revealed in a statement. title: Fatima fined for Asia Cup conduct breach
author: Sports Desk
description: Pakistan captain is fined 10 percent of her match fee
text: Pakistan captain Fatima Sana has been fined 10 percent of her match fee for breaching Level 1 of the International Cricket Council’s Code of Conduct during her team’s Women’s Asia Cup defeat by India. Fatima was found to have breached Article 2.5 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, relating to language, actions or gestures that disparage or could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon dismissal. One demerit point was also added to her disciplinary record, taking her total to two in a 24-month period. Her previous demerit point came during a T20 international against Ireland in Dublin on August 6, 2025. Fatima admitted the offence and accepted the sanctions proposed by Supriya Das of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees, meaning no formal hearing was required. The incident occurred after Fatima dismissed India’s Shafali Verma during Saturday’s Group A match in Dubai. After completing the catch, the Pakistan skipper gestured towards the pavilion. India’s bowlers had earlier dismissed Pakistan for just 55, but Fatima fought back with the ball, taking three wickets before India secured a seven-wicket victory. Level 1 breaches carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand and a maximum of 50 percent of a player’s match fee, along with one or two demerit points. Pakistan now face Hong Kong, China, in their next Asia Cup match. A victory would secure their place in the semi-finals.

title: Sabalenka reaches US Open quarters
author: AFP
description: She beats Townsend 6-4, 6-3 to extend her US Open winning streak to 17 matches
text: Aryna Sabalenka kept her US Open three-peat bid alive Sunday, charging into the US Open quarter-finals with a confidence boosting victory over tricky American Taylor Townsend. Sabalenka took everything the multi-faceted Townsend threw at her to emerge with a 6-4, 6-3 victory, winning the last five games to push her Flushing Meadows win streak to 17 matches. "I love matches like that, because it was really challenging, and going through tough challenges and overcoming those challenges, it definitely gives you strength and really strong belief that you can do it," Sabalenka said. "So these kind of matches is really, really, really like a boost of confidence." Sabalenka is vying to become just the third woman, after Chris Evert and Serena Williams, to win three straight US Open titles. She'll have to lift the trophy just to have a chance of retaining her world number one ranking, and even if she does her time at the top could end in New York, where second-ranked Elena Rybakina needs only to reach the semis to be assured of ascending. "I completely separate myself from that, because it's just guessing," Sabalenka said of the multiple number one scenarios -- which could also see third-ranked Jessica Pegula or even No. 4 Coco Gauff end the tournament at the top. "I'm just trying to bring my best tennis every time I'm competing out there and basically fight for it," she added. Sabalenka needed all of her powers of concentration in her first career meeting with Townsend, the world's second-ranked doubles player who boasts formidable skills at the net as well as power from the baseline and a steely return game. The match opened with five breaks of serve before Sabalenka managed a comfortable hold for a 4-2 first-set lead. She had double-faulted to hand Townsend a break in the second game and Townsend broke again in the fourth with a massive service return. But Sabalenka's sustained power and precision proved a little too much. Townsend broke her as she served for the set at 5-2, but by the time the American managed a hold for 5-4 it was too late, and Sabalenka held serve for just the second time to pocket the set, saving a break point before putting it away with a trademark forehand winner. Challenging beginning "She was returning really well," Sabalenka said. "She saw where I'm going. She was blocking really well. I guess playing doubles and mixed doubles really helped her to react on, like, heavy serve. "That was really challenging beginning, but then I had to adjust my serve, the speed, the spin, bring the variety into my service games just so I keep her guessing." The second set unfolded in more traditional style, neither player facing a break point through the first three games. Sabalenka blinked first, smacking a forehand into the net to give Townsend a break point then offering up a weak second serve that Townsend punished with a return winner for a break and a 3-1 lead. Sabalenka immediately broke back, however, launching a run of five straight games to take the match.

title: Tiafoe tops Medvedev in straight
author: AFP
description: American says he came up with some crazy stuff
text: American Frances Tiafoe swept past former champion Daniil Medvedev in straight sets Sunday to advance to the quarter-finals of the US Open. A two-time semi-finalist at New York's Flushing Meadows, the 11th-seeded Tiafoe defeated seventh-seeded Medvedev of Russia 7-6 (7/1), 6-4, 7-6 (8/6) to reach the quarter-finals for the fourth time in five years. Medvedev held leads in two of the three sets, but was outplayed by the American at key junctures. "I played well when it counted," Tiafoe said. "Yeah, I came up with some crazy stuff, but it had to be that good against such a quality player in Daniil." Tiafoe enjoyed loud support from the crowd in Louis Armstrong Stadium, where he has never lost. After the match, Tiafoe stood before the crowd and pointed to his ear, asking for noise. He also took a virtual basketball shot, acknowledging hoop stars Lisa Leslie, AJ Dybantsa and Victor Oladipo who were in his cheering section. "The energy has been amazing," Tiafoe told a court-side interviewer. "It's like the people's court. I'm loving the energy for sure." Medvedev had won six of seven prior matches against the American, including a straight-set drubbing in the same round of the 2020 US Open. But Medvedev, who won the US Open in 2021 for his only Grand Slam, has had an up-and-down 2026. He has won two ATP titles and notched a win over Carlos Alcaraz at the prestigious Indian Wells tournament. But Medvedev, who has reached six career Grand Slam finals, failed this year to advance beyond the round of 16 at any Grand Slam. Medvedev served for the first set, but was broken at 6-5 and then lost the tiebreaker decisively. Too often, Medvedev was unable to consolidate lead. He hit a brilliant backhand overhead to take a 4-3 lead in the third-set tiebreaker, but followed it up with a feeble backhand error. Still, the Russian held a set point in the third-set tiebreaker. But Tiafoe got the better of a net exchange between the men, then proceeded to take the next two points to seal the win.

title: Alcaraz books Shelton clash
author: AFP
description: Spaniard beats Tommy Paul to qualify for the quarter-finals
text: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz posted his most convincing win in his injury return at the US Open, downing Tommy Paul in straight sets on Sunday to line up a quarter-final clash with Ben Shelton. Two-time women's defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also advanced, booking a last-eight date with Wimbledon winner Linda Noskova. Second-seeded Alcaraz, playing his first tournament since he was sidelined by a right wrist injury in April, looked closer to his brilliant best in a 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 victory over Paul, the 20th-seeded American who posed the Spaniard's sternest test yet. "I played my game," said Alcaraz, who unleashed 33 winners as he moved fluidly around the court, thwarting Paul at every turn in the two-hour 20-minute match. He'll face red-hot Shelton -- a 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 winner over Stefanos Tsitsipas -- for a place in the semi-finals. "I tried to play my style," Alcaraz said. "Tommy is such a talented player. His shots are pretty dangerous and sometimes it's really difficult to control the ball when it comes to you. "I just tried to be ready for a battle and tried to be aggressive all the time." Alcaraz grabbed the first break of the contest in the final game of a tight first set. From there he was in control. He broke Paul twice in the second set and again early in the third. He finished it off with a gutsy hold of serve in which he saved a pair of break points, the second with a swinging forehand volley that he followed with a forehand winner to set up the only match point he needed. "I'm really happy with the performance today," Alcaraz said. Shelton, who needed four sets in each of his first three matches, raised his game to dismantle former world number three Tsitsipas in just one hour and 52 minutes. The American, riding high after a strong August that included a title at the ATP Montreal Masters, blasted a dozen aces and never faced a break point. "I played a complete match from start to finish," said Shelton, who was looking forward to taking on Alcaraz. "I think the level that he's been playing at is really, really impressive. To not play for five months then do what he's done so far this tournament has been super-human." "I think it's going to be fireworks on Tuesday night," Shelton said. Sabalenka on track Sabalenka kept her bid for a rare US Open three-peat on track with a 6-4, 6-3 victory over American Taylor Townsend. The Belarusian, whose world number one ranking is on the line in New York, will face a tough quarter-final against sixth-ranked Czech Noskova, who edged dangerous Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk 7-5, 5-7, 6-4. Sabalenka needed all of her resolve against the multi-faceted Townsend, whose blistering service returns and net prowess flummoxed the Belarusian star in a first set that opened with five breaks of serve. But her sustained power and precision proved too much and after falling behind 3-1 in the second set she won the last five games to seal the match. "I was just trying to stay focused on myself and play not only point by point but ball by ball," Sabalenka said. "I'm happy that I was able to turn around that second set." Noskova needed six match points to seal her victory over Kostyuk, failing to convert two in the second set. "I am more than relieved," Noskova said. "This match was so tough, emotionally more so than physically."

title: 480 newborns die at Mithi Civil Hospital in Tharparkar in eight months
author: Sajid Bajeer
description: The NICU monthly record shows that 2,273 newborns were admitted for treatment between January, August
text: As many as 480 newborn babies, nearly 21% of the total, died at the Civil Hospital Mithi’s Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) during the first eight months of 2026, according to hospital records, amid what sources describe as a worsening health crisis involving mother-child malnutrition, low birth weight and other medical complications. The NICU monthly record showed that 2,273 newborns were admitted for treatment between January and August, of whom 480 died. The highest number of newborn deaths was recorded in May. "In January, 70 newborns lost their lives in the NICU, followed by 39 in February, 54 in March, 47 in April, 75 in May, 65 in June, 69 in July and 61 in August," according to the data. The data further revealed that around 61% recovery rate was witnessed in the NICU during these eight months, with 1,387 babies discharged after recovering at the facility. During the same period, 106 newborns were referred to other hospitals for further treatment and 126 babies were discharged from the hospital against medical advice. Admissions also peaked in May, when 365 newborns were brought to the NICU for treatment. Read: Five dead, over 100 injured as tourists flock to Tharparkar The NICU monthly admission figures were 232 in January, 200 in February, 240 in March, 274 in April, 305 in June, 348 in July and 309 in August. Sources attributed the vulnerability of newborns in Tharparkar to a combination of malnutrition, maternal malnutrition, infectious diseases and early marriages that contribute to premature births and low birth weight. When contacted for the reasons behind the high newborn death toll, Mithi Civil Hospital Surgeon Dr Shahid Jhanjhi did not respond to the query or provide the requested information. Tharparkar District Health Officer Dr Lekhraj Sarangani also declined to provide details, saying that his office did not collect data on newborn mortality and that hospitals had been handed over to the Sindh Peoples Primary Healthcare Initiative (PPHI). Read more: Thar's coal must power people, not just plants However, Mithi Civil Hospital, five taluka hospitals and 95 medical dispensaries remain under the administrative control of the District Health Officer. Sources said that newborn deaths were also reported at the district’s seven THQ and rural health centres. However, the Tharparkar Health Department has not made the figures for these facilities public, leaving the overall scale of neonatal mortality in Tharparkar unclear.

title: Inam opts against B-sample
author: Muhammad Yousaf Anjum
description: Ace wrestler cites approved acetazolamide treatment after adverse doping finding; keeps CAS challenge option open
text: Pakistan ace-wrestler Muhammad Inam Butt has decided not to have his B sample tested after returning a positive doping finding at the Asian Beach Games in China, while leaving open the possibility of challenging any eventual sanction before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), sources close to the wrestler said. Inam, who won a silver medal at the Asian Beach Games in April, was among the wrestlers tested during the competition. A sample taken from him was found to contain a small amount of a prohibited substance, prompting anti-doping authorities to issue him a notice. Sources close to Inam confirmed that he received the notice and said the wrestler had used medication to treat an eye condition before the Games. Inam has told anti-doping authorities that he had been prescribed acetazolamide after consulting a doctor for an eye problem. He maintains that the medicine was taken for therapeutic purposes and had no connection with performance enhancement. According to sources familiar with the case, Inam provided information about the medication, including medical records, scans and the doctor's prescription, in response to the anti-doping notice. The International Testing Agency (ITA) subsequently conducted its own review and further testing as part of the inquiry. The case has also involved the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), which issued a letter to Inam on July 24 allowing him to use the medication twice a day until July 13, 2027, sources claimed. Inam's representatives argue that the subsequent authorisation for the medication raises questions about the adverse analytical finding and the handling of his case. Anti-doping authorities, however, have maintained that athletes are required to disclose the use of medicines containing prohibited substances through the prescribed process, including where applicable seeking a therapeutic use exemption before competition. The wrestler has now decided against a B-sample analysis. His representatives are reviewing the available options with legal advisers and could take the matter to the CAS if a suspension is imposed. Under anti-doping rules, a confirmed violation could result in a suspension, with the length depending on the substance detected, the circumstances of the case and whether the athlete can establish an applicable defence or mitigating factors. A suspension could have consequences beyond Inam's competitive career. He is also serving as secretary of the Pakistan Wrestling Federation (PWF) and could be barred from participating in wrestling-related activities. Inam has been the finest wrestlers in Pakistan’s last two decades journey. He has pulled off major medals in international circuit, also including two golds in the Commonwealth Game. He was also an undisputed beach wrestling world champion for few years and has also to his credit gold in the World Beach Games. Inam has also served quite well during his ongoing stint as PWF secretary and has conducted a lengthy talent-hunt programme as part of wrestling development at the grassroots level.

title: Lahore ATC grants 20-day remand of PTI leader Hammad Azhar in Jinnah House attack case
author: Rana Yasif
description: Azhar's mother approaches LHC to produce her son, disclose basis of his arrest and detention
text: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Lahore on Monday granted police a 20-day physical remand of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leader Hamad Azhar in the Jinnah House attack case during the May 9 riots for further investigation and recovery of his mobile phone. Azhar was arrested in Multan on Sunday and handed over to Lahore police for further proceedings. He was detained near the RA Bazaar area after being taken into custody from the home of a close friend. Azhar was wanted in several cases related to the May 9, 2023 protests and had been declared a proclaimed offender in a case involving an attack on the Government Officers’ Residence (GOR) Gate. The case proceedings were held before the Lahore ATC today amid tight security. ATC Judge Sardar Muhammad Akram Khan announced the reserved decision after hearing arguments on the prosecution’s request for Azhar’s physical remand. The prosecution had sought Azhar’s physical remand, maintaining that his custody was required for further investigation and to recover his mobile phone. However, Azhar’s counsel opposed the remand request, arguing that Azhar had been implicated in a fabricated case and should not be handed over to police custody. Earlier during the proceedings, the judge ordered media representatives and all other unrelated persons to leave the courtroom, allowing only lawyers and investigating officials to remain present. The judge told media representatives that they would be called back once the proceedings began and directed all non-relevant persons, including journalists, to leave the courtroom. Plea landed in LHC for Azhar's production Earlier, Azhar's mother, Ishrat Azhar, approached the Lahore High Court (LHC) for the recovery and production of her son, alleging that he was taken into custody from Multan two days ago but had not been produced before any court so far. The petition was filed through Barrister Abuzar Salman Khan Niazi under Article 199 of the Constitution. The Inspector General of Police (IGP) Punjab, Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Lahore, DIG Operations Lahore, and others were made respondents. The petitioner asked the LHC to direct the respondents to immediately produce Azhar before the court or the competent court and disclose the complete and lawful basis of his arrest and detention. Read: PTI leader Hammad Azhar arrested from Multan in May 9 cases The petition also sought immediate access for the detainee to his legal counsel and reasonable communication with his family members, in accordance with the law. It further requested the court to direct the authorities to place on record the FIR, arrest memo, remand order, detention order, if any, and all other documents under which Azhar is being kept in custody. Azhar's mother also urged the court to declare any detention of Azhar otherwise than in accordance with the Constitution and law as unlawful and without lawful authority. The petition sought any other relief deemed just and proper by the court in the circumstances of the case. Azhar arrested over May 9 protests The cases against Azhar stem from the events of May 9, 2023, when PTI founder Imran Khan was arrested at the Islamabad High Court in a corruption case. His arrest triggered widespread protests across Pakistan, during which demonstrators attacked and set fire to government buildings and military installations. Azhar was subsequently named in a number of cases related to the violence. Police sources said he had been declared a proclaimed offender in one of the cases after failing to appear before the court, which later issued permanent arrest warrants against him. He was wanted in connection with a case involving an attack on the gate of the Government Officers’ Residence (GOR) in Lahore, while police said he was also a nominated accused in more than 50 cases linked to the 9 May violence. An anti-terrorism court had declared Azhar a proclaimed offender over his continued absence from proceedings. He later approached the Lahore and Peshawar high courts seeking protective bail. Following the registration of the cases, Azhar resigned from his party position. PTI had previously assigned him responsibility for leading the party’s Punjab chapter. The PTI has consistently rejected the cases against its leaders and workers as politically motivated, accusing the government of using state institutions to suppress the party and its political opponents.

title: Fire engulfs factory in Karachi's Landhi, spreads to adjacent building
author: Sajid Rauf
description: A section of the building collapsed as emergency teams work to contain the third-degree blaze and evacuate workers
text: A fire broke out at an old-clothes factory in Karachi’s Landhi Export Processing Zone (EPZ) on Monday, prompting a large-scale response from the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) Fire Brigade, Rescue 1122, Sindh Rangers and police. The blaze later spread to an adjacent factory, while part of the original factory building also collapsed, a Rescue 1122 spokesperson said. According to fire brigade officials, the factory comprised a ground floor and two upper storeys. The fire initially broke out on the ground floor before spreading to the upper floors. Officials said the smoke was particularly intense, with firefighting operations being conducted from outside the building. KMC Fire Brigade and Rescue 1122 teams were engaged in a joint operation, with firefighting teams from Lyari also assisting at the scene. The blaze was later classified as a third-degree fire, prompting authorities to call in additional fire tenders. Eleven KMC fire tenders, two water bowsers and a snorkel were deployed to tackle the fire, with further tenders subsequently called in. Two men and a woman were initially reported to be in critical condition due to suffocation, according to Chhipa sources. The woman was taken to Jinnah Hospital after rescue teams and ambulances reached the scene. Also Read: Fire breaks out in Bannu hospital, no casualties reported Meanwhile, a Sindh Rangers spokesperson said personnel had reached the scene immediately given the severity of the fire and were assisting fire brigade and rescue teams in relief and rescue efforts. A large contingent of Rangers was deployed to cordon off the factory, manage traffic and ensure the safety of citizens. According to the spokesperson, the foremost priority was to protect human lives and prevent the fire from spreading further. Malir senior superintendent of police (SSP) also said a large contingent of police was present at the scene and that no loss of life had been reported. He added that all workers present in the factory at the time had been evacuated before the blaze spread. The SSP said authorities were facing no other major challenge apart from the firefighting operation. Rescue officials declared the factory unsafe, while media personnel and citizens were barred from entering the EPZ. Last month, 14 newborns were killed after a fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital at Islamabad's Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), triggering widespread outrage and demands from people and political parties for action against those responsible. The fire prompted authorities across Pakistan to review fire-safety arrangements at healthcare facilities and other public buildings. In Sindh, a fire-safety assessment of 22 government hospitals found widespread shortcomings, including a lack of fire alarms, sprinklers and adequate firefighting equipment. The provincial chief secretary subsequently gave departments 15 days to certify that public buildings under their control complied with fire-safety regulations. The tragedy also led to increased inspections and enforcement in Islamabad. The CDA sealed three buildings over fire-safety violations and later conducted a fire drill at Parliament House, while the Islamabad High Court sought a government report on fire-safety audits and mandatory NOCs for buildings in the capital. Punjab also ordered fresh safety checks following the fire at PIMS. The provincial health regulator directed public and private hospitals to strengthen emergency preparedness, conduct fire-safety audits and hold regular drills, while Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz ordered reviews of firefighting equipment, emergency exits, hydrants and electrical systems at public health facilities. Previous fire incidents in Karachi On January 17, 2026, a fire at the Gul Plaza shopping mall killed over 70 people and injured over 20. The Sindh government formed a single-member judicial commission, led by Sindh High Court's Justice Agha Faisal, on February 4 to probe the cause of the tragedy. The commission found that the dangers at the plaza were known well before the tragedy. Civil Defence inspections in 2024 and 2025 had identified the absence of fire-safety equipment, the presence of inflammable commercial material and deficiencies in exit routes. Yet the identified shortcomings were not rectified and no effective legal action followed. The building's management was also held responsible for failing to rectify known defects. Its regularised plan provided for 1,102 shops, while 1,153 shops were actually operating in the building, with large quantities of inflammable commercial goods stored inside. The Sindh Building Control Authority, too, could not escape responsibility by relying on the position that inspections were conducted only on complaints, the commission said. The Sindh Building Control Ordinance gave the authority powers to take corrective action against dangerous buildings, while Gul Plaza's incomplete records and ineffective fire-safety oversight also reflected institutional failure. Read More: Fire safety crackdown puts fuel stations on the block Overall, the commission rejected the idea that the tragedy could be attributed to one department, one institution or one government. It found that the legal powers, audit mechanisms, building-control authorities, firefighting services and emergency-response institutions existed across different periods. But the system as a whole failed to function effectively. The victims did not die from fire alone. Delays, darkness, blocked exits, obstructive windows, inactive safety systems, ineffective oversight and rescue opportunities that were not used in time all contributed to the loss of life. In March, a fire erupted at a private super market in the Zamzama area, but emergency teams successfully evacuated all management personnel inside the building, and no casualties were reported. Six fire tenders were deployed to control the fire and while the blaze was largely brought under control, it was dense smoke that remained a major challenge. It was reported in March that the port city had witnessed nearly 240 fire incidents that far into the year, leaving at least 99 people dead, several others injured, and causing financial losses worth millions of rupees.
